# idCerberus API Docs - full content for LLM

This file consolidates the idCerberus API guides and reference into plain text for use by LLMs, agents and development assistants.

Base URLs:

1. Staging: `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com`
2. Production: `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com`

## Rules for AI assistants

1. Use the documentation as the primary source and do not invent endpoints, parameters or services.
2. For external queries, use `POST /api/service-api` and select the product through the `service` field.
3. Use `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}` in protected calls.
4. Use staging for tests and production only when the user explicitly asks for it.
5. Never expose tokens, secrets, real CPFs, real CNPJs or real images in examples.
6. For OCR, send the complete base64 in `image1`/`image2` (with or without the `data:image/...;base64,` prefix, both formats work).
7. Do not use `fieldsOutput`, null fields or internal metadata as the public contract; use `result`.
8. If a service does not appear in the catalog, say it needs to be confirmed before documenting or integrating it.

## How to choose the right file

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Understand the documentation structure | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/llms.txt |
| Generate an integration, curl or choose a service | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/llms-small.txt |
| Look up payloads and responses per service | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/llms-api-reference.txt |
| Search for a service in a lightweight index | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/services-catalog.min.json |
| Run structured search from automation | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/services-catalog.json |
| Configure an MCP or agent with structured resources | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/mcp-manifest.json |
| Answer with the full documentation context | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/llms-full.txt |

## Use as a base for MCP and agents

These files can be used as context sources for a documentation MCP. The MCP should query the documentation, not execute calls against the idCerberus API.

### Recommended reading order

1. Read `llms.txt` as the initial manifest of the documentation.
2. Use `services-catalog.min.json` for a quick search by service, name, category, field and tag.
3. Use `services-catalog.json` when you need the full contract of a service.
4. Use `mcp-manifest.json` to list resources, suggested tools, safety rules and reading order.
5. Use `llms-api-reference.txt` for payloads, summarized responses and examples per service.
6. Use `examples/*.curl` when the answer needs a ready-to-use curl.
7. Use `llms-full.txt` only when the question requires the full context of the guides, API Reference and OpenAPI.

### Resources an MCP can expose

| Resource | Use in the MCP |
| --- | --- |
| https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/llms.txt | Manifest, rules, main URLs and shortcuts. |
| https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/llms-small.txt | Short context to generate an integration, curl and explanation. |
| https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/llms-api-reference.txt | Payloads, responses and examples per service. |
| https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/llms-full.txt | Full context for broad questions. |
| https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/services-catalog.min.json | Lightweight index for a quick search by service, category, tag and fields. |
| https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/services-catalog.json | Structured search and filters by service/category/field. |
| https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/mcp-manifest.json | Manifest with resources, suggested tools, rules and reading order. |
| https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/examples/*.curl | Ready-to-use examples to copy and test. |

### Rules for the MCP

1. Operate as a read-only source of the documentation.
2. Do not call staging, production, database or idCerberus endpoints.
3. Do not request or store `client`, `secret`, a JWT, CPF, CNPJ or a real image.
4. Use staging as the default environment when generating examples.
5. If the service does not exist in the catalog, answer that it needs to be confirmed before integrating.
6. Prefer `result` as the public contract; do not use `fieldsOutput` or internal metadata.

## Base contract of POST /api/service-api

1. Staging endpoint: `POST https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api`.
2. Production endpoint: `POST https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/service-api`.
3. Required header: `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}`.
4. Recommended header: `Content-Type: application/json`.
5. Required body field: `service`.
6. The alias sent in `service` must be the alias configured on the client's product.
7. Read public data in `result`; do not treat `fieldsOutput` or internal metadata as the public contract.
8. Preserve `status`, `onboardingStatus` and `externalId` when explaining responses.

## Important calling aliases

Use the public service enabled on the product in the `service` field.

| Service |
| --- |
| `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` |
| `SERVICE_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` |
| `SERVICE_EMAIL_VALIDATION1` |
| `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE` |
| `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE_PJ` |
| `economic_relationships` |

## Most used service shortcuts

| Case | Service | Main fields | Guide/API |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPF at the Federal Revenue | `SERVICE_RFB_PF` | `cpf`, `birthDate` | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-fisica#SERVICE_RFB_PF |
| CNPJ at the Federal Revenue | `SERVICE_RFB_PJ` | `cnpj` | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-juridica#SERVICE_RFB_PJ |
| React OCR | `SERVICE_OCR` | `documentType`, `image1`, `image2` | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-fisica#SERVICE_OCR |
| CNPJ card OCR | `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD` | `image1` | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-juridica#SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD |
| Proof of address OCR | `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS` | `image1` | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-fisica#SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS |
| Face Index | `SERVICE_FACE_INDEX` | `image1` | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-fisica#SERVICE_FACE_INDEX |
| Business (PJ) credit risk | `SERVICE_CREDIT_RISK_COMPANY` | `cnpj` | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-juridica#SERVICE_CREDIT_RISK_COMPANY |
| Individual (PF) credit score | `SERVICE_CREDIT_SCORE` | `cpf` | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-fisica#SERVICE_CREDIT_SCORE |
| Business (PJ) legal cases | `SERVICE_JURIDICAL_PROCESSES_PJ` | `cnpj` | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-juridica#SERVICE_JURIDICAL_PROCESSES_PJ |
| Family social benefits | `SERVICE_FAMILY_SOCIAL_BENEFITS` | `cpf` | https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-fisica#SERVICE_FAMILY_SOCIAL_BENEFITS |

## Quick notes for OCR and images

1. OCR uses a document image, not a selfie.
2. Face, FaceMatch and Face Index use a selfie/face, not a photo of an RG or CNH.
3. `image1` takes the image's base64, with or without the `data:image/...;base64,` prefix: both formats work.
4. RG usually needs front and back: `image1` and `image2`.
5. CNH uses `SERVICE_OCR`, `documentType: CNH` and `image1`.
6. CNPJ card uses `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD` and `image1`.
7. Proof of address uses `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS` and `image1`.
8. Emancipation uses `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION`; the document varies and success depends on OCR finding usable text.
9. If the image is missing, illegible or the wrong type, expect `REFUSED` with a clear message, do not invent success.

## Quick error diagnosis

| Symptom | Likely interpretation | Recommended action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing, expired or invalid token. | Generate a new token at `/api/token-generate`. |
| `Don't have access to the service` | Product without an active service/enabled API, or wrong alias. | Check the product configuration and calling alias. |
| Missing image | The payload did not send `image1`, `image2`, a URL or the expected `key`. | Check which OCR was called and rebuild the JSON. |
| `result: {}` | The query processed, but did not return useful data. | Validate the image, data, product configuration and the service's correct type. |
| `onboardingStatus: ERROR` | Technical failure in processing, storage or an external source. | Use `externalId`, time and environment to investigate. |
| Expected field missing | The field may not exist in the document/database or was not extracted. | Do not invent a value; explain that the return only carries available data. |

# Quick search

Use this page when you don't know exactly where to look. It gathers the
terms that best help the documentation's search find the right guide, the
correct service, or a ready-made example.

> Info:
  This page is a list of terms to type into the search box. If you want a
  path guided by role or goal instead of searching, see
  [Documentation map](/en/guides/mapa-da-documentacao).

## How to search better


    Search for `cpf`, `federal revenue`, `score`, `risk`, `phone`, `email`, `benefits`, `lawsuits`, `face`, or `SERVICE_RFB_PF`.


    Search for `cnpj`, `federal revenue`, `credit risk`, `business owners`, `domains`, `cnpj card`, `compliance`, or `SERVICE_RFB_PJ`.


    Search for `ocr`, `base64`, `image1`, `image2`, `CNH`, `RG`, `cnpj card`, `proof of address`, or `emancipation`.


    Search for `Don't have access`, `ERROR`, `REFUSED`, `externalId`, `payload`, `missing image`, `empty result`, or `status.message`.

## Ready-made search questions

You can search whole phrases:

1. `How do I call SERVICE_OCR in /api/service-api?`
2. `What payload for OCR of front and back RG?`
3. `How do I test SERVICE_FACE_INDEX in staging?`
4. `Don't have access to the service`
5. `Why did result come back empty?`
6. `Which service should I use for PJ credit risk?`
7. `How do I query a CNPJ card via OCR?`
8. `What are the required fields for SERVICE_CREDIT_RISK_COMPANY?`

## If the search doesn't find it

1. Search by the full alias, for example `SERVICE_OCR`.
2. Search by the document or data point, for example `CNH`, `CNPJ`, `score`, `phone`.
3. Search by the problem, for example `missing image`, `empty result`, `no access`.
4. Open the [service index](/en/guides/indice-de-services) and use `Ctrl + F`.
5. If it still doesn't show up, confirm whether the service is already documented or enabled for the API.

# Quickstart

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/quickstart
Source: en/guides/quickstart.mdx
Description: Make your first call to the idCerberus API with Postman, Windows, macOS, or Linux

# Quickstart

This guide shows the simplest path to making your first call to the idCerberus
API. It's written for anyone who isn't yet familiar with APIs, terminals, or
`curl`.

You can test in three ways:

| Way | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Postman | Best option if you prefer a visual interface |
| Windows PowerShell or CMD | Good for testing directly on Windows |
| macOS or Linux terminal | Good if you use a Unix terminal |

> Nota:
  Never run a `curl` command before? Start with Postman. Once the call
  works, copy the same pattern to your terminal or application code.

## Before you start

You need:

1. your application's `client` and `secret`;
2. access to the staging or production environment;
3. a test CPF or CNPJ;
4. permission to consume the product you want.

> Nota:
  Don't have a `client` and `secret` yet? This pair is released by React IT
  along with the contracted product, it's not something you generate
  yourself. Request it by email at
  [contact@react-it.com](mailto:contact@react-it.com) before following this
  guide.

The base endpoints are:

| Environment | `{base_url}` |
| --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` |

The call is the same in both environments. To use production, keep the
method, headers, and body the same and only swap the URL.

> Atencao:
  Don't mix environments. A token generated in staging must be used with the
  staging URL. A token generated in production must be used with the
  production URL.


    ### Postman

    1. Open Postman.
    2. Click **New**.
    3. Choose **HTTP Request**.
    4. Select the `POST` method.
    5. Paste the URL for the environment you want.
    6. Go to the **Headers** tab and add `Content-Type` with value `application/json`.
    7. Go to the **Body** tab.
    8. Choose **raw**.
    9. Select **JSON**.
    10. Paste the example body.
    11. Click **Send**.

    ### Windows PowerShell

    1. Open the start menu.
    2. Search for `PowerShell`.
    3. Open PowerShell.
    4. Paste the example `curl.exe` command.
    5. Press **Enter**.

    On Windows, prefer `curl.exe`. Plain `curl` alone can be interpreted as a
    different built-in PowerShell command.

    ### Windows CMD

    1. Open the start menu.
    2. Search for `cmd`.
    3. Open Command Prompt.
    4. Paste the command on a single line, or use `^` to break lines.
    5. Press **Enter**.

    ### macOS or Linux

    1. Open the Terminal.
    2. Paste the example `curl` command.
    3. Press **Enter**.

    On macOS and Linux, `curl` usually comes preinstalled. If the terminal says
    the command doesn't exist, install the `curl` package through your system's
    package manager.


    The first request generates a JWT token. That token will be used in the next
    protected calls.

    In Postman, set it up like this:

    | Field | Value |
    | --- | --- |
    | Method | `POST` |
    | Staging URL | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate` |
    | Production URL | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate` |
    | Header | `Content-Type: application/json` |
    | Body | `raw` + `JSON` |

    Body:

    ```json
    {
      "client": "{client}",
      "secret": "{secret}"
    }
    ```

    ### Staging

    ```bash
    curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
      --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data '{
        "client": "{client}",
        "secret": "{secret}"
      }'
    ```

    ### Production

    ```bash
    curl --location 'https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
      --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data '{
        "client": "{client}",
        "secret": "{secret}"
      }'
    ```

    ### Windows CMD

    ```bat
    curl.exe --location "https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate" ^
      --header "Content-Type: application/json" ^
      --data "{\"client\":\"{client}\",\"secret\":\"{secret}\"}"
    ```

    Expected response:

    ```json
    {
      "access_token": "{jwt_token}",
      "expires_in": "300"
    }
    ```

    Copy the `access_token` value. It will be used in the next step.

    In Postman, copy only the content between quotes. Example:

    ```json
    {
      "access_token": "eyJhbGciOi...",
      "expires_in": "300"
    }
    ```

    In this case, the token to use in the next step is `eyJhbGciOi...`.


    Use the returned token in the `Authorization` header.

    In Postman, create a new request:

    | Field | Value |
    | --- | --- |
    | Method | `POST` |
    | Staging URL | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api` |
    | Production URL | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/service-api` |
    | Header 1 | `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}` |
    | Header 2 | `Content-Type: application/json` |
    | Body | `raw` + `JSON` |

    ### Staging

    ```bash
    curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
      --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
      --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data '{
        "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
        "cpf": "cpf"
      }'
    ```

    ### Production

    ```bash
    curl --location 'https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
      --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
      --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data '{
        "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
        "cpf": "cpf"
      }'
    ```

    ### Windows CMD

    ```bat
    curl.exe --location "https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api" ^
      --header "Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}" ^
      --header "Content-Type: application/json" ^
      --data "{\"service\":\"SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT\",\"cpf\":\"cpf\"}"
    ```

    > Info:
      Going to test OCR? Use the [OCR via Service API](/en/guides/service-api/sobre-ocr-service-api)
      guide to build the payload with `image1`, `image2`, `documentType`, base64,
      and response examples. OCR needs a real image; a short payload only
      validates authentication and access.


    Replace:

    | Value | What to put |
    | --- | --- |
    | `{jwt_token}` | Token returned in the previous step |
    | `cpf` | CPF used for testing |
    | `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT` | Code of the service you want to run |



        Use this to validate the flow with a simple individual (PF) service.


        Use this to validate the flow with a simple business (PJ) service.


        Use this when the body needs base64, an image, a URL, or `documentType`.


        Use this to browse the product groups of `POST /api/service-api`.




    Most services return the data in `result` and the technical status in
    `status`.

    ```json
    {
      "result": {
        "cpf": "00000000000",
        "status": "REGULAR",
        "name": "PERSON NAME"
      },
      "status": {
        "code": 200,
        "message": "Success"
      }
    }
    ```

    | Field | How to interpret |
    | --- | --- |
    | `result` | Data returned by the service |
    | `status.code` | Technical processing code |
    | `status.message` | Technical message for the query |
    | `externalId` | Query identifier, when returned |


    Use `status.code` to decide your application's behavior.

    | Situation | How to handle it |
    | --- | --- |
    | `status.code` 200 | Processing complete. Read the `result` object. |
    | `status.code` 400 | The payload, parameter, permission, or external source may have failed. Read `status.message`. |
    | Expired token | Generate a new token and repeat the call. |
    | No JSON body | Handle it according to the endpoint. The onboarding report returns a PDF. |


## Next step

If you already know which product to consume, go to the [API Reference](/en/api-reference/autorização/gerar-token-de-api).

If you're still designing the flow, use [Choose the right service](/en/guides/escolha-o-servico-certo).

> Info:
  Did something go wrong in this test? You don't have to guess. See
  [Common integration errors](/en/guides/erros-comuns-integracao) before trying
  again. Most first-call problems are a token, environment mix-up, or a
  missing `service` field, and all of them have a direct fix there.

# Integration roadmap

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/roteiro-de-integracao
Source: en/guides/roteiro-de-integracao.mdx
Description: A practical step by step to go from the first test to a production-ready integration

# Integration roadmap

Use this roadmap as an execution checklist. The idea is to start with a
first manual call, validate the expected behavior, and only then bring the
flow into your application's code.


    Choose where the test will happen:

    | Environment | Base URL | When to use |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` | Testing, payload validation, and development |
    | Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` | Real use, after credentials and permissions are released |

    The call structure is the same in both environments. To switch from
    staging to production, just change the base URL.


    Before running protected services, generate a JWT token.

    ```bash
    curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
      --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data '{
        "client": "{client}",
        "secret": "{secret}"
      }'
    ```

    Copy the returned `access_token` value. In the following calls, send:

    ```http
    Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
    ```


    If the person integrating isn't familiar with the terminal yet, start
    with Postman. It keeps the URL, headers, and body separate, which
    reduces typos.

    Recommended flow:

    1. test in Postman;
    2. repeat the same request with `curl`;
    3. confirm the expected response;
    4. bring the request into Node.js, Python, C#, or another language.


    The `POST /api/service-api` endpoint works as a product runner. The
    route is always the same, but the `service` field defines what runs.

    ```json
    {
      "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
      "cpf": "cpf"
    }
    ```

    For individuals, the main input is usually `cpf`. For businesses, it's
    usually `cnpj`. Document, biometric, and document-analysis services may
    require base64 images, image URLs, a selfie, or a query key.


    For most services, the business data lives in `result` and the
    technical status lives in `status`.

    ```json
    {
      "result": {
        "cpf": "00000000000",
        "status": "REGULAR"
      },
      "status": {
        "code": 200,
        "message": "Success"
      }
    }
    ```

    Don't validate only the HTTP status. Also read `status.code`,
    `status.message`, and, when present, `externalId`.


    Before going to production, confirm:

    1. production credentials have been released;
    2. the base URL has been switched to `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com`;
    3. an expired token is handled by generating a new one;
    4. `400`, `401`, and `403` errors have clear handling;
    5. logs record `service`, the queried document securely, `status.code`,
      `status.message`, and `externalId`, when returned;
    6. sensitive data, base64, and tokens aren't written to open logs.


## Onboarding? Set up a webhook instead of just polling

If your flow is onboarding (SDK or Web Client), don't stop at polling from
the previous step. Set up a webhook to be notified automatically when the
status changes. See [Webhooks](/en/guides/webhooks). This applies to both
staging (to test receiving it) and production.

1. For a complete first call: [Quickstart](/en/guides/quickstart)
2. To choose products: [Choose the right service](/en/guides/escolha-o-servico-certo)
3. To see all service groups: [Service matrix](/en/guides/matriz-de-servicos)
4. For onboarding via SDK: [Onboarding via SDK](/en/guides/onboarding-sdk)
5. For the technical contract: [API Reference](/en/api-reference/autorização/gerar-token-de-api)

# Overview

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/visao-geral
Source: en/guides/visao-geral.mdx
Description: Understand the integration architecture, environments, endpoints, and response pattern of the idCerberus API

# Overview

The idCerberus API brings together digital onboarding, KYC, data enrichment,
biometrics, fraud prevention, risk analysis, and compliance services. The
integration was designed to support both complete onboarding flows and
single-shot queries by CPF or CNPJ.

## How it all fits together

Before diving into endpoints, tokens, and payloads, it's worth understanding
three pieces that repeat throughout this documentation. For each one: what it
is, why it exists, and what it's for in your implementation.

### Service

1. **What it is:** a specific query or check, like "CPF status at the
  Brazilian Federal Revenue" or "compare a selfie with a document." It has its
  own code (`SERVICE_SOMETHING`) and returns an isolated result.
2. **Why there are more than 300:** each type of data or check becomes a
  different service, because each company uses a different combination of
  them. You never need all of them.
3. **What it's for:** it's the unit you actually call. Every implementation
  starts by deciding which services solve your problem. See
  [Choose the right service](/en/guides/escolha-o-servico-certo).

### Single-shot query vs. onboarding

1. **What it is:** two ways to use a service. Single-shot means calling a
  service on its own, right away, directly through `POST /api/service-api`.
  Onboarding means combining several services into a guided journey, with
  steps, captured fields, and a final status (`APPROVED`, `IN_PROCESS`,
  `REFUSED`).
2. **Why both exist:** not every need is a full registration. Sometimes you
  just need to confirm one piece of data (single-shot); sometimes you need to
  guide the user through an entire KYC flow (onboarding).
3. **What it's for:** it defines the integration model you'll build. If the
  answer is "just confirm one piece of data right now," that's a single-shot
  query via API. If it's "register the user from scratch, with a document and
  a selfie," that's onboarding via SDK or Web Client.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T["POST /api/token-generate"] --> C{"What do you need?"}

    C -->|"Confirm one piece of data now"| A["POST /api/service-api\n(single-shot query)"]
    A --> R1["Synchronous response\nresult + status"]
    A -.->|"~10s later, if configured"| W["Webhook"]

    C -->|"Register from scratch,\nwith document and selfie"| S["SDK or Web Client\n(onboarding)"]
    S --> P["Processing\n(several services in sequence)"]
    P -->|"status changes"| W
    P --> R2["GET /api/onboarding/report\n(polling)"]
```

The webhook is the same mechanism for both paths. See
[Webhooks](/en/guides/webhooks) to set it up.

### Product

1. **What it is:** your company's specific configuration, including which
  services are enabled, in what order they run in onboarding, and which are
  available for single-shot queries.
2. **Why it exists:** each idCerberus client uses a different set of services.
  The product is what ties "idCerberus API" to "what your company actually
  contracted."
3. **What it's for:** you never choose among all 300+ services; you choose
  from what's already enabled for your product. If a service you need doesn't
  respond or doesn't appear, the first suspect is that it's not enabled for
  your product, not an implementation error.

With that in mind, the question that defines where to start isn't "how do I
use the API," but rather: **will my application call isolated queries (API),
or will it guide the user through a complete registration (SDK/Web)?** The
answer defines the integration model below.

### Common questions at this stage


    No. Use the API when your application only needs single-shot queries. Use
    the SDK or Web Client when you need to guide the user through a complete
    registration. Many clients use only one of the two; others combine both:
    onboarding for the initial registration and single-shot API for
    re-queries later.


    First confirm whether it's enabled for your product. That's arranged in
    advance with React IT, it's not something you enable yourself. If it's
    enabled and still fails, follow
    [Troubleshooting](/en/guides/troubleshooting).


    Yes. API, SDK, and Web Client consume the same services underneath; the
    difference is only how your application triggers and consumes the
    result. Migrating from one model to another doesn't change the data
    returned.


    No. Start with [Quickstart](/en/guides/quickstart) using a single test
    service, validate the end-to-end flow, and only then come back to the
    catalog to add the services that make sense for your case.


    `backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` and `backoffice.idcerberus.com` are the
    same URLs used by the idCerberus admin panel, but when you call
    `/api/...` on them, you're talking to the API, not the visual interface.
    There's no separate URL for the API: it's the same domain, different
    endpoints.


## Integration models

| Model | When to use | Your application's responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API | When your company's back end will consume queries directly | Authenticating, building payloads, calling endpoints, and handling responses |
| SDK | When data and document capture happens in a mobile app | Generating `tokenOnboarding`, handing it to the SDK, and querying the result |
| Web Client | When the flow will run via WebView, a responsive site, or a QR Code | Directing the user to the flow and consuming the processed result |

Beyond these three, there are two complements that aren't integration models
on their own, but add on to any of them:

1. [Backoffice](/en/guides/backoffice): idCerberus's visual interface, for
  looking at results and testing queries without writing code.
2. [Webhooks](/en/guides/webhooks): notifies your application when the
  status changes, for both onboarding and single-shot queries, instead of it
  having to keep asking (polling).

## If you're just getting started

An API is a way for one system to talk to another. In practice, you send a
request to a URL and get back a response with the result.

You can test the examples in this documentation in three ways:

| Tool | Who it's for |
| --- | --- |
| Postman | Anyone who prefers filling in URL, headers, and body in a visual interface |
| PowerShell or CMD | Anyone on Windows who wants to test from the terminal |
| macOS or Linux terminal | Anyone using macOS, Linux, or a Unix development environment |

The basic flow is always the same:

1. Generate a token with `client` and `secret`.
2. Copy the returned `access_token`.
3. Send that token in the `Authorization` header.
4. Run the endpoint or service you want.
5. Read the `result` object and the technical status in `status`.

If you've never made an HTTP call before, start with
[Quickstart](/en/guides/quickstart).

## Environments

The API has separate environments for staging and production. The endpoints
are the same in both environments; to switch environments, just change the
base URL.

The HTTP method, headers, and payload stay the same. The environment is
chosen by the URL used in the call.

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` |

In the documentation's examples, `{base_url}` represents the URL of the
chosen environment.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `base_url` | Base URL for staging or production |
| `generate token` | `api/token-generate` |
| `service-external-url` | `api/service-api` |
| `report-url` | `api/onboarding/report` |
| `token-url` | `api/token-history-onboarding` |

## Main endpoints

| Operation | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Generate API token | `POST /api/token-generate` |
| Query onboarding result | `GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}` |
| Download PDF result | `GET /api/history-onboarding-report/{tokenOnboarding}` |
| Generate `tokenOnboarding` | `POST /api/token-history-onboarding` |
| Run external service | `POST /api/service-api` |
| Query customer | `GET /api/customer?documentKey={cpf-or-cnpj}` |
| Change customer status | `POST /api/changeStatusOfCustomer` |

## Minimum flow to test

1. Generate a token at `POST /api/token-generate`.
2. Send the token in the `Authorization` header.
3. Choose a service under Individuals or Businesses.
4. Call `POST /api/service-api` with the `service` field.
5. Read `status.code`, `status.message`, and the data inside `result`.

## Pattern for external services

Individual (PF) and business (PJ) services are consumed through the same
technical endpoint:

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

The processing that runs is defined by the `service` field in the request
body. For example:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

## Response pattern

Most queries return:

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result` | Business data returned by the query |
| `status.code` | Technical processing code |
| `status.message` | Technical processing message |
| `externalId` | External query identifier, when returned |

## Next steps

1. For authentication, see [Authentication](/en/guides/autenticacao).
2. For onboarding via SDK, see [Onboarding via SDK](/en/guides/onboarding-sdk).
3. For the CPF catalog, see [Individual Services](/en/guides/servicos-pessoa-fisica).
4. For the CNPJ catalog, see [Business Services](/en/guides/servicos-pessoa-juridica).
5. For endpoint-by-endpoint implementation, use the [API Reference](/en/api-reference/autorização/gerar-token-de-api).

# Environments

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/ambientes
Source: en/guides/ambientes.mdx
Description: Understand the difference between staging and production in the idCerberus API

# Environments

The idCerberus API has two main environments: staging and production. The
endpoints, methods, headers, and bodies are the same. Only the base URL
used in the call changes.

| Environment | Base URL | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` | Testing, validation, and staging the integration |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` | Real queries in operation |

> Atencao:
  Don't mix credentials and data from different environments. A token
  generated in staging must be used with the staging URL. A token generated
  in production must be used with the production URL.

## How to switch environments

To switch from staging to production, change only the base URL.

| Item | Staging | Production |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base URL | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` |
| Generate token | `/api/token-generate` | `/api/token-generate` |
| Run service | `/api/service-api` | `/api/service-api` |
| Header | Same | Same |
| Body | Same | Same |

## Example: generate a token

Staging:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "client": "{client}",
    "secret": "{secret}"
  }'
```

Production:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "client": "{client}",
    "secret": "{secret}"
  }'
```

## Example: run a service

Staging:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

Production:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

## Common errors

| Situation | How to resolve it |
| --- | --- |
| Staging token used in production | Generate a new token at the production URL |
| Production token used in staging | Generate a new token at the staging URL |
| Wrong environment in the URL | Check whether you're using `backoffice-hml` or `backoffice` |
| Invalid credentials | Check `client`, `secret`, and the enabled environment |

## Recommendation

Always start with staging. Once the flow is validated, switch the base URL
and credentials to production.

## Next step


    Make your first API call in staging.


    Understand how to generate and renew the JWT token in each environment.


    Fix technical symptoms like a token from another environment or 401/403.

# Files for LLMs

The documentation also publishes plain-text and JSON files for use by LLMs,
code assistants, and automation tools.

These files help quickly look up guides, endpoints, services, environments,
and examples from the idCerberus API.

> Info:
The links below are static files. When clicked, the browser opens the
file's content in a new page. To use it with an AI tool or automation, copy
the full URL.

## Available files

| File | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| [`llms.txt`](https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/llms.txt) | Short documentation index, with main links and an overview. |
| [`llms-small.txt`](https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/llms-small.txt) | Operational summary for integrations: environments, authentication, `POST /api/service-api`, flows, and documented services. |
| [`llms-full.txt`](https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/llms-full.txt) | Full consolidated content from the guides, API Reference, and OpenAPI. |
| [`llms-api-reference.txt`](https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/llms-api-reference.txt) | Operational version of the API Reference, with services and curl examples ready for AI lookup. |
| [`services-catalog.json`](https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/services-catalog.json) | Structured JSON catalog for automations, validators, and agents. |
| [`services-catalog.min.json`](https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/services-catalog.min.json) | Lightweight index for quick lookup by service, category, tag, and field. |
| [`mcp-manifest.json`](https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/mcp-manifest.json) | Manifest for MCPs and agents, with resources, reading order, rules, and suggested tools. |
| [`examples/auth.hml.curl`](https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/examples/auth.hml.curl) | Ready-made authentication example in staging. |

## Recommended use

For quick questions about the documentation's structure, use:

```txt
https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/llms.txt
```

To ask for implementation help, `curl` generation, service selection, or a
flow explanation, use:

```txt
https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/llms-small.txt
```

To generate request examples from the documented services, use:

```txt
https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/llms-api-reference.txt
```

For deeper analysis or questions that depend on the documentation's full
content, use:

```txt
https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/llms-full.txt
```

For automations that need structured data, use:

```txt
https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/services-catalog.json
```

For a quick lookup before opening a service's full contract, use:

```txt
https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/services-catalog.min.json
```

To set up an MCP or agent with the list of recommended resources, use:

```txt
https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/mcp-manifest.json
```

## Using it as a base for an MCP

These files already work as the base for a documentation MCP. The idea is
for the MCP to consult the published files and answer questions about
services, payloads, examples, and guides without calling the idCerberus
API.

Recommended order:

1. Use `llms.txt` as the starting manifest.
2. Use `services-catalog.min.json` for a quick lookup by `service`, name, category, field, or tag.
3. Use `services-catalog.json` to open a service's full contract.
4. Use `mcp-manifest.json` to list resources, suggested tools, security rules, and reading order.
5. Use `llms-api-reference.txt` for the payload, a summarized response, and an example per service.
6. Use the `examples/*.curl` files to return ready-made calls.
7. Use `llms-full.txt` when you need the full context of the guides and API Reference.

A documentation MCP should be read-only. It doesn't need to call staging,
production, a database, or a real endpoint. It also shouldn't ask for a
token, `client`, `secret`, CPF, CNPJ, or a real image.

### Practical flow for using it in an MCP

1. Read `mcp-manifest.json` to discover which files exist, what order to use them in, and which rules to follow.
2. Search `services-catalog.min.json` first to find the right service without loading too much context.
3. Open `services-catalog.json` when you need the calling alias, fields, tags, common errors, a payload example, and agent tips.
4. Open `llms-api-reference.txt` when you need to explain the service's contract with more text.
5. Use `examples/*.curl` when the answer needs a ready-to-copy call.
6. Use `llms-full.txt` only when the question depends on the guides' full context.

In practice, the MCP doesn't need to "guess" anything. First it finds the
service in the catalog, then it uses the right guide to explain the
payload, the return, and common errors.

### What each file solves

| Question | Best source |
| --- | --- |
| Which service should I use? | `services-catalog.min.json` |
| Which alias goes in the body? | `services-catalog.json` under `callingAlias` |
| Which fields do I send? | `services-catalog.json` under `requiredFields`, `optionalFields`, and `payloadExample` |
| How do I test it in Postman/curl? | `examples/*.curl` and `llms-api-reference.txt` |
| What do I do about a common error? | `commonErrors` in the catalog and `llms-api-reference.txt` |
| I need a complete explanation of the flow? | `llms-full.txt` |

### Ready-made prompts

Use these prompts as a starting point when you want to test the
documentation with an AI or build a more targeted MCP.

**Choose a service**

```txt
Use https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/services-catalog.min.json and, if
needed, https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/services-catalog.json.

I want to solve this case: {describe the goal}.
Tell me which service to use, which alias goes in the body, which fields
are required, and which guide I should open before testing.
Don't make up a service outside the catalog.
```

**Build a curl**

```txt
Use https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/mcp-manifest.json,
https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/services-catalog.json, and the files at
https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/examples/*.curl.

Build a staging curl for the {SERVICE} service.
Use placeholders for token, CPF, CNPJ, client, secret, and image.
Don't use real data.
```

**Explain an error**

```txt
Use the troubleshootingByStatus block in mcp-manifest.json and the
service's commonErrors in services-catalog.json.

Explain this response: {paste the response without sensitive data}.
Tell me the likely cause, what to check first, and the next safe test.
Don't treat REFUSED as a technical failure without analyzing
status.message.
```

**OCR**

```txt
Use services-catalog.json, llms-api-reference.txt, and the OCR guide.

I want to test OCR for {RG/CNH/CNPJ card/proof of address}.
Tell me the minimum payload, the expected image type, the expected public
return, and common errors. Don't say OCR guarantees extracting every field.
```

### Responses the MCP should avoid

1. Don't say Face Index provides definitive identity validation. It searches for a match in the face base.
2. Don't treat `fieldsOutput` as a public contract.
3. Don't promise that OCR always extracts every field.
4. Don't make up a field's return when the field doesn't appear in the documentation.
5. Don't ask for a real CPF, CNPJ, token, client, secret, or image to build an example.
6. Don't suggest a real call in staging or production; this base is read-only.

Examples of questions this base should answer:

1. OCR: which service should I use for RG, CNH, CNPJ card, or proof of address?
2. CPF/CNPJ: what's the minimum payload for Federal Revenue, score, risk, or registration?
3. Face: how do I test `SERVICE_FACE_INDEX` and which image should I use?
4. Error: what does `Don't have access to the service` or `onboardingStatus: ERROR` mean?
5. Curl: how do I build a staging call without using real data?

## Example prompt

```txt
Use the documentation below as the primary source:
https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/llms-small.txt
https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/llms-api-reference.txt

Goal:
I want to integrate the idCerberus API to query individual data in
staging.

What I need you to deliver:
1. Explain the full flow, in order: authentication, generating the token,
   and calling the query endpoint.
2. State which endpoint I should use and which headers are required.
3. Choose the correct `service` to query a CPF at the Federal Revenue.
4. Generate a `curl` example to generate the token.
5. Generate a `curl` example to run the query at `POST /api/service-api`.
6. Show a summarized example of the expected response.
7. Explain how to validate success using `status.code`, `status.message`,
   and `result`.
8. List the most common errors and how to fix them.

Rules:
1. Use staging, unless I explicitly ask for production.
2. Don't make up endpoints, fields, services, or examples outside the
   documentation.
3. Don't use a real CPF, CNPJ, token, client, or secret.
4. Use placeholders like `{client}`, `{secret}`, `{jwt_token}`, and
   `"cpf"`.
5. If the documentation doesn't cover some information, say it needs to be
   confirmed before implementing.

Response format:
1. A short step by step.
2. Then the `curl` examples.
3. Then a "How to handle the response" section.
4. Then a "Checklist before testing" section.
```

# How to use this documentation

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/como-usar-a-documentacao
Source: en/guides/como-usar-a-documentacao.mdx
Description: Understand when to use guides, the technical catalog, and the API Reference

# How to use this documentation

The documentation is organized to support discovery, flow design, and
technical implementation. The goal is to keep you from having to search
through a large collection of requests with no context.

> Info:
  This page explains how the SITE is organized (guides vs. catalog vs. API
  Reference). If you want a recommended path by role or goal, see
  [Documentation map](/en/guides/mapa-da-documentacao). If you just want good
  search terms, see [Quick search](/en/guides/busca-rapida).

## The most common path


    Use the [Quickstart](/en/guides/quickstart) to validate credentials,
    generate a token, and run your first call with Postman, Windows, macOS,
    or Linux.


    Use the Individuals, Businesses, and Main flows guides to understand
    when each product makes sense.


    Use [Choose the right service](/en/guides/escolha-o-servico-certo) when
    you know the business problem but don't yet know which queries to
    combine.


    Use the [API Reference](/en/api-reference/autorização/gerar-token-de-api)
    to copy payloads, check parameters, and map responses.


## If you don't know where to run it from

You don't need to start by writing code. The simplest way is to test in
Postman, because the tool keeps the URL, headers, and body separated in
tabs.

Once the call works in Postman, you can repeat the same request in the
terminal:

| System | How to test |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | PowerShell or CMD with `curl.exe` |
| macOS | Terminal with `curl` |
| Linux | Terminal with `curl` |

The [Quickstart](/en/guides/quickstart) shows this step by step with
examples for each environment.

# Postman from scratch

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/postman-do-zero
Source: en/guides/postman-do-zero.mdx
Description: Set up Postman to test tokens, service-api, and OCR without writing code

# Postman from scratch

Use this guide to build a simple collection and test the idCerberus API in
staging.

> Nota:
  If you just want to test quickly without installing anything, every
  endpoint page in the [API Reference](/en/api-reference/autorização/gerar-token-de-api)
  already has a test panel built right into the browser. Use Postman when you
  want to keep a reusable collection for your team.

The goal is to end up with two working requests:

1. `POST /api/token-generate`
2. `POST /api/service-api`


    Without a valid token, no protected service should be tested.


    Just swap the `service` field and the required fields for each query.


    Use PowerShell to copy an image as base64 and paste it into the Postman body.


    See what to check when you get an access failure, a missing image, `{}`, or `ERROR`.


## 1. Create a collection

1. Open Postman.
2. Click **Collections**.
3. Click **New Collection**.
4. Name it `idCerberus API`.
5. Save.

## 2. Create a staging environment

1. Click **Environments**.
2. Click **New Environment**.
3. Name it `idCerberus HML`.
4. Create the `base_url` variable.
5. Set the value to:

```txt
https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com
```

6. Create the `jwt_token` variable.
7. Leave the value empty for now.
8. Save the environment.
9. Select `idCerberus HML` in the top-right corner of Postman.

## 3. Create the token request

1. Inside the collection, click **Add request**.
2. Name it `Generate token`.
3. Select the `POST` method.
4. Use the URL:

```txt
{{base_url}}/api/token-generate
```

5. In the **Headers** tab, add:

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |

6. In the **Body** tab, choose **raw**.
7. Select **JSON**.
8. Paste:

```json
{
  "client": "{client}",
  "secret": "{secret}"
}
```

9. Click **Send**.
10. Copy the `access_token` value.
11. Paste that value into the environment's `jwt_token` variable.

> Nota:
  If you prefer, set up a test script on the token request to save the token automatically:

```js
const data = pm.response.json();
pm.environment.set("jwt_token", data.access_token || data.token);
```

## 4. Create the service-api request

1. Inside the collection, click **Add request**.
2. Name it `Run service-api`.
3. Select the `POST` method.
4. Use the URL:

```txt
{{base_url}}/api/service-api
```

5. In the **Headers** tab, add:

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer {{jwt_token}}` |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |

6. In the **Body** tab, choose **raw**.
7. Select **JSON**.
8. Paste a test payload.

CPF example:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cpf": "00000000000"
}
```

CNPJ example:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_REGISTRATION_DATA_CNPJ",
  "cnpj": "00000000000000"
}
```

## 5. Read the response

A business response usually follows this format:

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "APPROVED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

Read it like this:

| Field | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `result` | Useful data returned by the service |
| `status.code` | Technical processing code |
| `status.message` | Technical processing message |
| `onboardingStatus` | Operational result of the service, when it exists |
| `externalId` | Identifier to trace the call in support/logs |

> Atencao:
  Don't rely only on the HTTP status to decide if it worked. The API can respond with HTTP 200 while the body shows `REFUSED` or `ERROR`.

## 6. Ready-made examples

If you'd rather copy an already-built curl, use:

| Case | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Staging token | [`auth.hml.curl`](/examples/auth.hml.curl) |
| Staging CPF | [`service-api-cpf.hml.curl`](/examples/service-api-cpf.hml.curl) |
| Staging CNPJ | [`service-api-cnpj.hml.curl`](/examples/service-api-cnpj.hml.curl) |
| OCR CNH | [`service-api-ocr-cnh.hml.curl`](/examples/service-api-ocr-cnh.hml.curl) |
| OCR RG | [`service-api-ocr-rg.hml.curl`](/examples/service-api-ocr-rg.hml.curl) |
| OCR CNPJ card | [`service-api-ocr-cnpj-card.hml.curl`](/examples/service-api-ocr-cnpj-card.hml.curl) |
| OCR proof of address | [`service-api-ocr-proof-of-address.hml.curl`](/examples/service-api-ocr-proof-of-address.hml.curl) |
| Face Index | [`service-api-face-index.hml.curl`](/examples/service-api-face-index.hml.curl) |

> Nota:
  If you want payload, expected return, and common errors in one place, open [Ready-made recipes](/en/guides/receitas-prontas).

## 7. Test OCR with an image

For OCR, the `image1` field receives the image's base64, with or without the `data:image/jpeg;base64,` prefix (both formats work).

### CNH

```powershell
$b64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\path\cnh.jpg"))
@{
  service = "SERVICE_OCR"
  documentType = "CNH"
  image1 = $b64
} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Clipboard
```

### RG front and back

```powershell
$front = [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\path\rg-front.jpg"))
$back = [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\path\rg-back.jpg"))
@{
  service = "SERVICE_OCR"
  documentType = "RG"
  image1 = $front
  image2 = $back
} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Clipboard
```

### CNPJ card

```powershell
$b64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\path\cnpj-card.jpg"))
@{
  service = "SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD"
  image1 = $b64
} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Clipboard
```

### Proof of address

```powershell
$b64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\path\proof.jpg"))
@{
  service = "SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS"
  image1 = $b64
} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Clipboard
```

After running the command, paste it into **Body > raw > JSON** in Postman.

## 8. Switch to production

To create a production environment, repeat the process and use:

```txt
https://backoffice.idcerberus.com
```

Use production credentials and generate a new token. Don't reuse a staging token in production.

## 9. If something goes wrong

| Symptom | What to check first | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` or `403` | Token expired, missing, or from another environment | Generate a new token in the same environment as the call |
| `Don't have access to the service` | Product doesn't have the service enabled for the API | Check the product setup before touching the payload |
| `Image ... not found` | Image field wasn't included in the body | Check `image1`, `image2`, `image1Url`, `image2Url`, or `key` |
| Returned `{}` | Service has no data for that record, or the image wasn't readable | Test valid data/image and check `status.message` |
| Got `ERROR` | Technical failure during processing | Save `externalId`, the time, and the service called |
| Expected field didn't come back | Field doesn't exist in the document or wasn't extracted | Validate the image, document type, and the service's contract |

For a more complete diagnosis, see [Common integration errors](/en/guides/erros-comuns-integracao).

# Authentication

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/autenticacao
Source: en/guides/autenticacao.mdx
Description: Generate JWT tokens and authenticate protected calls to the idCerberus API

# Authentication

Use this flow to generate the JWT token used in protected calls to the
idCerberus API. Authentication is the first step before consuming onboarding,
individual services, business services, or customer operations.

Access credentials consist of `client` and `secret`, provided in advance by
React IT.

If you don't have these credentials yet, contact us by email at
[contact@react-it.com](mailto:contact@react-it.com). Our team can guide you
through creating an account and getting the access you need for API
integration.

## What it is, why it exists, what it's for

1. **What it is:** the step that turns `client` + `secret` into a short-lived
  `access_token` (JWT) that your application uses in every protected call.
2. **Why it exists:** `client` and `secret` are long-lived credentials. If
  they leak, the damage is permanent until they're rotated. The
  `access_token` expires within minutes, so even if it leaks, the risk window
  is small. That's why day-to-day calls use the token, not `client`/`secret`
  directly.
3. **What it's for:** it defines a piece of your application's
  infrastructure, something in your back end that generates and renews the
  token automatically, so the rest of your code never has to worry about it.


    No. Generate a token and reuse it until it expires (`expires_in`).
    Generating a new one for every call works, but it wastes an extra call
    per request.


    The call returns an authentication error (401). Generate a new token and
    repeat the original call. See [Status and errors](/en/guides/status-e-erros)
    for the full handling.


    No. They're different credentials per environment. A staging
    `client`/`secret` doesn't generate a valid token to call production, and
    vice versa.


## When to use it

Use this page when you need to:

1. generate an access token for protected calls;
2. understand how to send the `Authorization` header;
3. identify the token's expiration time;
4. set up authentication before testing the API Reference endpoints.

## Recommended flow

1. Receive the `client` and `secret` credentials.
2. Generate a token at `POST /api/token-generate`.
3. Store the `access_token` value in your application's back end.
4. Send the token in the `Authorization` header.
5. Generate a new token when the previous one expires.

## Environments

The authentication endpoint exists in staging and production. The payload is
the same; just change the base URL for the environment.

In practice, the production `curl` is the same as the staging one; the only
difference is the URL in `--location`.

| Environment | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate` |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate` |

## Generate a token

Generate a token to access the API's services by sending `client` and
`secret`.

```http
POST /api/token-generate
```

```json
{
  "client": "{client}",
  "secret": "{secret}"
}
```

The response contains the access token and its expiration time.

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `access_token` | JWT token |
| `expires_in` | Token expiration time |

## How to test it

You can generate the token through Postman, PowerShell/CMD on Windows, or the
macOS/Linux terminal.

### In Postman

1. Create a `POST` request.
2. Use the URL `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate`.
3. In the **Headers** tab, add `Content-Type` with value `application/json`.
4. In the **Body** tab, select **raw** and then **JSON**.
5. Paste the body with `client` and `secret`.
6. Click **Send**.
7. Copy the returned `access_token` field.

### On Windows

In PowerShell, use `curl.exe` to avoid conflicts with built-in commands:

```powershell
curl.exe --location "https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate" `
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" `
  --data "{\"client\":\"{client}\",\"secret\":\"{secret}\"}"
```

In CMD, use `^` to break lines:

```bat
curl.exe --location "https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate" ^
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" ^
  --data "{\"client\":\"{client}\",\"secret\":\"{secret}\"}"
```

### On macOS or Linux

Use the `curl` command in the terminal:

Example with `curl` in staging:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "client": "{client}",
    "secret": "{secret}"
  }'
```

Example with `curl` in production:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "client": "{client}",
    "secret": "{secret}"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "access_token": "{jwt_token}",
  "expires_in": "300"
}
```

## Using the token

Send the returned token in the `Authorization` header of your next protected
requests.

```http
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```

Example in a service call in staging:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

Example in a service call in production:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

## Best practices

1. Keep `client` and `secret` only in your application's back end.
2. Don't expose credentials in mobile apps, front ends, or repositories.
3. Renew the token when `expires_in` indicates it's about to expire.
4. Handle invalid authentication responses by regenerating the token before repeating the call.

For technical endpoint details, see the
[API Reference](/en/api-reference/autorização/gerar-token-de-api).

## Next step


    Use your freshly generated token to make your first full call.


    Find the right `service` code to use after the token.


    See how to handle expired tokens and other authentication errors.


    Different from `client`/`secret`: see how the personal login works.

# First CPF query

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/primeira-consulta-cpf
Source: en/guides/primeira-consulta-cpf.mdx
Description: Run a simple individual query from start to finish

# First CPF query

This guide shows, step by step, how to run a first individual query using
the `POST /api/service-api` endpoint.

The example uses the `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT` service, which
queries a CPF's registration data.

## What you'll do

1. Choose the environment.
2. Generate a token.
3. Copy the `access_token`.
4. Run a CPF query.
5. Read `result` and `status`.

## 1. Choose the environment

Use staging for testing:

```txt
https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com
```

Use production only once the integration is validated:

```txt
https://backoffice.idcerberus.com
```

## 2. Generate the token

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "client": "{client}",
    "secret": "{secret}"
  }'
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "access_token": "{jwt_token}",
  "expires_in": "300"
}
```

Copy the `access_token` value.

## 3. Run the query

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

Replace:

| Value | What to put |
| --- | --- |
| `{jwt_token}` | Token generated in the previous step |
| `cpf` | CPF to query |

## 4. Understand the body

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `service` | Defines the product that will run |
| `cpf` | The queried individual's document |

## 5. Read the response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "status": "REGULAR",
    "name": "PERSON NAME"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

| Field | How to use it |
| --- | --- |
| `result` | Data returned by the query |
| `status.code` | Technical processing code |
| `status.message` | Technical processing message |

## 6. Common next services

| Need | Service |
| --- | --- |
| Check CPF status at the Federal Revenue | `SERVICE_RFB_PF` |
| Validate CPF with phone | `SERVICE_CPF_PHONE_VALIDATION` |
| Validate CPF with address | `SERVICE_CPF_ADDRESS_VALIDATION` |
| Check for politically exposed person (PEP) status | `SERVICE_PEP` |
| Run document OCR | `SERVICE_OCR` |
| Compare faces | `SERVICE_FACE_MATCH` |

To see every individual service, see
[Individual Services](/en/guides/servicos-pessoa-fisica).

# Onboarding via SDK

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/onboarding-sdk
Source: en/guides/onboarding-sdk.mdx
Description: Generate a TokenOnboarding, track registration status, and download the final report

# Onboarding via SDK

Use this flow when the user's data capture happens through the idCerberus
SDK. Your company's back end generates a `tokenOnboarding`, hands that token
to the app integrated with the SDK, and then queries the result processed by
the backoffice.

The `tokenOnboarding` identifies the registration through the entire cycle:
creation, execution in the SDK, processing, result query, and PDF report
download.

> Atencao:
  Don't confuse the two tokens in this flow. `access_token` authenticates
  your application and expires within minutes (see
  [Authentication](/en/guides/autenticacao)). `tokenOnboarding` identifies a
  specific registration and stays valid throughout the whole process, even
  after the `access_token` expires. If the `access_token` expires mid-flow,
  generate a new one. The `tokenOnboarding` doesn't change.

## What it is, why it exists, what it's for

1. **What it is:** a component (mobile or web) provided by idCerberus that
  captures the user's document, selfie, and data directly on their screen,
  following the onboarding script configured for your product.
2. **Why it exists:** capturing a document and biometrics with enough
  quality for validation (focus, lighting, angle, liveness) is a problem
  already solved by the SDK. Reimplementing this from scratch is expensive
  and error-prone.
3. **What it's for:** your application doesn't process images or implement a
  camera; it just generates the `tokenOnboarding`, hands it to the SDK, and
  then reads the result already ready. If your use case is just querying
  data (without capturing the user's document), you probably don't need the
  SDK. See [Choose the right service](/en/guides/escolha-o-servico-certo).

## When to use it

Use this integration when you need to:

1. start an onboarding flow in a mobile app or web experience integrated with the SDK;
2. send documents or initial data to support the registration;
3. query status, captured fields, and services run;
4. download the final PDF report for audit or storage purposes.

## Integration flow

1. Generate an API token at [Authentication](/en/guides/autenticacao).
2. Generate a `tokenOnboarding` for the user.
3. Send the `tokenOnboarding` to the app integrated with the SDK.
4. The user completes registration in the onboarding flow.
5. Query the result using the same `tokenOnboarding`.
6. If needed, download the onboarding report's PDF.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Backend as Your backend
    participant SDK as App with the idCerberus SDK
    participant idCerberus

    Backend->>idCerberus: POST /api/token-history-onboarding
    idCerberus-->>Backend: tokenOnboarding
    Backend->>SDK: Delivers the tokenOnboarding to the app
    SDK->>idCerberus: Captures document, selfie, and data (directly from the SDK)
    Note over idCerberus: Asynchronous processing
    idCerberus-->>Backend: Webhook or polling on GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}
    Backend->>idCerberus: GET .../history-onboarding-report/{tokenOnboarding} (optional)
    idCerberus-->>Backend: Report PDF
```

## Flow endpoints

| Step | Endpoint | Goal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Generate API token | `POST /api/token-generate` | Authenticate the application |
| Generate TokenOnboarding | `POST /api/token-history-onboarding` | Create the registration identifier |
| Query result | `GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}` | Get status, fields, and services processed |
| Download report | `GET /api/history-onboarding-report/{tokenOnboarding}` | Get the final onboarding PDF |

## Environments

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` |

In the examples below, `{base_url}` represents the base URL of the chosen
environment.

## Generate a TokenOnboarding

Generates a new `tokenOnboarding` to identify the user's registration in the
SDK flow. This token will later be used to query the result processed by the
backoffice.

```http
POST /api/token-history-onboarding
```

Full endpoint:

```txt
{base_url}/api/token-history-onboarding
```

Authorization:

```http
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
Content-Type: application/json
```

Example request:

```json
{
  "document": "cpf",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "cnpj": "cnpj",
  "name": "name",
  "documentFiles": [
    {
      "documentFileType": "OTHER",
      "document": "data:image/jpeg;base64",
      "documentUrl": "url"
    }
  ]
}
```

Values like `"cpf": "cpf"` are placeholders to swap for the real data; see the
convention in [Quickstart](/en/guides/quickstart).

Main fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `document` | CPF or CNPJ used in the onboarding |
| `cpf` | User's CPF, when applicable |
| `cnpj` | Related CNPJ, when applicable |
| `name` | Name of the user going through KYC |
| `documentFiles` | List of documents sent for the registration |
| `documentFiles.documentFileType` | Type of document sent |
| `documentFiles.document` | File in base64 |
| `documentFiles.documentUrl` | URL of the file to be sent |

Document types accepted in `documentFiles.documentFileType`:

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `RG_FRONT` | National ID (RG) front |
| `RG_BACK` | National ID (RG) back |
| `CNH` | Driver's license |
| `SELFIE` | Selfie |
| `SELFIE_3D` | 3D selfie |
| `OAB_FRONT` | Bar association card (OAB) front |
| `OAB_BACK` | Bar association card (OAB) back |
| `OTHER` | Other |
| `OTHER_SINGLE_FILE` | Other, single file |

Example response:

```json
{
  "tokenOnboarding": "56950dae-2d19-4092-a918-a612b3ca8f68",
  "dateHourProcess": "2023-02-17T16:49:41.577364Z"
}
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tokenOnboarding` | UUID of the onboarding, used in subsequent queries |
| `dateHourProcess` | Date and time the token was created |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/token-history-onboarding' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "document": "cpf",
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "cnpj": "cnpj",
    "name": "name",
    "documentFiles": [
      {
        "documentFileType": "OTHER",
        "document": "data:image/jpeg;base64",
        "documentUrl": "url"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## Query the result

Returns the status and results of an onboarding. To query, provide the
`tokenOnboarding` that was handed to the SDK.

```http
GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}
```

Full endpoint:

```txt
{base_url}/api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}
```

Authorization:

```http
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
```

Input field:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tokenOnboarding` | UUID of the onboarding returned to the SDK |

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tokenOnboarding` | UUID of the onboarding used for the query |
| `createdDate` | Date and time the onboarding was created |
| `numberSteps` | Number of steps configured for the registration |
| `status` | Onboarding status: `APPROVED`, `IN_PROCESS`, or `REFUSED` |
| `result` | Processing result: `AUT_APPROVED`, `IN_PROCESS`, or `REFUSED` |
| `fields` | Fields captured during registration |
| `services` | Services run during onboarding |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/onboarding/report/' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}'
```

Summarized example response:

```json
{
  "tokenOnboarding": "bb6adc72-0132-4b27-a723-98fe9f20cb81",
  "createdDate": "2022-06-15T19:02:04.877688Z",
  "numberSteps": 4,
  "status": "APPROVED",
  "result": "AUT_APPROVED",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field": "selfie_liveness_3d",
      "name": "Selfie Liveness 3D",
      "step": "1",
      "value": "https://bucket-onboarding.s3.amazonaws.com/arquivo"
    },
    {
      "field": "button_cnh",
      "name": "CNH - Carteira Nacional de Habilitação",
      "step": "2"
    }
  ],
  "services": [
    {
      "serviceName": "service_liveness_ft",
      "createdDate": "2022-06-15T19:02:06.233020Z",
      "status": "APPROVED",
      "statusMessage": "USER PASSED THE LIVENESS CHALLENGE",
      "fields": [],
      "rules": []
    }
  ]
}
```

### Captured fields

The `fields` array returns the data captured during registration.

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `fields.field` | Field alias |
| `fields.name` | Field name |
| `fields.step` | Step where the field was captured |
| `fields.value` | Captured value |

Example:

```json
{
  "field": "cnh_image",
  "name": "CNH",
  "step": "3.1",
  "value": "https://bucket-onboarding.s3.amazonaws.com/arquivo"
}
```

### Services run

The `services` array returns the services processed during onboarding, such
as OCR, Federal Revenue validation, PEP, FaceMatch, and Liveness.

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `services.serviceName` | Alias of the service run |
| `services.createdDate` | Date and time the service ran |
| `services.status` | Service status: `APPROVED`, `IN_PROCESS`, or `REFUSED` |
| `services.statusMessage` | Processing result or message |
| `services.fields` | Fields extracted by the service |
| `services.rules` | Rules evaluated during processing |

Example:

```json
{
  "serviceName": "SERVICE_FACE_MATCH",
  "createdDate": "2022-06-15T19:04:10.963326Z",
  "status": "APPROVED",
  "statusMessage": "SIMILARITY SCORE: 99.97%",
  "fields": [],
  "rules": []
}
```

### Processing rules

Some services return rules evaluated during processing. They help explain
why the onboarding was approved, refused, or is still processing.

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "situation_cpf_rfb",
  "value": "REGULAR"
}
```

## Download the PDF report

Downloads the onboarding report in PDF.

```http
GET /api/history-onboarding-report/{tokenOnboarding}
```

Full endpoint:

```txt
{base_url}/api/history-onboarding-report/{tokenOnboarding}
```

Authorization:

```http
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
```

Input field:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tokenOnboarding` | UUID of the onboarding returned to the SDK |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/history-onboarding-report/{tokenOnboarding}' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}'
```

This endpoint doesn't return a JSON body. Use it when you need to store or
present the final onboarding report as a PDF.

## Tracking processing

There are two ways to know when an onboarding finishes processing: webhook
(idCerberus notifies your application) or polling (your application asks).
See [Webhooks](/en/guides/webhooks) to set up automatic notification. It's
the recommended approach, because it reduces unnecessary calls. Even with a
webhook configured, keep the polling below as a fallback: a failed webhook
delivery isn't resent automatically (details in
[Webhooks](/en/guides/webhooks)).

Query `GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}` until the `status`
leaves `IN_PROCESS`.

1. Wait a few seconds between one query and the next. Don't poll every few
  milliseconds: the services behind onboarding may depend on external
  sources and take longer than a single-shot call.
2. Set a retry limit or maximum wait time in your application, with a clear
  path for "not done yet, notify the user, and try again later" instead of
  freezing the screen while waiting.
3. `REFUSED` is a final business result, not a technical error. The call
  itself succeeded (HTTP 200); it's the registration that wasn't approved.
  Don't treat `REFUSED` as a failure to retry. Treat it as a business
  decision your application needs to reflect to the user.

## Best practices

1. Generate the `tokenOnboarding` in the back end, never directly in the app.
2. Hand the SDK only the token needed to start the flow.
3. Use the same `tokenOnboarding` to query the result and download the report.
4. Treat `IN_PROCESS` as an intermediate state and query again later.
5. Store the PDF report only when there's an operational, regulatory, or audit need.

For technical endpoint details, see the
[API Reference](/en/api-reference/autorização/gerar-token-de-api).

## Next step


    Get notified automatically when the status changes, instead of only polling.


    See a specific onboarding's result directly on screen, without code.


    Understand `APPROVED`, `IN_PROCESS`, `REFUSED`, and how to handle each one.


    Review how to generate and renew the `access_token` used in this flow.
