# Webhooks

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/webhooks
Source: en/guides/webhooks.mdx
Description: Get automatic notifications when an onboarding changes status, without polling

# Webhooks

Use webhooks to have idCerberus notify your application when an onboarding
changes status, or when a single-shot query finishes processing, instead of
your application having to keep asking (polling).

## What it is, why it exists, what it's for

1. **What it is:** a URL of your application that idCerberus calls
  automatically (`POST`) every time an onboarding's processing changes
  status.
2. **Why it exists:** querying `GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}`
  in a loop until the status leaves `IN_PROCESS` works, but it burns calls
  and delays your application's reaction. The webhook flips this: you're
  notified the moment there's news.
3. **What it's for:** it's the recommended way to track onboarding in
  production. Reserve polling (see [Onboarding via SDK](/en/guides/onboarding-sdk))
  for when the webhook isn't configured yet, or as an occasional check.

> Info:
  Configuring the webhook (URL and security key) is currently done by the
  React IT team, it's not self-service via the API. Request activation at
  [contact@react-it.com](mailto:contact@react-it.com), providing the URL
  that should receive the calls.

## How it works

1. Something relevant happens: an onboarding changes status (goes from
   `IN_PROCESS` to `APPROVED` or `REFUSED`), a manual review decision is
   made, or a single-shot query in `POST /api/service-api` finishes
   processing.
2. idCerberus builds the content (the same format as
   `GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}`, adapted when the source
   is a single-shot query).
3. idCerberus makes a `POST` with that content to the URL configured for
   your product.
4. Your application responds with success (`2xx`) to confirm receipt.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Você as Your application
    participant idCerberus
    participant Webhook as Your webhook URL

    Você->>idCerberus: POST /api/service-api or onboarding flow
    idCerberus-->>Você: Synchronous response (result + status)
    Note over idCerberus: status changes / query finishes /manual review decides
    idCerberus->>Webhook: POST with id-cerberus-token
    Webhook-->>idCerberus: 2xx (confirms receipt)
    Note over idCerberus,Webhook: No 2xx? No automatic retry,see the warning below
```

> Info:
  The webhook isn't instantaneous in a strict sense. Automatic onboarding
  processing is checked every few seconds and fires when it finds a change;
  a single-shot query fires the webhook about 10 seconds after the HTTP
  response. A manual review decision (someone approves/rejects through the
  backoffice) fires right away. None of these times are a contractual SLA.
  Treat them as observed behavior, not a guarantee.

> Atencao:
  If your application doesn't respond with success, the call is marked
  internally as pending retry, but **there is no automatic process that
  keeps resending deliveries that failed**. A new delivery only happens if:
  (a) the same onboarding's content changes again later (this fires as a new
  delivery, not a retry), or (b) someone with access to the
  [Backoffice](/en/guides/backoffice) manually forces a resend on the
  screen. Because of this, don't treat webhooks as a delivery guarantee.
  Keep polling
  (`GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}`) as a real safety net, not
  just a formality.

## Payload

The body format depends on the event's source.

**Onboarding (SDK or Web Client):** same format as the onboarding report.

```json
{
  "tokenOnboarding": "bb6adc72-0132-4b27-a723-98fe9f20cb81",
  "createdDate": "2022-06-15T19:02:04.877688Z",
  "numberSteps": 4,
  "status": "APPROVED",
  "result": "AUT_APPROVED",
  "fields": [],
  "services": []
}
```

See the full field table in
[Onboarding via SDK](/en/guides/onboarding-sdk#consultar-resultado): it's the
same structure.

**Single-shot query (`POST /api/service-api`):** the same JSON that already
came back in the call's synchronous HTTP response (`result`, `status`,
`onboardingStatus`, and `externalId`), not the onboarding report format
above.

## Authenticating the incoming call

Every webhook call arrives with a verification header:

```http
id-cerberus-token: {webhookKey}
```

Before processing the payload, check that `id-cerberus-token` matches the
key React IT gave you when setting up the webhook. This confirms the call
really came from idCerberus, not from a third party who found your URL.

> Atencao:
  Don't expose the `webhookKey` in the front end or in public repositories. Treat it like any other authentication secret.

## Best practices

1. Respond quickly (ideally under a few seconds) and process the content
  afterward, asynchronously. A slow endpoint can be interpreted as a
  failure.
2. Always validate the `id-cerberus-token` header before trusting the
  payload.
3. Handle repeated events. Reprocessing the same `tokenOnboarding` with the
  same status shouldn't cause a duplicate side effect.
4. Don't treat `REFUSED` as a technical error. It's a business result, just
  like single-shot consumption via polling. See
  [Status and errors](/en/guides/status-e-erros).
5. Keep a polling fallback. Since there's no automatic resend for failed
  deliveries (see "How it works" above), this fallback is what guarantees
  your application doesn't stay stuck waiting for an event that won't
  arrive on its own.

## Common questions


    No. Use the webhook as the primary mechanism and polling
    (`GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}`) as a check or fallback,
    especially right after setting up the webhook for the first time.

    `POST /api/service-api` already return the result directly in the HTTP
    response; the webhook arrives afterward (around 10 seconds later), with
    the same content. In practice it's redundant for simple single-shot
    consumption; it matters more when you want to centralize everything
    (single-shot and onboarding) in a single listener instead of handling
    the API's synchronous response in multiple places in your code.

    multiple internal systems, receive them at your own URL and distribute
    from there.

    the call. If you're not sure whether the setup was applied, check with
    whoever granted the access.


## Next step


    See the full flow that generates the events the webhook notifies you about.


    See delivery attempt logs and force a manual resend from the screen.

# Backoffice

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/backoffice
Source: en/guides/backoffice.mdx
Description: idCerberus's visual interface, dashboard, onboarding history, and manual queries without writing code

# Backoffice

## What it is, why it exists, what it's for

1. **What it is:** idCerberus's web interface, accessed with a login
  (username and password), separate from the API integration. It's the same
  domain (`backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` / `backoffice.idcerberus.com`)
  that serves the `/api/...` endpoints. See why in
  [Overview](/en/guides/visao-geral).
2. **Why it exists:** not every task needs code. Tracking registration
  volume, looking at a specific onboarding result, or testing a one-off
  query shouldn't require opening Postman.
3. **What it's for:** it's the place to view and explore, not to integrate.
  Your application keeps consuming data through the API, SDK, or webhook;
  the backoffice is the panel your team uses on top of that.

## What you'll find there

| Area | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| Dashboard | Registration volume, onboarding summary, geographic and age distribution of processed customers |
| Onboardings | List and detail of each processed registration, the same content that `GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}` returns, but on screen. The detail view also shows that onboarding's webhook attempt history and lets you force a manual resend |
| Quick queries | Run a one-off query (CPF, CNPJ, document with OCR, name, phone, face) directly in the interface, without building a payload or calling the API |

> Nota:
  Use the backoffice's quick queries to quickly confirm that a service does
  what you expect, before replicating the same call in code via
  `POST /api/service-api`. It's the fastest way to "see the result" without
  writing anything.

## Backoffice or API: which to use

| If you need to... | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Automate queries within your application's flow | API ([Quickstart](/en/guides/quickstart)) |
| Guide a complete registration inside your app | SDK or Web Client ([Onboarding via SDK](/en/guides/onboarding-sdk)) |
| Get notified when a registration changes status | Webhook ([Webhooks](/en/guides/webhooks)) |
| Look at a specific result quickly, without coding | Backoffice, Onboardings screen |
| Test a query before integrating | Backoffice, Quick queries |
| Track volume and metrics | Backoffice, Dashboard |

## Common questions


    The dashboard and onboarding history reflect the same data that
    `GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}` exposes. Quick queries use
    the same `POST /api/service-api` services underneath; it's the same
    query, just triggered from the screen instead of code.


    No. The backoffice login is a username and password, for a person.
    `client` and `secret` authenticate your application. They're two
    different authentication mechanisms for the same system. See
    [Authentication](/en/guides/autenticacao) for the API side.


    Webhook setup (URL and key) is currently done by React IT on request,
    it's not yet a self-service screen. See
    [Webhooks](/en/guides/webhooks) for how to request activation.


## Next step


    Make your first API call to compare against what you saw on screen.


    Set up an automatic notification instead of watching the screen manually.


    Understand the difference between your personal login and the API's `client`/`secret`.


    Go back to the big picture: service, onboarding, product, and backoffice.

# Choose the right service

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/escolha-o-servico-certo
Source: en/guides/escolha-o-servico-certo.mdx
Description: Find the idCerberus services best suited for each use case

# Choose the right service

Use this page to go from a business need to the `service` codes you should
use in `POST /api/service-api`.

Useful search terms: CPF Federal Revenue, RFB PF, CNPJ Federal Revenue, RFB
PJ, KYC PF, KYC PJ, OCR, document extraction, FaceMatch, facial comparison,
Liveness, proof of life, fraud score, financial risk, electoral data, active
debts, protests, business owners, and compliance.

> Info:
  This page is a decision guide by need, not the complete list of services.
  The full technical catalog lives in
  [Individual Services](/en/guides/servicos-pessoa-fisica) and
  [Business Services](/en/guides/servicos-pessoa-juridica).

## Before the tables, what's your role?

You don't need to read `SERVICE_SOMETHING` codes to decide anything. Skip
straight to the table for your need (validate identity, analyze risk,
validate contact, analyze a company) and read the **Need** column. It
describes what the service does in plain language. The code in the column
next to it is just what your technical team will copy afterward.

If you'd rather have a conversation than a table, start with the
[Overview](/en/guides/visao-geral), which explains what a service and an
onboarding are without technical jargon.

Follow the normal process: find the service in the table, copy the exact
code, and go to the [API Reference](/en/api-reference/autorização/gerar-token-de-api)
to get the full contract (payload, response, errors). If you haven't made
your first call yet, start with the [Quickstart](/en/guides/quickstart)
before choosing the final service.

This page is about `POST /api/service-api` (single-shot queries). If your
case is capturing a user's document and selfie in an app, the flow is
different. See [Onboarding via SDK](/en/guides/onboarding-sdk). You can
still come back here later to complement onboarding with extra single-shot
queries.

The tables below apply to staging and production with no code difference.
After choosing the service, see [Environments](/en/guides/ambientes) to confirm
the URL and test credentials, and [Status and errors](/en/guides/status-e-erros)
to know how to interpret responses before reporting a bug.

## How to decide

1. Identify whether the query is for an individual, a business, onboarding, or a customer.
2. Confirm the main document: `cpf`, `cnpj`, `phone`, images, or `tokenOnboarding`.
3. Choose the service by business need, not by its technical name.
4. Copy the exact name from the [Service index](/en/guides/indice-de-services).
5. Build the request in staging.
6. Read `status.code`, `status.message`, and `result` before releasing to production.

> Nota:
If the person integrating doesn't know the API, start with the CPF, CNPJ,
FaceMatch, or document analysis examples in
[Examples by environment](/en/guides/exemplos-por-ambiente).


    CPF, document OCR, face matching, and government biometrics.


    Full journey via SDK, from the token to the final report.


    PEP, KYC, fraud score, debts, lawsuits, and certificates.


    Email, phone, address, and related people.


    Candidacies, electoral donations, and political involvement.


    CNPJ registration data, owners, debts, and PJ credit score.


    Sets of services that typically go together per flow.

| Check a CNPJ at the Federal Revenue | `SERVICE_RFB_PJ` |
| Check a CNPJ at the Federal Revenue in on-demand mode | `SERVICE_RFB_PJ_ON_DEMAND` |
| Query a company's business owners or relationships | `SERVICE_COMPANY_RELATIONSHIP`, `SERVICE_FIRST_LEVEL_PARTNER` |
| Query a company's debts | `SERVICE_ACTIVE_DEBT_PJ` |
| Query business owners' KYC | `SERVICE_COMPANY_KYC_OWNERS` |
| Query a company's protests | `SERVICE_PROTEST_PJ` |

## Validate a person's identity

| Need | Recommended services | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Confirm CPF registration data | `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT`, `SERVICE_RFB_PF` | Validate name, date of birth, registration status, and Federal Revenue source |
| Update CPF data with an on-demand query | `SERVICE_RFB_PF_ON_DEMAND` | Fetch registration data at request time |
| Extract data from a document | `SERVICE_OCR` | Read RG/CIN, CNH, OAB, RNE/CRNM, passport, and auto-identification |
| Compare a selfie and a document | `SERVICE_FACE_MATCH` | Validate whether two images belong to the same person |
| Query government biometrics | `SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH` | Get a similarity score against government databases |
| Validate a CNH with DataValid | `SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH` | Support document validation with a document-validation integration |
| Run a full document analysis | `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` | Extract data and match a document with a selfie in a single flow |

## Build a complete onboarding

| Step | Services or endpoints |
| --- | --- |
| Start a journey via SDK | `POST /api/token-history-onboarding` |
| Capture document and selfie | SDK or Web Client |
| Query the result | `GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}` |
| Download evidence | `GET /api/history-onboarding-report/{tokenOnboarding}` |
| Complement with single-shot queries | `SERVICE_RFB_PF`, `SERVICE_PEP`, `SERVICE_FACE_MATCH`, `SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH` |

## Common combinations

| Flow | Recommended combination |
| --- | --- |
| Simple CPF registration | `SERVICE_RFB_PF` + `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT` |
| Onboarding with a document | `SERVICE_OCR` + `SERVICE_FACE_MATCH` |
| Individual KYC | `SERVICE_PEP` + certificates + debts + risk score |
| Business registration | `SERVICE_RFB_PJ` + `SERVICE_CORPORATE_DATA_ENRICHMENT` + `SERVICE_SINTEGRA_CONSULTATION` |
| Business KYC | PJ data + business owners + owners' KYC + debts + protests |

# Ready-made recipes

Use this page when you want to test a common flow without hunting service by service.

All the queries below use:

```txt
POST /api/service-api
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
Content-Type: application/json
```


    Registration data and enrichment for individuals.


    Registration data and business status.


    CNH, RG, CNPJ card, and proof of address.


    Search for a selfie in the facial base.


    Score, rating, and business risk signals.

## Before testing

1. Generate a token in the same environment as the call.
2. Confirm the product has the service active and enabled for the API.
3. Use valid staging data.
4. For OCR, send the full base64 (with or without the `data:image/...;base64,` prefix, both work).
5. Read `result`, `status.message`, `onboardingStatus`, and `externalId`.

Common error:

```json

  "status": {
    "code": 400,

}
```

## How to adapt a recipe

1. Swap only the `service` and the required fields.
2. Keep the `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}` header.
3. Use staging to validate the payload and data.
4. Don't automatically treat a missing field as an error.
5. Save `externalId` when you need to investigate.

Use credentials, a token, and a base URL from the same environment. A
staging token shouldn't be used in production, and a production token
shouldn't be used in staging.

# Examples by language

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/exemplos-por-linguagem
Source: en/guides/exemplos-por-linguagem.mdx
Description: Integration examples with curl, Node.js, Python, and C#

# Examples by language

The examples below follow the same flow:

1. Generate a token at `POST /api/token-generate`.
2. Copy the `access_token`.
3. Call `POST /api/service-api`.
4. Read `result` and `status`.

The service used in the examples is `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT`, but
you can swap the `service` field and the other parameters for the product
you want.

## Environments

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` |

## cURL on macOS or Linux

This example uses `jq` to extract the token automatically.

```bash
BASE_URL="https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com"

TOKEN=$(curl --silent --location "${BASE_URL}/api/token-generate" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "client": "{client}",
    "secret": "{secret}"
  }' | jq -r '.access_token')

curl --location "${BASE_URL}/api/service-api" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

If you don't have `jq`, generate the token in a first command, copy
`access_token`, and use it in the second command.

## cURL on Windows PowerShell

In PowerShell, use `curl.exe`.

```powershell
$baseUrl = "https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com"

$tokenResponse = curl.exe --silent --location "$baseUrl/api/token-generate" `
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" `
  --data "{\"client\":\"{client}\",\"secret\":\"{secret}\"}"

$token = ($tokenResponse | ConvertFrom-Json).access_token

curl.exe --location "$baseUrl/api/service-api" `
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $token" `
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" `
  --data "{\"service\":\"SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT\",\"cpf\":\"cpf\"}"
```

## Node.js

> Info:
  The examples use the global `fetch`, available from Node 18 onward. On
  earlier versions, install a polyfill like `node-fetch`. The final snippet
  runs inside an immediately-invoked `async` function so it works in both
  CommonJS and ESM projects with no extra configuration.

### Node.js with fetch

```js
const baseUrl = "https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com";

async function generateToken() {
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/api/token-generate`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      client: "{client}",
      secret: "{secret}",
    }),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Failed to generate token: ${response.status}`);
  }

  return response.json();
}

async function runService(token) {
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/api/service-api`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      service: "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
      cpf: "cpf",
    }),
  });

  const body = await response.json();

  if (body.status?.code !== 200) {
    throw new Error(body.status?.message || "Processing failed");
  }

  return body.result;
}

(async () => {
  const { access_token } = await generateToken();
  const result = await runService(access_token);
  console.log(result);
})();
```

### Node.js with Axios

Install it first with `npm install axios`.

```js
const axios = require("axios");

const baseUrl = "https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com";

(async () => {
  const tokenResponse = await axios.post(`${baseUrl}/api/token-generate`, {
    client: "{client}",
    secret: "{secret}",
  });

  const token = tokenResponse.data.access_token;

  const serviceResponse = await axios.post(
    `${baseUrl}/api/service-api`,
    {
      service: "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
      cpf: "cpf",
    },
    {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      timeout: 60000,
    },
  );

  if (serviceResponse.data.status?.code !== 200) {
    throw new Error(serviceResponse.data.status?.message || "Processing failed");
  }

  console.log(serviceResponse.data.result);
})();
```

## Python

```python
BASE_URL = "https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com"
```

## C#

```csharp
using System.Net.Http;
using System.Net.Http.Headers;
using System.Text;
using System.Text.Json;

var baseUrl = "https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com";
using var http = new HttpClient();

var tokenPayload = JsonSerializer.Serialize(new
{
    client = "{client}",
    secret = "{secret}"
});

var tokenResponse = await http.PostAsync(
    $"{baseUrl}/api/token-generate",
    new StringContent(tokenPayload, Encoding.UTF8, "application/json")
);

tokenResponse.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
using var tokenJson = JsonDocument.Parse(await tokenResponse.Content.ReadAsStringAsync());
var token = tokenJson.RootElement.GetProperty("access_token").GetString();

http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);

var servicePayload = JsonSerializer.Serialize(new
{
    service = "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    cpf = "cpf"
});

var serviceResponse = await http.PostAsync(
    $"{baseUrl}/api/service-api",
```

## Java

Example using `HttpClient` (Java 11+) and text blocks (`"""`) for the JSON,
which require Java 15+. On Java 11-14, replace the text blocks with regular
concatenated strings.

```java
import java.net.URI;
import java.net.http.HttpClient;
import java.net.http.HttpRequest;
import java.net.http.HttpResponse;

public class IdCerberusExample {
  public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
    var baseUrl = "https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com";
    var http = HttpClient.newHttpClient();

    var tokenRequest = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
      .uri(URI.create(baseUrl + "/api/token-generate"))
      .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
      .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        {
          "client": "{client}",
          "secret": "{secret}"
        }
      """))
      .build();

    var tokenResponse = http.send(tokenRequest, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString());
    var tokenBody = tokenResponse.body();
    var token = tokenBody.split("\"access_token\"\\s*:\\s*\"")[1].split("\"")[0];

    var serviceRequest = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
      .uri(URI.create(baseUrl + "/api/service-api"))
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + token)
      .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
      .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        {
          "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
          "cpf": "cpf"
        }
      """))
      .build();

    var serviceResponse = http.send(serviceRequest, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString());
    System.out.println(serviceResponse.body());
  }
}
```

## How to adapt it for another service

Swap the `service` value and the body fields.

Example for CNPJ:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_CORPORATE_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Example for FaceMatch:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_FACE_MATCH",
  "image1": "base64",
  "image2": "base64"
}
```

# FAQ

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/duvidas-e-solucoes
Source: en/guides/duvidas-e-solucoes.mdx
Description: Direct answers to the most common integration questions, organized by topic, before opening a ticket

# FAQ

This page brings together, in one place, the questions that come up most
often during an idCerberus integration. The idea is simple: before opening a
support ticket, look for your question here. A good share of reported "bugs"
are expected behaviors that just weren't clear in the technical
documentation.

> Nota:
  Use `Ctrl + F` (or `Cmd + F` on Mac) to search for a keyword on this page before going through the sections manually.

## Authentication and token


    No. Generate an `access_token` at `POST /api/token-generate` and reuse it
    until it expires, according to the `expires_in` field in the response.
    Generating a new one for every call works, but it wastes an extra call
    per request.


    You get HTTP 401. Generate a new token with `client` and `secret` and
    repeat the original call. This is a real HTTP status, different from
    service permission failures that also show up as "401 in the body" (see
    the status section below).


    No. They're different credentials per environment. A staging
    `client`/`secret` doesn't generate a valid token to call production, and
    vice versa. The databases and the authentication realm are physically
    separated between the two environments.


    This pair is released by React IT along with the contracted product,
    it's not something you generate yourself. Request it by email at
    [contact@react-it.com](mailto:contact@react-it.com).


## Single-shot query (POST /api/service-api)


    Yes, and it's the number-one source of confusion in this API.
    `POST /api/service-api` almost always returns HTTP 200, even when the
    query failed completely. The real reason lives inside the body, in
    `status.code` and `status.message`. Never decide success or failure
    based only on the HTTP status.


    A real HTTP 401/403 only happens due to an authentication problem
    (missing, expired, or wrong-environment token), and the call doesn't
    even reach service processing. "Product not enabled for the service" and
    "inactive product" don't generate HTTP 401/403 on this endpoint: the
    call returns HTTP 200 with the problem described in `status.code` (400
    for payload/service permission, 401 for inactive or not-found product)
    inside the body.


    There are at least three distinct causes: the data source found nothing
    for that document (a valid behavior, not every empty return is an
    error), the image wasn't read successfully during OCR, or, if your
    product is prepaid, the organization's balance is insufficient. That
    last case is tricky because it also comes with HTTP 200 and
    `status.code` 200, with `status.message` saying something like "Not
    enough balance." Always read `status.message` when `result` comes back
    empty, even with 200/200.


    No. Each service's alias (the value you send in `service`) is unique in
    the system: there's no product-customized alias. If a service doesn't
    work, the issue is that it's not enabled for your product, not that the
    alias name is wrong (unless you typed it incorrectly).


    Only in one specific case: `SEVICE_ONLINE_BETTING_PROPENSITY` is
    documented without the letter R in `SERVICE` on purpose. That's the
    spelling implemented in the backend. Fixing that alias when you copy it
    breaks the call. Outside that case, copy aliases exactly as they appear
    in the [service catalog](/en/guides/indice-de-services).


## Onboarding via SDK or Web Client


    No, and mixing up the two is a common source of errors. `access_token`
    authenticates your application and expires within minutes.
    `tokenOnboarding` identifies a specific registration and stays valid
    throughout the whole process, even after the `access_token` expires. If
    the `access_token` expires mid-flow, generate a new one: the
    `tokenOnboarding` doesn't change.


    There's no fixed guaranteed time. Automatic processing is checked every
    few seconds internally, but the total time depends on how many services
    are in the pipeline and whether any of them depend on slow external
    sources. Treat it as observed behavior, not a contractual SLA, and
    always implement a maximum wait limit in your application.


    No. `REFUSED` is a business result: the call itself succeeded (HTTP
    200), and it's the registration that wasn't approved by the product's
    rules. Don't treat `REFUSED` as something to retry; treat it as a
    decision your application needs to reflect to the user.


## Webhooks


    First, confirm that the event you're expecting actually triggers a
    webhook: onboarding status change, manual review decision, or a
    single-shot query at `POST /api/service-api` (when the product has a
    webhook configured). Second, remember that a single-shot query fires the
    webhook about 10 seconds after the HTTP response, not instantly. Third,
    check that your URL is publicly reachable (idCerberus can't deliver to
    an endpoint behind a firewall without access granted).


    No. There's no automatic process that keeps resending deliveries that
    failed. A new delivery only happens if the same onboarding's content
    changes again later (which fires as a new delivery, not a retry), or if
    someone with access to the [Backoffice](/en/guides/backoffice) manually
    forces a resend on the screen. Because of this, never rely only on the
    webhook. Keep polling
    (`GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}`) as a real safety net.


    Yes. A webhook originating from onboarding uses the full report format
    (`tokenOnboarding`, `status`, `fields`, `services`). A webhook
    originating from a single-shot query uses the same JSON that already
    came back in the call's synchronous HTTP response (`result`, `status`,
    `onboardingStatus`, `externalId`). They're different formats, so don't
    assume a single structure.


## OCR and images


    No. The system accepts base64 with or without that prefix and removes
    it automatically when present. If your tool generates base64 with the
    prefix (common in browsers, for example), don't waste time stripping it.


    Confirm three things in order: whether `documentType` matches the actual
    document sent, whether the image is complete and legible (no cropped
    edges), and whether the base64 wasn't truncated partway through sending.
    That last one is common when the payload is built manually and the cut
    happens with no visible error until it reaches the API.


    It can vary. `SERVICE_OCR` is processed by different partners depending
    on your product's configuration, and that can change one specific
    `result` field (most commonly the field name that indicates the
    recognized document type). Treat this page's contract as "the fields
    usually come like this," not as a rigid field-by-field guarantee, and
    always validate against the `result` returned in your real environment.


## Backoffice


    No. They're two different authentication mechanisms for the same
    system. The backoffice login is a personal username and password.
    `client` and `secret` authenticate your application and generate
    `access_token` via `POST /api/token-generate`. See
    [Authentication](/en/guides/autenticacao) for the API side.


    Webhook setup (URL and key) is currently done by React IT on request,
    it's not yet a self-service screen. See
    [Webhooks](/en/guides/webhooks) for how to request activation.


    `backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` and `backoffice.idcerberus.com` are the
    same URLs used by the admin panel. When you call `/api/...` on them,
    you're talking to the API, not the visual interface. There's no
    separate URL just for the API: it's the same domain, different
    endpoints.


## Environments


    Not recommended. Staging and production use completely separate
    databases and credentials. Always test in staging first; use production
    only after validating the flow, with real data and awareness that
    production queries usually have a cost.


    Confirm, in this order: whether the token used is a production one (not
    staging), whether the production product has the same services enabled
    as the staging one, and whether the data tested in production is real
    (staging usually has fake data that doesn't exist in production
    sources). Configuration mismatch between environments is the most
    common cause here.


## Before opening a ticket

If your question isn't here, gather this information before contacting
support. It avoids back-and-forth and speeds up the response.

| Information | Where to find it |
| --- | --- |
| Environment (staging or production) | The base URL used in the call |
| `service` sent | The `service` field in your payload |
| `status.code` and `status.message` | The response body, not the HTTP status |
| `externalId` | Returned in the body, when present |
| Approximate time of the call | To cross-reference with internal logs |

See the full ticket format in
[Common integration errors](/en/guides/erros-comuns-integracao#how-to-request-support).


    Diagnosis by category: token, payload, image, and technical error.


    Specific technical symptoms, like PowerShell breaking curl.


    How it works, payload by source, and why there's no automatic retry.


    Technical terms used on this page and throughout the documentation.

# Status and errors

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/status-e-erros
Source: en/guides/status-e-erros.mdx
Description: Understand how to interpret responses, failures, and cases with no JSON body

# Status and errors

The idCerberus API separates the HTTP status from the technical status
returned in the body. When integrating, read both.

## Standard structure

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  },
  "externalId": "8e1ac243-4510-4ebf-ac7d-4b6d133dd619"
}
```

| Field | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `result` | Data returned by the queried product |
| `status.code` | Technical processing code |
| `status.message` | Technical processing message |
| `externalId` | External query identifier, when returned |

## How to interpret it

| Case | Practical meaning | Recommended action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP 200 and `status.code` 200 | The call was processed | Read `result` and follow the business rule |
| HTTP 200 and `status.code` 400 | Invalid payload or service without permission on the product | Read `status.message`, validate parameters and permission |
| HTTP 200 and `status.code` 401 | Product inactive or not found for the `client` used | Confirm whether the product is active, it's not a token problem |
| HTTP 401 or 403 (real) | Token missing, expired, or from another environment, rejected before processing | Generate a new token in the correct environment |
| Timeout | External source or network may have been slow | Apply controlled retry, without an aggressive loop |
| No JSON body | The endpoint returns another type of content | Handle it per the contract, like a PDF in the onboarding report |

> Atencao:
  A real exception to the first row of the table: if your product is prepaid
  and the balance is insufficient, the call returns HTTP 200 **and**
  `status.code` 200, but `status.message` carries something like "Not enough
  balance" and `result` comes back empty. Always read `status.message` when
  `result` comes back empty, even with HTTP 200 and `status.code` 200.

## Common problems

| Problem | Possible cause | How to resolve it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invalid token | Token generated with wrong credentials or environment | Generate a new token in the same environment as the call |
| Expired token | The token's validity period ended | Generate a new token and repeat the call |
| Missing `Authorization` | Header wasn't sent | Send `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}` |
| Missing `Content-Type` | JSON body sent without the correct header | Send `Content-Type: application/json` |
| Missing `service` field | Payload didn't specify which product to run | Include the `service` field in the body |
| Invalid CPF or CNPJ | Incomplete, masked, or out-of-format document | Review the value sent before calling the API |
| Service without permission | Product not enabled for the account | Confirm the service's release with the responsible team |
| External source unavailable | Query depends on an external agency, base, or processing | Retry with a controlled backoff or try again later |
| Wrong environment URL | Staging token used in production, or the reverse | Check whether the base URL and token are from the same environment |

## Error examples

### Missing or invalid token

When the `Authorization` header isn't sent, is expired, or belongs to
another environment, the API can return an authentication error.

```http
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
```

How to fix it:

1. Generate a new token at `POST /api/token-generate`.
2. Confirm the token was generated in the same environment as the call.
3. Send the header in the format below.

```http
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
```

### Missing `service` field

The `POST /api/service-api` endpoint needs the `service` field to know which
product to run.

Incorrect payload:

```json
{
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

Correct payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

### Missing required document

If the service requires `cpf`, `cnpj`, an image, or another required field,
send the corresponding field in the body.

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "CPF não encontrado."
  }
}
```

How to fix it:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_RFB_PF",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

### Product without permission or not enabled

If the credential doesn't have access to the product, the call can fail
even with a valid token.

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Serviço não disponível para este cliente."
  }
}
```

How to fix it:

1. confirm that `service` is written exactly as in the documentation;
2. validate whether the product is enabled for the account;
3. confirm you're calling the correct environment.

### External source unavailable

Some queries depend on external databases. When the source fails or is
slow, the API can return a technical error.

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 500,
    "message": "Failed to fetch information"
  }
}
```

How to handle it:

1. record the `externalId`, when it exists;
2. try again later with a limited retry;
3. don't run an infinite loop of calls;
4. if the error persists, send the payload and the attempt time to support.

## A negative result isn't a technical error

Some services return a negative query as a technical success. Examples:

| Result | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing on record | Criminal certificates or legal cases |
| Customer not found | CPF validation with an address |
| No debts | Active debts with zeroed totals |
| Not PEP | Person not politically exposed |

In these cases, the call can have `status.code` 200 and still represent a
negative business response.

## Handling best practices

1. Record the `externalId` when it's returned.
2. Don't use only the HTTP status to decide business success.
3. Handle an expired token by generating a new one.
4. Validate required fields before calling the API.
5. Avoid automatic retry on payload errors.
6. Use limited retries for timeouts or temporary external source failures.

## Decision example

```js
if (response.status?.code !== 200) {
    throw new Error(response.status?.message || "Falha no processamento");
}

return response.result;
```

# Common integration errors

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/erros-comuns-integracao
Source: en/guides/erros-comuns-integracao.mdx
Description: Practical diagnosis for token, access, payload, base64, OCR, empty return, and external failures

# Common integration errors

Use this page when a call fails, returns empty, or looks different than expected.

The most important rule: in `POST /api/service-api`, look at the response body, not just the HTTP status. A call can return HTTP 200 and still have processing come back as `REFUSED` or `ERROR`.

> Info:
  Looking for a specific technical symptom (environment error, PowerShell
  breaking `curl`, a response that isn't JSON)? See
  [Troubleshooting](/en/guides/troubleshooting), which is more to the point
  for those cases.


    Missing/expired token (HTTP 401/403) or product without permission for
    the service (HTTP 200, `status.code` in the body).


    Missing required field, wrong alias, invalid CPF/CNPJ, or malformed JSON.


    Base64, `image1`, `image2`, illegible document, or OCR without the expected field.


    `ERROR`, `500`, external failure, timeout, or investigation by `externalId`.


## Quick diagnosis

| Symptom | Common cause | How to fix it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` or `403` | Token missing, expired, invalid, or from another environment | Generate a new token in the same environment as the call |
| `Don't have access to the service` | Product without the service active or without API enabled | Check the product setup before touching the payload |
| `Unable to convert http message` | Invalid JSON, broken base64, or malformed body | Validate the JSON and generate the base64 again |
| API returns HTTP 200 with `REFUSED` | The call authenticated, but the business rule declined it | Read `status.message` and treat it as a valid decline |
| API returns HTTP 200 with `ERROR` | A technical failure happened during processing | Save `externalId`, the time, and the service called |
| Empty result `{}` | Data without a match, image not readable, or service with no return for that case | Test valid data and check `status.message` |
| Empty result `{}` with HTTP 200 and `status.code` 200 | On a prepaid product, it could be insufficient balance (`status.message`: "Not enough balance") | Check the organization's balance before investigating the payload |
| Expected field didn't come back | Field doesn't exist in the source or wasn't safely extracted | Don't make up data; treat a missing field as optional when the contract allows it |
| Base64 rejected | Broken encoding, truncated base64, or invalid file | Generate the base64 again from the original file (with or without the `data:image/...;base64,` prefix, both are accepted) |
| CPF/CNPJ not found | Masked or incomplete document, bad data, or wrong environment | Test without a mask and check the base URL |
| Timeout | External source was slow or unavailable | Apply controlled retry and record the `externalId`, when present |

## Token or access

Before investigating your code, confirm:

1. The call is going to the right environment.
2. The token was generated in the same environment.
3. The header is `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}`.
4. The product linked to the token has the service active.
5. The service is enabled for the API.
6. The alias sent in `service` is the calling alias configured for the product.

Typical example:

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Don't have access to the service"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "REFUSED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

In this case, the first thing to check is the product configuration. There's no point swapping the CPF, CNPJ, or image before confirming access.

## Payload

Fields that most often cause errors:

| Field | Watch out for |
| --- | --- |
| `service` | Must match the alias enabled on the product |
| `cpf` | Send without a mask when the service doesn't document another format |
| `cnpj` | Send the full CNPJ, preferably without a mask |
| `birthDate` | Use the format documented for the service |
| `documentType` | For React OCR, use `CNH` or `RG` depending on the document |
| `image1`, `image2`, `selfie1` | Confirm whether the service expects an image, selfie, front, back, or comparison |
| `key` | Use only when the flow supports a key for an already-stored file |

Minimal valid JSON example:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_REGISTRATION_DATA_CNPJ",
  "cnpj": "00000000000000"
}
```

## Image and OCR

For OCR services:

1. Use a real, sharp, complete image.
2. Send the full base64, without truncating it (with or without the `data:image/jpeg;base64,` prefix, both formats work).
3. For RG, send front and back when the service requires it.
4. For face queries, use a real selfie, not a photo of a document.
5. Check that the document sent matches the service.

Example error for a missing image:

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Imagem do verso do documento não encontrada"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "REFUSED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

Action: review the payload. For RG, send `image1` with the front and `image2` with the back.

If the return is:

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Não foi possível ler o documento"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "REFUSED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

Action: test a sharper image and confirm the document type matches the service.

## Technical error

A technical error usually shows up as `ERROR` or a failure message in the body:

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 500,
    "message": "Falha ao realizar OCR"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "ERROR",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

In this situation, save:

1. environment;
2. endpoint;
3. service sent;
4. approximate time;
5. `externalId`;
6. `status.code`;
7. `status.message`;
8. the payload without sensitive data.

Don't send a JWT token, `client`, `secret`, CPF, CNPJ, a real image, or full base64 over open channels.

## Checklist before contacting support

1. I confirmed the call's environment.
2. I generated a new token in the same environment.
3. I checked the service's alias in the product.
4. I validated that the service is active and has the API enabled.
5. I validated the JSON before sending it.
6. I removed the mask when the contract didn't require one.
7. For OCR, I checked whether the base64 is clean.
8. For OCR, I opened the image and confirmed it's legible.
9. I saved `externalId`, the time, and `status.message`.

## How to request support

Send a summary in this format:

```txt
Environment: HML or PROD
Endpoint: POST /api/service-api
Service: SERVICE_EXAMPLE
Approximate time: 2026-01-01 10:30
ExternalId: ...
Status code: ...
Status message: ...
What was expected: ...
What came back: ...
```

Don't include credentials, tokens, real documents, real images, or full base64.

# Troubleshooting

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/troubleshooting
Source: en/guides/troubleshooting.mdx
Description: Fix common problems when integrating with the idCerberus API

# Troubleshooting

Use this page when a call isn't working as expected.

> Info:
  Page focused on specific technical symptoms (401/403, wrong environment,
  PowerShell). For a broader diagnosis, with cards by category and a
  message template to request support, see
  [Common integration errors](/en/guides/erros-comuns-integracao).


    401/403, token from another environment, or a token that works in staging but not production.


    HTTP 200 that's actually an error: `status.code` 400 or 401 inside the body.


    Works in cURL but not your code, or PowerShell breaks the command.


    Success with no data, or a return that isn't JSON (like the report's PDF).


## I got a 401 or 403 (HTTP)

In `POST /api/service-api`, a real HTTP 401/403 only happens due to an
authentication problem: the call doesn't even reach service processing.

1. Missing token.
2. Expired token.
3. Token generated in another environment.

How to fix it:

1. Generate a new token.
2. Confirm whether the URL is staging or production.
3. Send the header:

```txt
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
```

> Atencao:
  "Product not enabled for the account" and "service without permission"
  **don't** generate HTTP 401/403 on this endpoint. The call returns HTTP
  200 with the problem described in `status.message` (`status.code` 400 or
  401 inside the body). See the next section.

## HTTP 200, but status.code other than 200

This is the most common error case in `POST /api/service-api`: the call
"worked" in the HTTP sense, but the body shows the real problem.

| `status.code` in the body | Cause | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | Invalid body, missing required field, wrong `service`, invalid CPF/CNPJ, external source unavailable | Read `status.message` for the exact reason |
| 401 | Product not found or inactive for the `client` used | Different from HTTP 401: here the token is valid, it's the product that's disabled |

How to fix it:

1. Read `status.message`.
2. Check whether the body is valid JSON.
3. Check whether you sent `Content-Type: application/json`.
4. Check whether the `service` field is correct.
5. Compare the body with the API Reference example.

## The token works in staging, but not in production

The token and URL need to be from the same environment.

| Environment | URL |
| --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` |

Generate a new token in production using production credentials.

## cURL works, but my code doesn't

Check:

1. Base URL.
2. HTTP method.
3. Headers.
4. JSON body.
5. Timeout.
6. JSON serialization.
7. `Authorization` header.
8. `Content-Type` header.

Compare your code's request with the API Reference request.

## PowerShell breaks the cURL command

On Windows, use `curl.exe` instead of `curl`.

```powershell
curl.exe --location "https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate" `
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" `
  --data "{\"client\":\"{client}\",\"secret\":\"{secret}\"}"
```

Plain `curl` alone can be interpreted by PowerShell as a different alias.

## The query returned success, but not the data I expected

Not every return with no data is a technical error.

Examples:

1. certificate with "nothing on record";
2. CPF not found in an address validation;
3. person not politically exposed;
4. company with no debts;
5. empty list of relationships.

Read `result` and apply your product's business rule.

## The response didn't come back as JSON

Some endpoints return another type of content. Example:

```txt
GET /api/history-onboarding-report/{tokenOnboarding}
```

This endpoint returns a PDF, not JSON.

## Quick checklist

Before requesting support, check:

1. Is the URL correct?
2. Is the HTTP method correct?
3. Was the token generated in the same environment?
4. Was the `Authorization` header sent?
5. Was the `Content-Type` header sent?
6. Is the body valid JSON?
7. Is the `service` field correct?
8. Is the CPF/CNPJ in the expected field?
9. Is the service enabled for the account?
10. Did you read `status.message`?

# Integration best practices

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/boas-praticas-integracao
Source: en/guides/boas-praticas-integracao.mdx
Description: Recommendations for integrating the idCerberus API securely and reliably

# Integration best practices

Use these recommendations to reduce failures, avoid exposing credentials,
and get your integration ready for production.

## Credentials and token

| Practice | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| Generate the token in the back end | Avoids exposing `client` and `secret` |
| Don't put `client` and `secret` in the front end | Users could inspect the credentials |
| Don't version credentials in Git | Avoids accidental leaks |
| Renew the token when it expires | The token has limited validity |
| Don't log the full JWT | The token can allow protected calls |

## Environments

1. Use staging for development and testing.
2. Use production only after validating the flow.
3. Don't mix a staging token with the production URL.
4. Don't mix a production token with the staging URL.

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` |

## Requests

1. Always send `Content-Type: application/json` on requests with a JSON body.
2. Always send `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}` on protected calls.
3. Validate required fields before calling the API.
4. Send CPF/CNPJ in the format expected by your flow.
5. Use a timeout on HTTP calls.

## Retry

Use retry only when it makes sense.

| Situation | Retry? |
| --- | --- |
| Timeout | Yes, with a limit |
| Temporary network failure | Yes, with a limit |
| Expired token | Generate a new token and repeat |
| Invalid payload | No |
| Service without permission | No |
| Invalid CPF/CNPJ | No |

## Responses

1. Don't use only the HTTP status to decide business success.
2. Also read `status.code` and `status.message`.
3. Handle a `status.code` other than 200.
4. Save `externalId` when it's returned.
5. Remember that a negative result isn't necessarily a technical error.

Example:

```js
if (body.status?.code !== 200) {
  throw new Error(body.status?.message || "Falha no processamento");
}

return body.result;
```

## Logs

Record useful information for investigation, but without exposing sensitive
data.

| Safe to log | Avoid logging |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoint called | `client` and `secret` |
| `service` code | Full JWT token |
| `status.code` | Full document without a need |
| `status.message` | Base64 images |
| `externalId` | Selfies and documents |

When you need to log CPF, CNPJ, phone, or email for investigation, prefer
masking part of the value. Tokens, images, selfies, and documents in base64
shouldn't be written to open logs.

## Production

Before going to production, validate the flow in staging, generate a token
with the correct environment's credentials, and confirm your application
handles success, error, and timeout responses.

# Glossary

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/glossario
Source: en/guides/glossario.mdx
Description: Common terms used in the idCerberus API documentation

# Glossary

This page explains common terms used in the guides and the API Reference.

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| API | A way for one system to talk to another system through requests |
| Endpoint | A specific URL that runs an operation |
| Request | A call sent to the API |
| Response | The response returned by the API |
| HTTP method | The type of operation, like `GET` or `POST` |
| Header | Information sent along with the call, like authentication or content type |
| Body | The content sent in the request, usually in JSON |
| JSON | The data format used in the API's examples |
| Base URL | The environment's starting address, like staging or production |
| HML | The staging environment, used for testing |
| Production | The environment used for real queries |
| Token | A temporary code used to authenticate calls |
| JWT | The format of the authentication token returned by the API |
| Bearer | The authentication type used in the `Authorization` header |
| `client` | The application identifier used to generate a token |
| `secret` | The application secret used to generate a token |
| `service` | The field that defines which product runs in `POST /api/service-api` |
| CPF | Individual taxpayer document |
| CNPJ | Business taxpayer document |
| `result` | The object with the data returned by the service |
| `status.code` | Technical processing code |
| `status.message` | Technical processing message |
| `externalId` | External query identifier, when returned |
| OCR | Extracting data from documents via image |
| Webhook | An automatic notification idCerberus sends to your URL when an onboarding changes status |
| `id-cerberus-token` | The header sent in every webhook call, used to confirm it came from idCerberus |
| FaceMatch | Facial comparison between two images |
| Liveness | Proof-of-life validation |
| KYC | Customer knowledge and validation process |
| PEP | Politically exposed person |

## Practical example

In this request:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

`service` tells the API which product to run, and `cpf` tells it which
person to query.

In this header:

```txt
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
```

`Authorization` is the header, `Bearer` is the authentication type, and
`{jwt_token}` is the token generated by the API.

# Service matrix

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/matriz-de-servicos
Source: en/guides/matriz-de-servicos.mdx
Description: Quick overview of the main services by document type, input, and moment of use

# Service matrix

This matrix helps you quickly find which service to use before opening the
full payload in the API Reference.

> Info:
  This page is a shortcut by goal. The full technical catalog, with every
  field and example for each service, lives in
  [Individual Services](/en/guides/servicos-pessoa-fisica) and
  [Business Services](/en/guides/servicos-pessoa-juridica). Use them as the
  reference source when you need a service's full contract.

> Nota:
  Every item below runs through `POST /api/service-api`, except the
  authentication, onboarding, and customer endpoints. On the central
  endpoint, the `service` field picks the product.


    Registration data, OCR, biometrics, risk, and CPF history.


    Registration data, owners, debts, protests, and CNPJ risk.


    Authentication, onboarding, customers, and other dedicated endpoints.


## Individuals

> Info:
  OCR services are listed in this matrix, but the full payloads are in the
  [OCR via Service API](/en/guides/service-api/sobre-ocr-service-api) guide. Use
  that guide when the call involves `image1`, `image2`, base64, an image
  URL, or `documentType`.

| Goal | Service | Main input | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Enrich registration data | `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT` | `cpf` | Get basic identification data |
| Check CPF at the Federal Revenue | `SERVICE_RFB_PF` | `cpf` | Validate the CPF's registration status |
| Check CPF at the Federal Revenue on-demand | `SERVICE_RFB_PF_ON_DEMAND` | `cpf` | Fetch registration data at query time |

| Read an emancipation document | `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION` | `image1` | Extract text and possible data from a variable document |
| Read a proof of address | `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS` | `image1` | Extract name, address, dates, and values when available |
| Search for a face in the base | `SERVICE_FACE_INDEX` | `image1` | Search for a face in the indexed base and return CPF/similarity when found |

| Query FGTS | `SERVICE_FGTS` | `cnpj` | Check the FGTS compliance certificate |
| Query basic data history | `SERVICE_HISTORY_BASIC_DATA` | `cnpj` | Track basic registration changes to the CNPJ over time |
| Query business owner influence | `SERVICE_OWNERS_INFLUENCE` | `cnpj` | Assess inferred influence from the business ownership structure |
| Query employee KYC and compliance | `SERVICE_EMPLOYEES_KYC` | `cnpj` | Check PEP and sanctions for the company's employees |
| Query marketplaces | `SERVICE_MARKETPLACE_DATA` | `cnpj` | Check the company's presence and performance in marketplaces |
| Query Federal Revenue - QSA | `SERVICE_RF_QSA` | `cnpj` | Get the CNPJ's complete corporate/management ownership structure |
| Query economic group relationships | `SERVICE_ECONOMIC_GROUP_RELATIONSHIPS` | `cnpj` | Map entities in the CNPJ's same economic group |
| Query phone numbers | `SERVICE_PHONES_EXTENDED_COMPANY` | `cnpj` | Get phone numbers associated with the company along with validity indicators |

## Flows outside service-api

| Goal | Endpoint | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Generate JWT token | `POST /api/token-generate` | Before protected calls |
| Generate onboarding token | `POST /api/token-history-onboarding` | Before starting SDK integration |
| Query onboarding | `GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}` | To retrieve the structured JSON result |
| Download onboarding report | `GET /api/history-onboarding-report/{tokenOnboarding}` | To get the final PDF |
| Query customer | `GET /api/customer` | To locate a customer by CPF or CNPJ |
| Change customer status | `POST /api/changeStatusOfCustomer` | To activate or deactivate a customer |

## Next step

After choosing the service, open [POST /api/service-api](/en/api-reference/serviços--pessoas/executar-serviço-de-dados-risco-ou-compliance) in the API Reference and copy the corresponding example.

# Service index

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/indice-de-services
Source: en/guides/indice-de-services.mdx
Description: Operational list of the services already documented in the API Reference

# Service index

Use this index when you already know which product you need to run and want to confirm the exact `service` name before building the call.

> Info:
All the queries below use `POST /api/service-api`. The product executed is defined by the `service` field in the body.

## How to search better

Search works best when the term appears as a title, alias or page text. If you do not know the exact alias, search by the type of document, data or problem you want to solve.


 Search for `cpf`, `revenue`, `score`, `risk`, `phone`, `email`, `ocr`, `face` or `lawsuits`.


 Search for `cnpj`, `revenue`, `credit risk`, `partners`, `domains`, `CNPJ card` or `compliance`.


 Search for `OCR`, `CNH`, `RG`, `CNPJ card`, `proof of address`, `base64` or `image1`.


 Go to the API Reference when you need body, curl, a summarized response and a common error.


### Search shortcuts


 Identification documents: CNH, RG, OAB, RNE/CRNM and passport.


 OCR of the CNPJ card with `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD`.


 OCR of a utility bill, invoice or proof of address with image/base64.


 Facial search by selfie in the face database.


 Score, rating, risk and credit services for PF/PJ.


 Validations and contact history.


> Atencao:
Before running the call, confirm which service is enabled on the client's product. The `service` field must receive exactly the public value shown in the catalog.

In practice: copy the `Service` value from the card or accordion of the product and send that value in the request body. The documentation does not expose internal integration aliases.

## Services by person type


 67 services for CPF, biometrics, OCR, contacts, risk, credit, compliance and electoral data.


 58 services for CNPJ, Federal Revenue, partners, contacts, risk, compliance, OCR and corporate data.

---

# About the OCR Service API

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/service-api/sobre-ocr-service-api
Source: en/guides/service-api/sobre-ocr-service-api.mdx
Description: Practical guide to choosing, configuring, testing, and interpreting OCR services in POST /api/service-api.

Use this page to integrate OCR services through `POST /api/service-api`.
It shows which service to use, how to build the payload, what the return
should look like, and what to check before opening a ticket or touching
your implementation.

> Basic requirement: the token needs to belong to the correct product, and
> the product needs to have the service active with the API enabled. If the
> product setup is incomplete, the call can authenticate and still return an
> access failure.

> Info:
  `SERVICE_OCR` can be processed by different partners depending on your
  product's configuration. This usually doesn't change what you do in the
  integration, but it can occasionally vary one specific `result` field
  (for example, the recognized document type). Treat the contract as "the
  fields on this page usually come like this," not as a rigid
  field-by-field guarantee.


    Use `SERVICE_OCR` when the document is an RG, CNH, OAB, RNE, or PASSPORT and the payload has `documentType`.


    Use `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD` to extract the CNPJ and OCR text from the CNPJ card.


    Use `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS` for bills, invoices, and accepted proofs.


    Use `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION` for variable documents with no fixed layout.


## Fastest test

If you just need to validate the call in staging, start with the
ready-made examples:


    Ready-made curl with `SERVICE_OCR`, `documentType: CNH`, and `image1`.


    Ready-made curl with `SERVICE_OCR`, `documentType: RG`, `image1`, and `image2`.


    Ready-made curl for `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD` with a CNPJ card image.


    Ready-made curl for `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS` with a base64 proof.


> Nota:
  For manual testing in Postman, use the [Copy and test](#copy-and-test) section. It builds the full JSON on your clipboard.

## Visual OCR journey


    Decide whether the test is CNH, RG, CNPJ card, proof of address, or an emancipation document before building the payload.


    Send a sharp, uncropped image, in base64 (with or without the `data:image/...;base64,` prefix, both work). Bad OCR almost always starts with a bad image or the wrong document.


    The useful return lives in `result`. Use `status`, `onboardingStatus`, and `externalId` to trace processing.


## Decision blocks


    Use `SERVICE_OCR` with `documentType`. For RG, send front and back when the document requires both sides.


    Use `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD`. The minimum expected is a valid CNPJ, a consistent `docType`, and a filled `genericOcr`.


    Use `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS`. The document needs a visible address and enough text to read.


    Use `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION`. Don't treat CPF, RG, or a code as required, since the layout can vary.


## Recommended path

If you need to test right now, follow this order:

1. Confirm the service on the client's product.
2. Generate a token for the same product.
3. Convert a real image to clean base64.
4. Send the correct OCR payload.
5. Validate `status`, `onboardingStatus`, `externalId`, and the fields inside `result`.

This path avoids mixing up a permission problem, a bad image, and a wrong
payload.

## What this page solves

| Audience | How to use it |
| --- | --- |
| Development | Copy the payload, understand required fields, and validate the expected return. |
| Product | Check whether the right service is configured for the right document. |
| Support | Separate a configuration problem, a bad image, a wrong payload, and a technical failure. |
| CS/Operations | Explain to the client what to send and what to expect from the response. |

The goal is to avoid trial and error. Before opening a ticket, the person
should be able to answer: which service was called, which image was sent,
which product authorized the call, and which `externalId` came back.

## Quick pick

| I need to read | Service | Send | Main return |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CNH | `SERVICE_OCR` | `documentType: CNH` + `image1` | CPF, name, birth date, CNH data |
| RG | `SERVICE_OCR` | `documentType: RG` + `image1` + `image2` | CPF, name, parents' names, birth date, RG data |
| CNPJ card | `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD` | `image1` | CNPJ, document type, OCR text |
| Emancipation document | `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION` | `image1` | OCR text, extracted fields, and structured analysis |
| Proof of address | `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS` | `image1` | Name, address, document type, dates, and amounts |

The `image1` field receives the image's base64. It works with clean base64
or with the `data:image/jpeg;base64,` prefix. The system accepts both
formats and removes the prefix automatically when present.

## Which image to use

| Service | Right image | Don't use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SERVICE_OCR` with CNH | A sharp photo or image of the full CNH | A selfie, a cropped screenshot, or a different document type |
| `SERVICE_OCR` with RG | Front in `image1` and back in `image2` | Only the front when the back is required |
| `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD` | A complete, legible CNPJ card | Articles of incorporation, an invoice, or a proof |
| `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS` | A bill, invoice, or accepted proof with a visible address | A personal document or selfie |
| `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION` | A legible notary document, declaration, deed, or certificate | A document unrelated to emancipation |

## Success criteria by service

| Service | Minimum expected success | When it declines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SERVICE_OCR` with CNH | Document read and the CNH's main fields returned. | Missing image, unread document, or inconsistent document type. |
| `SERVICE_OCR` with RG | Front and back sent, document read, and main data returned. | Missing back, illegible image, or core data not extracted. |
| `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD` | Valid CNPJ extracted and `docType` consistent with a CNPJ card. | CNPJ not found or invalid CNPJ. |
| `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION` | OCR returned text and the API returned the fields found, with no fixed layout required. | Empty OCR or an image that can't be read. |
| `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS` | OCR returned useful text and possible proof data. | Image not read or a document outside what's expected for a proof. |

Not every service has the same required fields. For variable documents,
like emancipation and proof of address, the return should carry what was
extracted without making up data.

## Full flow

1. Generate a token at `/api/token-generate`.
2. Confirm the product has the service active and enabled for the API.
3. Choose the correct `service` from the table above.
4. Convert the image to clean base64.
5. Send the payload to `POST /api/service-api`.
6. Validate `status.code`, `onboardingStatus`, `externalId`, and the fields inside `result`.

## Generate base64 in PowerShell

To copy just the image's base64:

```powershell
[Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\path\document.jpg")) | Set-Clipboard
```

This value is already clean base64. If your tool generates it with the
`data:image/jpeg;base64,` prefix (common in browsers, for example), you
don't need to remove it. The system accepts both formats.

## Copy and test

Use these blocks when you want to build the full JSON on your clipboard and
paste it directly into Postman's raw JSON body.
Just swap the file path and keep the `service` matching the OCR being tested.

### CNH

```powershell
$b64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\path\cnh.jpg"))
@{
  service = "SERVICE_OCR"
  documentType = "CNH"
  image1 = $b64
} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Clipboard
```

### RG with front and back

```powershell
$front = [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\path\rg-front.jpg"))
$back = [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\path\rg-back.jpg"))
@{
  service = "SERVICE_OCR"
  documentType = "RG"
  image1 = $front
  image2 = $back
} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Clipboard
```

### CNPJ card

```powershell
$b64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\path\cnpj-card.jpg"))
@{
  service = "SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD"
  image1 = $b64
} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Clipboard
```

### Proof of address

```powershell
$b64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("C:\path\proof-of-address.jpg"))
@{
  service = "SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS"
  image1 = $b64
} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress | Set-Clipboard
```

After running the command, paste the clipboard content into Postman under
`Body > raw > JSON`.

## Testing in Postman

1. Generate a token at `POST /api/token-generate`.
2. Copy the `access_token`.
3. Open `POST https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api`.
4. Add the header `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`.
5. Add `Content-Type: application/json`.
6. Paste the JSON generated by PowerShell into the raw body.
7. Run it and check `status`, `onboardingStatus`, `externalId`, and `result`.

Example headers:

```http
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Content-Type: application/json
```

## Checklist before contacting support

| Point | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Product | The token used belongs to the product where the service is active. |
| Payload | The `service` field uses the alias enabled for the product. |
| Image | The image opens normally and the text is legible to a person. |
| Base64 | The value decodes back into a valid image (with or without the `data:image/...;base64,` prefix, both are accepted). |
| Return | Save `externalId`, `status.message`, and the test's time. |

If these points are correct and OCR still fails, the ticket already arrives
with enough information to investigate without repeating basic tests.

## Quick diagnosis

| Symptom | Check first | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No access to the service | Token, product, whether the service is active, and API enabled. | Fix the product setup before touching the image. |
| Missing image | `image1`, `image2`, `image1Url`, `image2Url`, or `key`, depending on the OCR. | Regenerate the JSON and confirm the expected field made it into the body. |
| Returned `{}` | Whether the image is the right type and legible. | Test with a sharper image and validate whether the chosen service matches the document. |
| Got `ERROR` | `externalId`, time, environment, and a safe technical message. | Retry once; if it persists, escalate to technical support with the `externalId`. |
| Came back without an expected field | Whether the field visually exists in the document and whether this service's OCR returns that field. | Compare with the return pattern below and don't treat a missing field as a required contract. |

## Image quality

To reduce declines from poor reading:

| Item | Recommendation |
| --- | --- |
| Framing | Whole document visible, no cropped edges. |
| Sharpness | Text legible when opening the image manually. |
| Lighting | Avoid glare, heavy shadow, and blur. |
| Orientation | Prefer a straight document, without excessive rotation. |
| File | Use a real JPG/PNG image converted to base64. |

A document photo doesn't work for a face service. A selfie doesn't work for
document OCR.

## Product configuration

Before testing in staging or production, check:

| Setting | What to verify |
| --- | --- |
| Token | `client` and `secret` belong to the product being tested. |
| Service | The service is registered and active on the product. |
| API | The service is enabled for calls via the API. |
| Alias | The value sent in `service` is the product's calling alias. |
| Fields | The service has the expected input and output fields. |

If the return is `"Don't have access to the service"`, the first thing to
check is the product setup, not the image.

## Return pattern

The public return should stay clean, with the useful data inside `result`.

Success example:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "docType": "CNH",
    "name": "EXTRACTED NAME"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "OCR realizado com sucesso"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "APPROVED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

The client shouldn't depend on internal fields like:

1. `fieldsOutput`
2. `required`
3. `enabled`
4. `valid`
5. `callService`
6. `nextStep`
7. `fields`
8. `visible`

The practical, simple rule: the integrator looks at `result`. If a field
isn't in `result`, it shouldn't be used as a public API contract.

## Don't do this

| Avoid | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| Sending truncated or cut-off base64 | The file becomes corrupted and OCR fails to decode it. |
| Using an RG/CNH photo on a face service | Face and OCR use different flows. |
| Using a selfie for document OCR | OCR needs the document's image. |
| Testing RG by sending only the front | The back may contain important fields. |
| Testing a CNPJ card on the proof-of-address service | Each OCR has its own parser and criteria. |
| Putting real CPFs, CNPJs, or names in the documentation | Public examples should use fictitious data. |
| Assuming a missing field is always a bug | The field may not exist in the document or may not have been read. |

## Known limits

| Point | How to handle it |
| --- | --- |
| OCR doesn't guarantee a perfect read on a bad image | Validate sharpness, framing, and a complete document before contacting support. |
| Some fields may not exist in the document | The API should return only what was safely extracted. |
| A product without API enabled looks like an access error | Fix the product setup before touching the payload. |
| RG can vary by state/model | Always send front and back when the service requires an RG. |
| Emancipation has no single layout | Success depends on OCR text, not on every optional field. |
| Proofs vary a lot | `fullAddress`, amounts, dates, and barcode depend on the type of document sent. |

---

# Identification documents

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/service-api/identificacao-de-documentos
Source: en/guides/service-api/identificacao-de-documentos.mdx
Description: Service for extracting data from identification documents via API.

Use `SERVICE_OCR` to extract data from identification documents such as RG, CNH, OAB, RNE, and PASSPORT.

## RG / CIN

Payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR",
  "documentType": "RG",
  "image1": "FRONT_BASE64",
  "image2": "BACK_BASE64"
}
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "docType": "RG/CIN",
    "name": "EXTRACTED NAME",
    "fatherName": "FATHER'S NAME",
    "motherName": "MOTHER'S NAME",
    "birthDate": "yyyy-mm-dd",
    "rg": "000000000", // <- RG document only
    "rgIssuer": "SSP/UF",
    "rgIssueDate": "yyyy-mm-dd",
    "nationality": "BRA", // <- CIN document only
    "validDate": "yyyy-mm-dd", // <- CIN document only
    "naturality": "CITY/STATE",
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "OCR realizado com sucesso"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "APPROVED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```
