## Automatic identification

This type of OCR identifies the document by inference and extracts the
corresponding data from the identified document.

Payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR",
  "documentType": "IDENTIFICATION_DOCUMENT",
  "image1": "DOCUMENT_FRONT_BASE64",
  "image2": "DOCUMENT_BACK_BASE64" // <- Optional
}
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    // Depends on the identified document type.
  },
  "status": {
      "code": 200,
      "message": "OCR realizado com sucesso"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "APPROVED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

For now, this page covers RG, CNH, OAB, RNE, and PASSPORT. Other documents
should be validated once OCR support is finalized for each type.

## Expected fields by return

| DocumentType | Returned fields | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RG | `cpf`, `docType`, `name`, `birthDate`, `fatherName`, `motherName`, `rg`, `rgIssuer`, `rgIssueDate`, `nationality`, `naturality`, `validDate` | If the document sent is a `CIN`, it may include `nationality` and `validDate`, and not include `rg`. Send front and back of the document |
| CNH | `cpf`, `docType`, `name`, `birthDate`, `fatherName`, `motherName`, `cnhCategory`, `cnhNumber`, `validDate`, `emissionPlace`, `rg`, `rgIssuer`, `cnhIssueDate`, `cnhDocEmissionPlace`, `cnhFirstQualificationDate`, `cnhLastEmissionDate`, `renach`, `paidActivity`, `state` | Single document upload |
| OAB | `cpf`, `docType`, `name`, `birthDate`, `fatherName`, `motherName`, `rg`, `issueDate`, `naturality`, `registrationNumber`, `isOrganDonor`, `via`, `observations` | Send front and back of the document |
| RNE | `cpf`, `docType`, `name`, `birthDate`, `fatherName`, `motherName`, `rneNumber`, `rnmNumber`, `nationality`, `issueDate`, `classification`, `entryDate`, `naturality`, `sex`, `via`, `rneValidDate`, `issueBody`, `residencePeriod` | Fields exclusive to `RNE`: `entryDate`, `naturality`, `via`, `rneNumber`. Fields exclusive to `CRNM`: `rnmNumber`, `cpf`, `residencePeriod`.  Send front and back of the document |
| PASSAPORT | `docType`, `name`, `fatherName`, `motherName`, `birthDate`, `nationality`, `validDate`, `issueDate`, `naturality`, `sex`, `issueCountry`, `passaportType`, `passaportNumber`, `authority` | Single document upload |
| IDENTIFICATION_DOCUMENT | Depends on the document identified internally | The OCR text is analyzed to infer whether the document is a CNH, RG, OAB, RNE, or Passport. In this case, sending the back of the document, `image2`, is optional. |

Missing fields shouldn't show up as `null` just to fill out the contract.
The Service API's public standard is to return only useful data.

> Nota:
For questions about the API's return, see [Questions and Support](/en/guides/service-api/duvidas-e-suporte).

## CNPJ card OCR

Use `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD` for a CNPJ card image.

Payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD",
  "image1": "CNPJ_CARD_BASE64"
}
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "00000000000000",

  },

    "message": "Cartão CNPJ processado com sucesso!"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "APPROVED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

If the CNPJ isn't found or is invalid, the expected outcome is a decline
with a clear message. If the image, storage, or provider read fails, it
can return an error.

# Emancipation document

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/service-api/documento-de-emancipacao
Source: en/guides/service-api/documento-de-emancipacao.mdx
Description: Service for extracting data from emancipation documents via API.

## Emancipation OCR

Use `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION` for emancipation documents.

This document has no single layout. It can be a declaration, a deed, a
certificate, or a notary document. Because of this, the service should
prioritize OCR text and extract what it can, without declining just
because a CPF, RG, or code didn't appear.

Payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION",
  "image1": "DOCUMENT_BASE64"
}
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "docType": "EMANCIPATION_DOCUMENT",
    "genericOcr": "text extracted from the document",
    "extractedFields": {
      "cpf": "00000000000",
      "rg": "000000000",
      "authenticationCode": "ABC123456",
      "dates": ["2026-01-01"]
    },
    "analysis": {
      "isEmancipationRelated": true,
      "summary": "Document summary",
      "confidence": "MEDIUM",
      "evidence": ["Text mentions emancipation"],
      "warnings": ["Authentication code not found"]
    }
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Documento de emancipação processado com sucesso!"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "APPROVED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

## Expected fields by return

| Service | Most common fields in `result` |
| --- | --- |
| `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION` | `docType`, `genericOcr`, `extractedFields`, `analysis` |

Missing fields shouldn't show up as `null` just to fill out the contract.
The Service API's public standard is to return only useful data.

> Nota:
For questions about the API's return, see [Questions and Support](/en/guides/service-api/duvidas-e-suporte).

# Questions and Support

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/service-api/duvidas-e-suporte
Source: en/guides/service-api/duvidas-e-suporte.mdx
Description: Guidance for possible questions when testing OCR via API, and cases for contacting technical support.

## Common responses

| Scenario | Expected status | How to act |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OCR read and extracted data | `APPROVED` | Use the data in `result`. |
| Document is legible, but the main field didn't come back | `REFUSED` | Check whether the image matches the correct service. |
| Product without access to the service | `REFUSED` or an access message | Fix the product setup. |
| Real failure in the provider, image, or storage | `ERROR` | Retry the test and contact technical support if it persists. |


    When the token is valid, but the product doesn't have the service enabled for the API.


    When `image1`, `image2`, a URL, or `key` wasn't sent as the service expects.


    When the image arrives, but OCR doesn't extract enough data.


    When the failure needs to be investigated by `externalId`, logs, and environment.


Example of a decline due to a document not being read:

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Não foi possível ler o documento"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "REFUSED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

## Error examples

### Product without service access

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Don't have access to the service"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "REFUSED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

Action: check whether the service is active on the product and enabled for the API.

### Missing image

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Imagem do documento não encontrada"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "REFUSED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

Action: check whether `image1`, `image2`, `image1Url`, or `key` were sent
as required by the chosen service.

### RG with no back

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Imagem do verso do documento não encontrada"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "REFUSED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

Action: send `image1` with the front and `image2` with the back.

### Document not read

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Não foi possível ler o documento"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "REFUSED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

Action: check the image quality and whether the document matches the
service used.

### Internal error

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 500,
    "message": "Falha ao realizar OCR"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "ERROR",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

Action: save the `externalId`, retry with a valid image, and contact
technical support if it persists.

## Checklist before handing off to the client

1. Tested in staging with the correct product's token.
2. Confirmed the service is active and has the API enabled.
3. Confirmed the base64 isn't truncated (with or without the `data:image` prefix, both work).
4. Validated a success case.
5. Validated an expected decline case.
6. Checked whether the return came back without `fieldsOutput` and without internal metadata.
7. Checked whether `externalId` came back for tracing.
8. Checked whether the returned data came back inside `result`.

## Summary for support and CS

When a client says OCR didn't work, check in this order:

1. Whether the product and service are enabled for the API.
2. The correct alias in the `service` field.
3. The correct document type for the chosen service.
4. Whether the image is legible and complete.
5. The `status.message` returned.
6. `externalId` to trace the execution.

This avoids treating a configuration problem as an OCR problem, and also
avoids swapping the payload when the real error is in the product.

## Who to escalate to

| Situation | Who to contact | What to send |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No access to the service | Product/configuration | Product, client, alias sent, and a screenshot of the configuration. |
| OCR returns empty with a good image | Technical team | Payload without base64, the image used, and `externalId`. |
| 500 error | Backend/logs | `externalId`, environment, approximate time, and service used. |
| Wrong field extracted | Technical/OCR team | Image, return received, expected field, and `externalId`. |
| Not sure which service to use | Product/CS | Document type and the query's goal. |
| Mismatch between staging and production | Product + technical | Both environments' products, configured alias, and each environment's return. |

# Service families

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/service-api/familias-de-servicos
Source: en/guides/service-api/familias-de-servicos.mdx
Description: Browse the main product groups run via POST /api/service-api

# Service families

The `POST /api/service-api` endpoint brings together different products.
Grouping by family helps you quickly find the right payload instead of
treating the endpoint as one long, undifferentiated list.

> Info:
  This page groups by product family. The full technical catalog, with
  every field and example for each service, lives in
  [Individual Services](/en/guides/servicos-pessoa-fisica) and
  [Business Services](/en/guides/servicos-pessoa-juridica). Use them as the
  reference source when you need a service's full contract.


    CPF, registration, score, compliance, and complementary data services.


    CNPJ, business registration, business owners, risk, and compliance services.


    OCR, face, liveness, document analysis, and image payloads.


    Scores, validations, compliance, certificates, and risk signals.


## How to use this page

1. Choose the service family.
2. Copy the `service` code or confirm the calling alias configured for the product.
3. Open `POST /api/service-api` in the API Reference.
4. Select the corresponding example.
5. Map the expected response.

## Consumption pattern

Every product on this page uses the same call base:

```json
{
  "service": "service_code",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

The `service` field picks the product. The other fields vary by query:
document services use images or URLs, PF services use `cpf`, PJ services
use `cnpj`, and some certificates require extra data like `uf`, `rg`, or
`court`.

> Atencao:
  The API validates `service` against the services enabled for the
  client's product. Because of this, in some cases the value sent in the
  call can be a short product alias, not another alias documented in the
  catalog.

Before testing with the client, confirm the alias for the product, copy
that value into the body, and then fill in the required fields for the
chosen family.

| Documented alias | Product's short alias |
| --- | --- |
| `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` | `SERVICE_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` |
| `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY_CONSULT` | `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` |
| `SERVICE_ECONOMIC_RELATIONSHIP` | `economic_relationships` |
| `SERVICE_EMAIL_VALIDATION` | `SERVICE_EMAIL_VALIDATION1` |
| `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE`, `SERVICE_PROTEST_PF` | `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE` |
| `SERVICE_PROTEST_PJ` | `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE_PJ` |

Think of `POST /api/service-api` as a runner. The route is always the
same, but the service executed changes based on the value sent in
`service`.

Example:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

In this case, the API understands it should run the individual data
enrichment service. If `service` changes, the product run changes too.

| Query type | Main document | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Individual | `cpf` | May require extra data for certificates, validations, or biometrics |
| Business | `cnpj` | May require `uf` for state-level queries or complementary documents |
| Document and biometrics | `image1`, `image2`, `selfie1`, or URLs | Use base64 or a URL depending on the product |
| Onboarding/async document analysis | `key` | The key lets you query the result later |

> Nota:
  For implementation, copy the full example in the API Reference and use this page just to quickly pick the right product.

## PF registration and identity

| Product | `service` code | Main input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Individual enrichment | `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT` | `cpf` |

| PIS data | `SERVICE_PIS_CONSULTATION` | `cpf` |

| Professional history | `SERVICE_PROFESSIONAL_HISTORY` | `cpf` |
| Account holder's professional history | `SERVICE_PROFESSIONAL_HISTORY_OWNER_ONLY` | `cpf`, `birthDate` |
| PF financial data and addresses | `SERVICE_PF_FINANCIAL_AND_ADDRESS` | `cpf`, `birthDate` |
| Demographic data | `SERVICE_DEMOGRAPHIC_DATA_CPF` | `cpf`, `birthDate` |

## Documents and biometrics

In this family, the payload needs extra care: a wrong image, base64 with a
prefix, or an incorrect alias can let the call authenticate and still not
produce the expected return. For OCR, also use the [OCR via Service API](/en/guides/service-api/sobre-ocr-service-api) guide.

| Product | `service` code | Main input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| React OCR | `SERVICE_OCR` | `documentType`, `image1`, `image2` |
| Emancipation OCR | `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION` | `image1` |
| Proof of address OCR | `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS` | `image1` |
| Face search in the base | `SERVICE_FACE_INDEX` | `image1` |
| FaceMatch | `SERVICE_FACE_MATCH` | `image1`, `image2` |
| Biometric score / CNH validation with DataValid | `SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH` | `cpf`, `image1` |
| Digital document analysis | `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` | `key`, `image1`, `image2`, `selfie1` |
| Document analysis result | `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY_CONSULT` | `key` |

# Registration enrichment

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/pessoas/enriquecimento-cadastral
Source: en/guides/pessoas/enriquecimento-cadastral.mdx
Description: Query, validate, and complement individuals' registration data

# Registration enrichment

Use these services to validate CPF data, complement registrations, and
confirm associations between a person and their contact data. They support
onboarding, registration updates, fraud prevention, operational analysis,
and database qualification.

All services in this category are consumed through the endpoint:

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

The service run is defined by the `service` field.

## When to use it

Use this category when you need to:

1. validate whether a CPF is in good standing at the Federal Revenue;
2. enrich an individual's registration data;
3. confirm data associated with a phone number, address, or email;
4. query complementary information like MEI, PIS, E-Social, SUS card,
  addresses, and economic relationships.

## Available services

| Service | `service` code | Main use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PF data enrichment | `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT` | Returns registration data, status, parents' names, birth date, tax region, and name-uniqueness indicators |
| CPF status at the Federal Revenue | `SERVICE_RFB_PF` | Queries the CPF's registration status, date of birth, date of death, and information source |
| CPF at the Federal Revenue on-demand | `SERVICE_RFB_PF_ON_DEMAND` | Fetches or updates the CPF's registration data at request time |
| Individual data modeling | `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_MODELING` | Consolidates registration data, contacts, relationships, lawsuits, and addresses into a text view |
| AI prompt for a person | `SERVICE_PERSON_AI_PROMPT` | Generates an analytical reading of the queried person's consolidated data |
| Email validation | `SERVICE_EMAIL_VALIDATION` | Checks validity, normalization, risk, disposable domain, spam trap, and address characteristics |
| CPF validation with phone | `SERVICE_CPF_PHONE_VALIDATION` | Checks the association between a CPF and a phone number and returns a match rate |
| CPF validation with address | `SERVICE_CPF_ADDRESS_VALIDATION` | Checks the association between a CPF, a postal code, and an address number |
| MEI query | `SERVICE_MEI` | Returns MEI businesses associated with the CPF |
| PIS data | `SERVICE_PIS_CONSULTATION` | Queries Social Integration Program (PIS) data when available |
| SUS card | `SERVICE_ONDEMAND_SUS_CARD_PERSON_CPF` | Returns National Health Card data found for the CPF, with the card number, capture date, and birth data |
| E-Social validation | `SERVICE_ESOCIAL_REGISTRATION_QUALIFICATION` | Validates registration qualification in E-Social, with CPF, name, birth date, and PIS |
| Address query | `SERVICE_ADDRESS` | Returns addresses associated with the CPF |
| Data by phone number | `SERVICE_CONFIRM_PHONE` | Returns a person's data based on a phone number |
| Phone history | `SERVICE_PHONE_HISTORY` | Returns phone numbers associated with the CPF, line type, and a recency indicator |
| Email history | `SERVICE_EMAILS_EXTENDED` | Returns emails associated with the CPF along with usage, validation, and priority signals |
| Related people | `SERVICE_RELATED_PEOPLE` | Returns people related to the CPF and the identified relationship type |
| Related people's emails | `SERVICE_RELATED_PEOPLE_EMAILS` | Returns emails of people related to the CPF, with the identified relationship |
| Related people's phones | `SERVICE_RELATED_PEOPLE_PHONES` | Returns phones of people related to the CPF, with the identified relationship |
| Related people's addresses | `SERVICE_RELATED_PEOPLE_ADDRESSES` | Returns addresses of people related to the CNPJ, with the identified relationship |
| TSE - Polling place | `SERVICE_ONDEMAND_TSE_POLLING_PLACE_PERSON_CPF` | Returns the polling place, electoral status, and current biometrics at the TSE |
| Economic relationships | `SERVICE_ECONOMIC_RELATIONSHIP` | Returns economic relationships associated with the CPF |
| Professional history | `SERVICE_PROFESSIONAL_HISTORY` | Queries professional relationships and history |
| Account holder's professional history | `SERVICE_PROFESSIONAL_HISTORY_OWNER_ONLY` | Returns professional relationships where the person appears as the account holder or partner |
| PF financial data and addresses | `SERVICE_PF_FINANCIAL_AND_ADDRESS` | Combines registration data, addresses, and financial information into a single query |

## Quick example

Individual registration enrichment query:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

Payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "status": "REGULAR",
    "name": "PERSON NAME",
    "birthDate": "1998-07-05",
    "origin": "RECEITA FEDERAL",
    "age": 24
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

## How to combine services

A simple registration validation usually starts with `SERVICE_RFB_PF`. For
a fuller view, use `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT`. When the goal is to
validate contact or delivery, combine the email, phone, and address
queries.

# Biometrics and documents

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/pessoas/biometria-e-documentos
Source: en/guides/pessoas/biometria-e-documentos.mdx
Description: Validate documents, selfies, facial biometrics, and identity evidence

# Biometrics and documents

Use these services to extract data from documents, compare facial images,
validate liveness, and support identity decisions in onboarding and KYC
flows. They help reduce document fraud, automate document reading, and
verify whether the person presented matches the evidence sent.

All services in this category are consumed through the endpoint:

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

> Info:
  For OCR, start with the [OCR via Service API](/en/guides/service-api/sobre-ocr-service-api)
  guide. It brings together the payloads for RG, CNH, CNPJ card,
  emancipation, and proof of address, plus the clean return pattern in
  `result`.


    Extract data from RG, CNH, CNPJ card, proofs, and variable documents.


    Compare two facial images and read the similarity percentage.


    Process a document, an image, and a selfie in document-analysis flows.


## When to use it

Use these services when you need to:

1. extract data from documents via OCR;
2. compare face images with FaceMatch;
3. query a biometric score;
4. run digital document analysis and query the result later.

## Available services

| Service | `service` code | Main use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| React OCR | `SERVICE_OCR` | Reads RG/CIN, CNH, OAB, RNE/CRNM, passport, or auto-identifies, and returns clean fields inside `result` |
| CNPJ card OCR | `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD` | Extracts the CNPJ and OCR text from the CNPJ card |
| Proof of address OCR | `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS` | Extracts name, address, dates, and amounts when found |
| Emancipation OCR | `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION` | Reads variable emancipation documents and returns text, objective fields, and analysis |
| FaceMatch | `SERVICE_FACE_MATCH` | Compares two images and returns a status and facial similarity percentage |
| Biometric score | `SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH` | Compares a CPF and a selfie against official databases and returns similarity |
| CNH validation with DataValid | `SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH` | Validates CNH data with document-validation support |
| Digital document analysis | `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` | Processes a document, extracts data, and runs FaceMatch when a selfie is present |
| Document analysis result | `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY_CONSULT` | Queries the result of a document analysis using the key sent at creation |

## Documents supported in OCR

| Document | Value |
| --- | --- |
| CNH | `CNH` |
| RG | `RG` |
| New RG | `NEWRG` |
| RNE | `RNE` |
| CPF card | `CARTAOCPF` |
| Passport | `PASSPORT` |
| CRLV (vehicle registration) | `BR_CAR_LICENCE` |
| Utility bill | `LIGHTRECEIPT` |
| Work card (CTPS) | `CTPS` |

## Quick example

Facial comparison between two images:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_FACE_MATCH",
    "image1": "base64",
    "image2": "base64"
  }'
```

Payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_FACE_MATCH",
  "image1": "base64",
  "image2": "base64"
}
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "status": "Face picture match",
    "similarity": 99.95
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

## Best practices

1. Send sharp images, without cropping the document or the face.
2. Use `image1Url` and `image2Url` when the images are already hosted at a
  URL the service can access.
3. For documents with a front and back, send both images when available.
4. Combine OCR and FaceMatch when the flow requires more robust identity
  validation.

# Risk and compliance

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/pessoas/risco-e-compliance
Source: en/guides/pessoas/risco-e-compliance.mdx
Description: Assess exposure, restrictions, certificates, debts, and risk signals for individuals

# Risk and compliance

Use these services to identify risk signals associated with an individual,
including political exposure, certificates, criminal records, protests,
debts, lawsuits, warrants, and scores. They support decisions in
onboarding, credit, fraud prevention, compliance, and ongoing monitoring.

All services in this category are consumed through the endpoint:

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

## When to use it

Use this category when you need to:

1. check whether the person is a PEP or has relevant public exposure;
2. query sanctions and compliance history in a consolidated view;
3. assess propensity for fraud or default;
4. query certificates, criminal records, and nothing-on-record checks;
5. check protests, active debts, and lawsuits;
6. complement an approval pipeline with risk signals.

## Available services

| Service | `service` code | Main use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Politically exposed person | `SERVICE_PEP` | Indicates whether the CPF belongs to a Politically Exposed Person |
| Individual KYC and compliance | `SERVICE_PERSON_KYC` | Consolidates PEP, sanctions, and compliance history associated with the CPF |
| PF media exposure and profile | `SERVICE_MEDIA_PROFILE_EXPOSURE_PF` | Queries public exposure, notoriety, unpopularity, and news related to the CPF |
| PF active debt | `SERVICE_ACTIVE_DEBT_PF` | Returns totals and a list of active debts associated with the CPF |
| Fraud risk score | `SERVICE_FRAUD_RISK_SCORE` | Measures fraud propensity based on a risk factor |
| Financial risk | `SERVICE_FINANCIAL_RISK_SCORE` | Returns a score and a summarized financial risk reading |
| Default risk score | `SERVICE_DEFAULT_RISK_SCORE` | Returns a score, risk band, and expected probability of default |
| Credit score | `SERVICE_QUOD_CREDIT_SCORE_PERSON` | Queries an individual's credit score, with level and risk classification |
| Multi-data credit score | `SERVICE_BOAVISTA_ONE_SCORE_PERSON` | Queries an individual's multi-data credit score |
| Restrictive data | `SERVICE_BOAVISTA_CREDIT_SCORE_PERSON` | Queries an individual's restrictive credit data, with an indicator and count of restrictions |
| Negative flags | `SERVICE_QUOD_CREDIT_RISK_PERSON` | Queries an individual's negative credit flags, with level and risk classification |
| Propensity for online betting | `SEVICE_ONLINE_BETTING_PROPENSITY` (no R, official spelling) | Assesses signals of propensity for online betting associated with the CPF |
| Nothing on record in lawsuits | `SERVICE_NOTHING_RECORD_LAWSUITS` | Issues a "nothing on record" certificate in federal regional courts |
| Federal criminal records | `SERVICE_CRIMINAL_RECORD_FEDERAL` | Queries a federal criminal record certificate |
| Civil criminal records | `SERVICE_CRIMINAL_RECORD_CIVIL` | Queries a state criminal record certificate |
| Negative protest certificate | `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE` | Queries protests at notary offices and title details |
| Legal cases | `SERVICE_JURIDICAL_PROCESSES` | Queries legal and administrative cases associated with the CPF |
| Public servants | `SERVICE_PUBLIC_SERVANTS` | Queries relationships with public service |
| Arrest warrant | `SERVICE_ARREST_WARRANT` | Checks for an existing arrest warrant |

## Quick example

Fraud risk score query:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_FRAUD_RISK_SCORE",
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "factor": "minRisk or minattrition"
  }'
```

Payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_FRAUD_RISK_SCORE",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "factor": "minRisk or minattrition"
}
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "score": "8.0691",
    "factor": "MEDIUM RISK",
    "message": "Success calculating score"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

## Reading the results

The `status` object indicates the call's technical result. Business
signals live in the `result` object, such as certificate status, scores,
risk factors, debt amounts, protests, and indicators found. In critical
flows, combine more than one query to avoid basing a decision on a single
signal.

```bash
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_POLITICAL_INVOLVEMENT",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

Payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_POLITICAL_INVOLVEMENT",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "electionsCount": 5,
    "isCurrentlyInOffice": true,
    "wasFormerlyElected": true,
    "isPep": true,
    "amountDonated": 19804076,
    "amountReceived": 20599420,
    "politicalInvolvementScore": 1
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

## How to interpret it

These services don't replace an internal compliance policy, but they help
bring structured evidence about public exposure and electoral
relationships. Use the returns as inputs for risk classification,
enhanced due diligence, or monitoring.

# Business registration data

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/empresas/dados-cadastrais
Source: en/guides/empresas/dados-cadastrais.mdx
Description: Query registration status, official data, economic activities, and obligations of businesses

# Business registration data

Use these services to validate whether a company exists, enrich CNPJ data,
and query official registration information. They help with PJ onboarding
flows, registration analysis, database updates, fraud prevention, and
operational validation before opening a business relationship.

All services in this category are consumed through the endpoint:

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

The `service` field defines which query runs.

## When to use it

Use this category when you need to:

1. confirm a CNPJ's registration status at the Federal Revenue;
2. retrieve the official name, trade name, opening date, activities, and legal nature;
3. check state registration in SINTEGRA;
4. query extended addresses associated with the CNPJ;
5. query digital presence, domains, and online operation signals;
6. query periods, invoices, and barcodes for DAS MEI or Simples Nacional - MEI collection;
7. track the company's registration change history, share capital, and tax regime;
8. query phone numbers, merchant category (MCC), marketplace presence, online ads, and the company's reputation on review platforms;
9. query investment fund data linked to the CNPJ and the time evolution of capital, employees, and business owners.

## Available services

| Service | `service` code | Main use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PJ data enrichment | `SERVICE_CORPORATE_DATA_ENRICHMENT` | Returns the company's full registration, including official name, trade name, economic activities, legal nature, regime, and capital |
| CNPJ status at the Federal Revenue | `SERVICE_RFB_PJ` | Queries the CNPJ's registration status and the status date at the Federal Revenue |
| CNPJ at the Federal Revenue on-demand | `SERVICE_RFB_PJ_ON_DEMAND` | Fetches or updates the company's registration data at request time |
| SINTEGRA | `SERVICE_SINTEGRA_CONSULTATION` | Queries state registration data in SINTEGRA, including state, status, and CFDF when applicable |
| Extended business addresses | `SERVICE_ADDRESSES_EXTENDED_CNPJ` | Returns addresses associated with the CNPJ, including street, neighborhood, city, state, country, postal code, and address type |
| PJ electoral donations | `SERVICE_ELECTORAL_DONORS_CNPJ` | Queries electoral donations made by the company and aggregated statistics |
| PJ electoral service providers | `SERVICE_ELECTORAL_PROVIDERS_CNPJ` | Queries electoral service provision associated with the CNPJ |
| DAS MEI at the Federal Revenue | `SERVICE_DAS_MEI` | Queries DAS MEI periods, assessment status, invoice, and barcode |
| Simples Nacional - MEI collection | `SERVICE_PGMEI` | Queries the MEI's DAS with monthly collection history and payment status |
| Basic data history | `SERVICE_HISTORY_BASIC_DATA` | Queries the CNPJ's basic registration change history: name, tax regime, registration status, CNAE, and share capital |
| Merchant category | `SERVICE_MERCHANT_CATEGORY_DATA` | Queries the company's MCC categorization, by direct association with Abecs or inferred from the CNAE |
| Phone numbers | `SERVICE_PHONES_EXTENDED_COMPANY` | Queries phone numbers associated with the company, with validity, priority, and source indicators |
| Company evolution | `SERVICE_COMPANY_EVOLUTION` | Queries the time evolution of capital, employees, branches, and business owners, with growth trend |
| Marketplaces | `SERVICE_MARKETPLACE_DATA` | Queries the company's presence in marketplaces, stores operated, products listed, and ratings |
| Online ads | `SERVICE_ONLINE_ADS` | Queries online ads linked to the company on classifieds portals and peer-to-peer marketplaces |
| Ratings and reputation | `SERVICE_REPUTATIONS_AND_REVIEWS` | Queries the company's reputation across different review platforms, with a consolidated view and history |
| Investment fund data | `SERVICE_INVESTMENT_FUND_DATA` | Queries registration and operational information for investment funds associated with the CNPJ, per CVM |

## Quick example

Business registration enrichment query:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_CORPORATE_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cnpj": "cnpj"
  }'
```

Payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_CORPORATE_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "00000000000000",
    "status": "ATIVA",
    "name": "REACT IT SOLUCOES EM TECNOLOGIA LTDA",
    "fantasyName": "REACT IT SOLUTIONS",
    "origin": "Receita Federal",
    "regime": "SIMPLES",
    "foundedDate": "2018-04-04T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

## Best practices

1. Send the CNPJ without a mask when possible, keeping only digits.
2. Use data enrichment when you need to build a complete registration view of the company.
3. Use the CNPJ status when you only need to validate whether the company is active or in good standing.
4. For companies with state-level operations, combine Federal Revenue and SINTEGRA.

# Business owners and relationships

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/empresas/socios-e-relacionamentos
Source: en/guides/empresas/socios-e-relacionamentos.mdx
Description: Analyze ownership structure, business relationships, relationship circles, and risks associated with business owners

# Business owners and relationships

This category brings together queries to understand who's behind a
company, what ties exist between people and CNPJs, and what risks show up
around the ownership structure. It's useful for PJ onboarding, ultimate
beneficial owner analysis, business owner KYC, economic relationship
assessment, and investigating relevant ties.

All services in this category are consumed through the endpoint:

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

## When to use it

Use this category when you need to:

1. identify owners, representatives, and a company's relationships;
2. map individuals related to the CNPJ at the first level;
3. query the full corporate/management ownership structure (QSA) of the headquarters at the Federal Revenue;
4. map the economic group and infer the ownership structure's influence level;
5. assess legal cases associated with business owners, individually or aggregated;
6. query PEP, sanctions, and compliance history indicators for business owners.

## Available services

| Service | `service` code | Main use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Company relationships | `SERVICE_COMPANY_RELATIONSHIP` | Returns the company's relationships, including owners, employees, owned companies, and relationships with people |
| Business owners at the Federal Revenue | `SERVICE_COMPANY_RFB_OWNERS` | Returns registration data for business owners identified at the Federal Revenue |
| First-level partners | `SERVICE_FIRST_LEVEL_PARTNER` | Summarizes circles of individuals related to the CNPJ, with metrics on age, income, location, lawsuits, and distributions |
| Federal Revenue - QSA | `SERVICE_RF_QSA` | Queries the CNPJ's corporate/management ownership structure, with the headquarters' registration data and the list of business owners and administrators |
| Economic group relationships | `SERVICE_ECONOMIC_GROUP_RELATIONSHIPS` | Queries entities (people and companies) that are part of the same economic group as the CNPJ, with current and historical relationships |
| Business ownership influence | `SERVICE_OWNERS_INFLUENCE` | Infers the ownership structure's influence level, considering media exposure, political involvement, and business owners' lawsuits |
| Business owners' lawsuit distribution | `SERVICE_OWNERS_LAWSUITS_DISTRIBUTION` | Queries aggregated data on the distribution of lawsuits the company's business owners are involved in |
| Business owners' legal cases | `SERVICE_JURIDICAL_PROCESSES_PJ_OWNERS` | Queries cases associated with business owners and groups indicators by document |
| Business owners' KYC and compliance | `SERVICE_COMPANY_KYC_OWNERS` | Queries PEP exposure, current and historical sanctions, and relevant occurrences within the ownership structure |
| Business owners' electoral donations | `SERVICE_OWNERS_ELECTORAL_DONORS_CNPJ` | Queries electoral donations made by business owners linked to the CNPJ |

## Quick example

Company relationships query:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_COMPANY_RELATIONSHIP",
    "cnpj": "cnpj"
  }'
```

Payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_COMPANY_RELATIONSHIP",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "00000000000000",
    "relationshipTotal": 1,
    "totalOwners": 1,
    "totalEmployees": 1,
    "companyRelationships": [
      {
        "cpf": "77272722314",
        "name": "BUSINESS OWNER NAME",
        "relationshipName": "SOCIO-ADMINISTRADOR",
        "origin": "RECEITA FEDERAL"
      }
    ]
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

## How to combine services

A PJ analysis usually starts with `SERVICE_COMPANY_RELATIONSHIP` to
understand the company's structure. Next, `SERVICE_FIRST_LEVEL_PARTNER`
helps summarize the ownership surroundings. When you need to dig deeper
into risk, use `SERVICE_JURIDICAL_PROCESSES_PJ_OWNERS` and
`SERVICE_COMPANY_KYC_OWNERS`.

# Business compliance

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/empresas/compliance
Source: en/guides/empresas/compliance.mdx
Description: Query debts, protests, restrictions, and regulatory exposure of businesses

# Business compliance

Business compliance services help identify financial, regulatory, and
reputational risks tied to CNPJs. They can be used in PJ onboarding,
vendor monitoring, third-party assessment, credit processes, fraud
prevention, and AML/CFT routines.

All services in this category are consumed through the endpoint:

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

## When to use it

Use this category when you need to:

1. check a company's active debts with government agencies;
2. query protests at notary offices;
3. assess public exposure and news related to business owners;
4. assess exposure and compliance of companies related to the betting market;
5. identify ultimate beneficial owners and equity stake percentages;
6. query federal and state negative certificates (PGFN, CGU, CNJ, state debts, PCD, Simples Nacional);
7. assess aggregated KYC for the company's full economic group;
8. complement a registration analysis with risk and restriction signals.

## Available services

| Service | `service` code | Main use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PJ active debts | `SERVICE_ACTIVE_DEBT_PJ` | Queries the company's active debts with the government and returns totals, sources, and a list of debts |
| PJ negative protest certificate | `SERVICE_PROTEST_PJ` | Queries protests at notary offices and returns title details found |
| Business owners' media exposure and profile | `SERVICE_MEDIA_PROFILE_EXPOSURE_PJ` | Queries public exposure, notoriety, unpopularity, and news related to the company's business owners |
| PJ betting compliance | `SERVICE_COMPLIANCE_BET_PJ` | Queries sports exposure, betting relationship, registration data, and regulatory signals for companies in the sector |
| FGTS | `SERVICE_FGTS` | Queries the employer's FGTS compliance certificate |
| Labor lawsuits | `SERVICE_LABOR_LAWSUITS` | Queries an on-demand certificate stating whether there are labor lawsuits related to the company |
| Legal case distribution | `SERVICE_LAWSUITS_DISTRIBUTION_DATA_COMPANY` | Queries aggregated data on the distribution of lawsuits the company is involved in |
| Employee KYC and compliance | `SERVICE_EMPLOYEES_KYC` | Queries KYC and regulatory compliance indicators for employees, including PEP status and national and international sanctions |
| Union agreements | `SERVICE_SYNDICATE_AGREEMENTS` | Queries the union agreements signed between the company and the unions that represent its employees |
| PJ credit score | `SERVICE_QUOD_CREDIT_SCORE_COMPANY` | Queries a business's credit score by CNPJ, with level and risk classification |
| PJ multi-data credit score | `SERVICE_BOAVISTA_ONE_SCORE_COMPANY` | Queries a business's multi-data credit score by CNPJ |
| PJ restrictive data | `SERVICE_BOAVISTA_CREDIT_SCORE_COMPANY` | Queries a business's restrictive credit data, with an indicator and count of restrictions |
| PJ negative flags | `SERVICE_QUOD_CREDIT_RISK_COMPANY` | Queries a business's negative credit flags, with level and risk classification |
| PJ Quantum credit score | `SERVICE_QUANTUM_CUSTOM_SCORE_COMPANY` | Queries a business's Quantum credit score by CNPJ |
| Ultimate beneficial owners | `SERVICE_ULTIMATE_BENEFICIAL_OWNERS` | Identifies the company's ultimate beneficial owners, with an accumulated equity stake percentage through indirect chains |
| Equity stake percentage | `SERVICE_BOAVISTA_OWNER_PARTICIPATION_DATA_COMPANY` | Queries the equity stake percentage of each of the company's business owners |
| PGFN debts | `SERVICE_PGFN_COMPANY` | Queries a certificate for federal tax debts and active union debt at the PGFN |
| PCD quota | `SERVICE_PCD_COMPANY` | Queries a certificate confirming compliance with the legal PCD quota and rehabilitated beneficiaries |
| CGU negative certificate | `SERVICE_CGU_NEGATIVE_CERTIFICATE_COMPANY` | Queries active sanctions in CEIS, CNEP, and CEPIM |
| CNJ negative certificate | `SERVICE_CNJ_NEGATIVE_CERTIFICATE_COMPANY` | Queries civil convictions for administrative misconduct and ineligibility |
| State debt negative certificate | `SERVICE_STATE_DEBT_CERTIFICATE_COMPANY` | Queries state debts, available for every state |
| Simples Nacional status | `SERVICE_SIMPLES_COMPANY` | Queries enrollment status in Simples Nacional and SIMEI |
| Economic group KYC and compliance | `SERVICE_ECONOMIC_GROUP_KYC_COMPANY` | Queries aggregated PEP and sanctions indicators for the full economic group |

## Quick example

PJ betting compliance query:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_COMPLIANCE_BET_PJ",
    "cnpj": "cnpj"
  }'
```

Payload:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_COMPLIANCE_BET_PJ",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Expected response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "00000000000000",
    "status": "ATIVA",
    "origin": "Receita Federal",
    "officialName": "ANONYMIZED OFFICIAL NAME",
    "tradeName": "ANONYMIZED TRADE NAME",
    "isBet": false,
    "onlineBettingCompliance": []
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Consulta de API Realizada com Sucesso"
  }
}
```

## Reading the results

The `status` object indicates the query's technical result. Business
signals live in the `result` object, such as debt amounts, protests,
relationships, regulatory exposure, and compliance indicators. In critical
analyses, combine these services with registration data and ownership
relationships.

# Individual Services

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/servicos-pessoa-fisica
Source: en/guides/servicos-pessoa-fisica.mdx
Description: External services available for CPF queries

# Individual Services

Individual services let you query, validate, and enrich CPF data across
onboarding, KYC, fraud prevention, registration analysis, biometrics,
documents, compliance, and electoral data flows.

All of them run through the central services endpoint. The `service` field
defines which product will be processed, and the other fields vary
depending on the query chosen.

Before building the body, check the client's product to see which alias is
enabled. That's the value that should go in the `service` field.

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

In the `curl` examples, `{base_url}` represents the URL of the chosen
environment:

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` |

Example request:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

## How to use this catalog

This is the full technical reference for individuals. Use it when you need
a service's full contract. To navigate by goal or product family first, see
[Choose the right service](/en/guides/escolha-o-servico-certo),
[Service matrix](/en/guides/matriz-de-servicos), or
[Service families](/en/guides/service-api/familias-de-servicos).

Use this page to look up the full list of CPF services, their `service`
codes, main fields, and more extensive request and response examples.

> Atencao:
  The catalog shows the functional name and the documented alias for the
  service. If the client's product was configured with a short alias, use
  the product's alias in the `service` field. This avoids access errors
  even when the product is active.

Quick step to avoid errors:

1. Open the client's product in the Backoffice.
2. Confirm the alias enabled for the service.
3. Send that alias in the `service` field.
4. Use the table's other fields as the query's main input.

| Documented alias | Product's short alias |
| --- | --- |
| `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` | `SERVICE_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` |
| `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY_CONSULT` | `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` |
| `SERVICE_ECONOMIC_RELATIONSHIP` | `economic_relationships` |
| `SERVICE_EMAIL_VALIDATION` | `SERVICE_EMAIL_VALIDATION1` |
| `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE`, `SERVICE_PROTEST_PF` | `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE` |

> Info:
  OCR, document analysis, FaceMatch, and Liveness need a real image/base64,
  URL, or `key` to return complete data. A short payload helps validate
  authentication, product access, and the basic call format, but doesn't
  validate the full processing return.

## Status and errors

In the query response, the API includes a `status` object that indicates
the query's status. This object has `code` and `message` attributes, used
to interpret technical processing.

```json
{
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

For handling details, see [Status and errors](/en/guides/status-e-erros).

## Advanced queries added

Some services return consolidated information or analyses derived from
complementary sources. They follow the same call pattern for the
`POST /api/service-api` endpoint, but can have broader responses depending
on data availability for the query.

| Service | When to use it | Body example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SERVICE_RFB_PF_ON_DEMAND` | Look up the CPF at the Federal Revenue at query time | `{ "service": "SERVICE_RFB_PF_ON_DEMAND", "cpf": "cpf" }` |
| `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_MODELING` | Consolidate modeling data, contacts, relationships, lawsuits, and addresses | `{ "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_MODELING", "cpf": "cpf" }` |
| `SERVICE_PERSON_AI_PROMPT` | Generate an analytical text summary from the person's consolidated data | `{ "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_AI_PROMPT", "cpf": "cpf" }` |
| `SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH` | Validate a CNH with document-validation support | `{ "service": "SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH", "cpf": "cpf", "image1": "base64" }` |
| `SERVICE_FINANCIAL_RISK_SCORE` | Query the financial risk score | `{ "service": "SERVICE_FINANCIAL_RISK_SCORE", "cpf": "cpf" }` |
| `SERVICE_PF_FINANCIAL_AND_ADDRESS` | Combine registration data, addresses, and financial information | `{ "service": "SERVICE_PF_FINANCIAL_AND_ADDRESS", "cpf": "cpf" }` |
| `SERVICE_PROFESSIONAL_HISTORY_OWNER_ONLY` | Return professional history where the person appears as the account holder or partner | `{ "service": "SERVICE_PROFESSIONAL_HISTORY_OWNER_ONLY", "cpf": "cpf" }` |
| `SEVICE_ONLINE_BETTING_PROPENSITY` | Assess propensity for online betting | `{ "service": "SEVICE_ONLINE_BETTING_PROPENSITY", "cpf": "cpf" }` |

> Atencao:
  The alias `SEVICE_ONLINE_BETTING_PROPENSITY` is documented without the
  letter `R` in `SERVICE` because that's the spelling implemented in the
  backend. Don't change this spelling without technical validation, since
  the call may stop being recognized.

## Examples

### Individual data enrichment

The individual data enrichment query returns information about an
individual that exists in the Federal Revenue's site. The return can
include registration status, the query's protocol, an indication of death
when available, and other information related to the queried CPF.

This query's information is obtained from the Federal Revenue's public
individual query.

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

Authorization:

```http
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
Content-Type: application/json
```

Body:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cpf` | CPF |
| `result.status` | Status in the Federal Revenue's base |
| `result.statusDate` | Date of the status in the Federal Revenue's base |
| `result.name` | Name |
| `result.fatherName` | Father's name |
| `result.motherName` | Mother's name |
| `result.birthdate` | Date of birth |
| `result.birthCountry` | Country of birth |
| `result.dead` | Indication of death |
| `result.deathYear` | Year of death |
| `result.gender` | Gender |
| `result.age` | Age |
| `result.origin` | Source of the information |
| `result.fiscalRegion` | CPF's tax region |
| `result.numberOfPeopleWithTheSameName` | Number of people with the same full name |
| `result.nameWordCount` | Number of names in the full name |
| `result.nameUniqueScore` | Name uniqueness score, where `1` means unique and `0` extremely common |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "status": "REGULAR",
    "statusDate": "2022-05-29T00:00:00",
    "name": "PERSON NAME",
    "gender": "M",
    "fatherName": "FATHER'S NAME",
    "motherName": "MOTHER'S NAME",
    "birthDate": "1998-07-05",
    "birthCountry": "BRASILEIRA",
    "dead": false,
    "country": "BRAZIL",
    "fiscalRegion": "DF-GO-MS-MT-TO",
    "numberOfPeopleWithTheSameName": "3",
    "nameWordCount": "3",
    "nameUniqueScore": "0.994",
    "origin": "RECEITA FEDERAL",
    "age": 24
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

### CPF status at the Federal Revenue

The CPF status query at the Federal Revenue returns the registration
status of a CPF that exists in the Federal Revenue's public base.

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

Authorization:

```http
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
Content-Type: application/json
```

Body:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_RFB_PF",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "birthDate": "yyyy-MM-dd (optional)"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cpf` | CPF |
| `result.status` | Status in the Federal Revenue's base |
| `result.statusDate` | Date of the status in the Federal Revenue's base |
| `result.origin` | Source of the information |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_RFB_PF",
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "birthDate": "yyyy-MM-dd (optional)"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "123414124",
    "status": "REGULAR",
    "name": "EXAMPLE NAME",
    "birthDate": "yyyy-MM-ddT00:00",
    "dead": false,
    "origin": "RECEITA FEDERAL",
    "age": 30
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Consulta de API Realizada com Sucesso"

  "externalId": "1782ea0a-8663-41a8-b156-688527f5363b"
}
```

### React OCR

Use `SERVICE_OCR` to extract data from identification documents such as
RG/CIN, CNH, OAB, RNE/CRNM, and PASSPORT. To let the API identify the
document, send `documentType: IDENTIFICATION_DOCUMENT`.

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

Authorization:

```http
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
Content-Type: application/json
```

Body:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR",
  "documentType": "CNH",
  "image1": "base64"
}
```

Supported document types:

| Document | Value |
| --- | --- |
| CNH | `CNH` |
| RG / CIN | `RG` |
| OAB | `OAB` |
| RNE / CRNM | `RNE` |
| Passport | `PASSAPORT` |
| Automatic identification | `IDENTIFICATION_DOCUMENT` |

For full responses by document type, see
[Identification documents](/en/guides/service-api/identificacao-de-documentos).

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_OCR",
    "documentType": "CNH",
    "image1": "base64"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "name": "PERSON NAME",
    "fatherName": "FATHER'S NAME",
    "motherName": "MOTHER'S NAME",
    "birthDate": "1992-01-05",
    "cnhCategory": "AB",
    "cnhNumber": "07796497926",
    "emissionPlace": "DETRAN DE",
    "rg": "3451620",
    "rgIssuer": "SSP/UF",
    "cnhIssueDate": "2020-04-13",
    "renach": "DF767732467",
    "state": "DF"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "OCR realizado com sucesso"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "APPROVED",
  "externalId": "..."
}
```

### FaceMatch

This service compares two images and returns the similarity between the
people in the images. The images can be sent as base64 or by URL,
depending on the integration.

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

Authorization:

```http
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
Content-Type: application/json
```

Body:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_FACE_MATCH",
  "image1": "base64",
  "image2": "base64"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.status` | Facial similarity status for the images |
| `result.similarity` | Facial similarity for the images |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_FACE_MATCH",
    "image1": "base64",
    "image2": "base64"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "status": "Face picture match",
    "similarity": 99.95
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

| `result.unpopularityLevel` | Unpopularity level |
| `result.fullName` | Full name returned |
| `result.shortName` | Short name returned |
| `result.fullNameUniquenessScore` | Full name uniqueness score |
| `result.shortNameUniquenessScore` | Short name uniqueness score |
| `result.newsItems` | Related news found |

### Fraud risk score

The fraud risk score measures the fraud propensity of an interaction
associated with a CPF. This propensity is calculated using statistical
inference based on historical fraud information, and supports fraud
prevention and risk analysis decisions.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_FRAUD_RISK_SCORE",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "factor": "minRisk or minattrition"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cpf` | CPF |
| `result.score` | Fraud risk score |
| `result.factor` | Risk status returned by DataRisk: `HIGH RISK`, `MEDIUM RISK`, or `LOW RISK` |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_FRAUD_RISK_SCORE",
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "factor": "minRisk or minattrition"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "score": "8.0691",
    "factor": "MEDIUM RISK",
    "message": "Success calculating score"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

```json
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |

| `result.score` | Calculated score |
| `result.message` | Message with score and risk interpretation |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example response:

```json

  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "score": "650",
    "message": "Score: 650 | Análise: RISCO MÉDIO"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

### Default risk score

The default risk score identifies a customer or prospect's default risk
level. The result ranges from 0 to 1000; the higher the value, the lower
the default risk.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_DEFAULT_RISK_SCORE",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cpf` | CPF |
| `result.score` | Default risk score |
| `result.origin` | Score source |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_DEFAULT_RISK_SCORE",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "{00000000000}",
    "status": "REGULAR",
    "origin": "Datarisk",
    "score": "462",
    "rank": "E",
    "expectedDefault": "58.94%",
    "processType": "SEM PROCESSOS"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

### Biometric score

The biometric score query compares a CPF and a selfie against images
present in Federal Government databases, such as CPF, CNPJ, and CNH. The
return indicates the similarity index found.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "image1": "{base64Image}"
}
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cpf` | CPF |
| `result.status` | Biometric score query status |
| `result.message` | Query message |
| `result.similarity` | Image similarity score against the Federal Government's base |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH",
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "image1": "{base64Image}"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "status": "Altíssima probabilidade",
    "message": "Biometrics exist at the base of the Government",
    "similarity": 99.66
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

### CNH validation with DataValid

Validates CNH data with document-validation support. The service takes the
CPF and a reference image, usually in base64, to run the validation
available in the integration.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "image1": "base64"
}
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

> Nota:
  Currently, the return exposed by this service can be minimal and vary
  based on the availability of the document-validation integration. Use the
  call's status and the fields returned in `result` as the response's
  effective contract.

### Nothing on Record Certificate - Lawsuits

Issues a "nothing on record" certificate at federal regional courts. In the
electoral sphere, the query is only available for TRF1 and TRF4 sources.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_NOTHING_RECORD_LAWSUITS",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "court": "TRF1",
  "uf": "uf",
  "sphere": "CIVIL"
}
```

Optional parameters:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `court` | Court: `TRF1`, `TRF2`, `TRF3`, `TRF4`, or `TRF5` |
| `uf` | Brazilian federation state |
| `sphere` | Sphere: `CIVIL`, `CRIMINAL`, or `ELEITORAL` |

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cpf` | CPF |
| `result.status` | "Nothing on record" status |
| `result.origin` | "Nothing on record" source |
| `result.uf` | State for the record, when returned under this name |
| `result.state` | Court or state returned in the API example |
| `result.name` | Individual's name |
| `result.certificateNumber` | Certificate number |
| `result.certificateText` | Certificate text |
| `result.expirationDate` | Expiration date |
| `result.emissionDate` | Issue date |
| `result.type` | Certificate type |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_NOTHING_RECORD_LAWSUITS",
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "court": "TRF1",
    "uf": "uf",
    "sphere": "CIVIL"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "status": "NADA CONSTA",
    "origin": "NadaConsta",
    "state": "TRF1",
    "name": "Fulano",
    "certificateNumber": "212312312311231",
    "certificateText": "A Polícia Federal CERTIFICA, após pesquisa no Sistema Nacional de Informações Criminais - SINIC, que até a presente data, NÃO CONSTA decisão judicial condenatória com trânsito em julgado* em nome de NOME DA PESSOA, nascido(a) aos 05/07/1998",
    "expirationDate": "2022-10-20",
    "emissionDate": "2022-10-20",
    "type": "CIVEL E CRIMINAL"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

### Criminal Record Certificate - Civil

Issues a criminal record certificate with the queried state's Civil
Police. If the person has no record, the result's status returns as
`NADA CONSTA`. When there is a record, this query doesn't return a
description of the records.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_CRIMINAL_RECORD_CIVIL",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "rg": "rg",
  "uf": "uf"
}
```

Accepted parameters:

| Field | Description | Accepted value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cpf` | CPF number | Any text |
| `rg` | ID card (RG) number | Any text |
| `uf` | State | Any text |
| `motherName` | Mother's name | Any text |
| `fatherName` | Father's name | Any text |
| `rgIssuingAgency` | Document's issuing agency | Any text |
| `rgIssuingUf` | State of the document's issuing agency | Any text |
| `rgExpeditionDate` | Document's issue date | Any valid date |
| `dateFormat` | Format of the document's issue date | Example: `yyyy-MM-dd` |
| `placeOfBirth` | Place of birth | Any text |
| `address` | Address | Any text |
| `numberAddress` | Address number | Any number |
| `zipcode` | Postal code | Any text |
| `neighborhood` | Neighborhood | Any text |
| `city` | City | Any text |

Required parameters by state:

| State | CPF | UF | RG | MOTHERNAME | FATHERNAME | RGISSUINGAGENCY | RGISSUINGUF | RGEXPEDITIONDATE | DATEFORMAT | PLACEOFBIRTH | ADDRESS | NUMBERADDRESS | NEIGHBORHOOD | CITY | ZIPCODE |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MG | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| CE | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| RR | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| MT | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | Optional | Required | Required | - | - | Required | - | - | - | - | - |
| RJ | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | Optional | Required | - | Required | - | - | Semi-required | Semi-required | Semi-required | Semi-required | Semi-required |
| PE | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | - | Required | Required | - | - | Required | Semi-required | - | Semi-required | Semi-required | - |
| PA | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | - | - | Required | - | - | Required | - | - | - | - | - |
| MS | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | - | Required | Required | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| SE | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | Optional | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| BA | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | Optional | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| SP | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | Optional | - | - | Required | Required | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| ES | Required | Required | Required | Semi-required | Optional | - | Required | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| RS | Required | Required | Required | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - |

States available for query: `BA`, `CE`, `ES`, `MG`, `MS`, `MT`, `PA`,
`PE`, `RJ`, `RR`, `RS`, `SE`, and `SP`.

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cpf` | CPF |
| `result.status` | Criminal record certificate status |
| `result.uf` | Queried state |
| `result.emissionDate` | Certificate issue date |
| `result.expirationDate` | Certificate expiration date, when returned |
| `result.certificateNumber` | Criminal record certificate number |
| `result.certificateText` | Criminal record certificate text |
| `result.origin` | Certificate source |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_CRIMINAL_RECORD_CIVIL",
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "rg": "rg",
    "uf": "uf"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "status": "NADA CONSTA",
    "uf": "BA",
    "emissionDate": "00:00 de 20/12/2022",
    "certificateNumber": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
    "certificateText": "Antecedentes Criminais CERTIFICADO DE ANTECEDENTES CRIMINAIS Nome: NOME DA PESSOA Número do Rg: 14781688 Nome do Pai: NOME DO PAI Nome da Mãe: NOME DA MÃE Data de Nascimento: 19/6/1997 Naturalidade: \"Certifico que o requerente acima qualificado NÃO registra antecedentes criminais até a presente data no Centro de Documentação e Estatística Policial (CEDEP), da Polícia Civil \". IMPORTANTE: Este certificado é válido somente com a apresentação da cédula de Identidade expedida pelo Instituto de Identificação Pedro Melo/DPT/SSP. Este certificado foi emitido terça-feira, 20 de dezembro de 2022 e está disponível para consulta no endereço https://exemplo.com/validar, informando o código 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 Obs: Este certificado tem validade até a data 20/3/2023 Imprimir Fechar Janela",
```

### Email validation

Runs a real-time verification of the given email, applied to scenarios
such as fraud prevention, correct email identification, marketing,
campaigns, and sending billing communications.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_EMAIL_VALIDATION",
  "email": "email@email.com"
}
```

Possible statuses:

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `VALID` | The email is valid and has no restrictions |
| `INVALID` | The email is invalid |
| `UNKNOWN` | Validation wasn't completed within the time limit |

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.email` | Email |
| `result.status` | Email status |
| `result.normalizedEmail` | Normalized email |
| `result.address` | Address |
| `result.account` | Email account |
| `result.domain` | Email domain |
| `result.disposable` | Indicates whether the email is temporary |
| `result.roleAddress` | Indicates whether the email references a group |
| `result.riskyAccount` | Indicates a risky account pattern |
| `result.riskyDomain` | Indicates a risky domain pattern |
| `result.junk` | Indicates possible spam or junk mail |
| `result.limited` | Indicates volume-based filtering rules |
| `result.acceptAll` | Indicates whether the domain accepts any email |
| `result.possibleSpamTrap` | Indicates a possible spam trap email |
| `result.wasSyntaxValid` | Indicates whether the original syntax is valid |
| `result.wasSyntaxNormalized` | Indicates whether the syntax was normalized |
| `result.wasOwnershipFound` | Indicates whether domain ownership was found |
| `result.possibleStoogeDomain` | Indicates a possible front-man domain |
| `result.domainType` | Domain type |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{
    "service": "SERVICE_EMAIL_VALIDATION",
    "email": "usuario@example.com"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "email": "usuario@example.com",
    "status": "VALID",
    "normalizedEmail": "usuario@example.com",
    "address": "usuario@example.com",
    "account": "teste",
    "domain": "test.com",
    "disposable": false,
    "roleAddress": false,
    "riskyAccount": false,
    "riskyDomain": false,
    "junk": false,
    "limited": false,
    "acceptAll": false,
    "possibleSpamTrap": false,
    "wasSyntaxValid": true,
    "wasSyntaxNormalized": false,
    "wasSiteFound": true,
    "wasOwnershipFound": false,
    "possibleStoogeDomain": false,
    "domainType": "BLOG"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

### CPF validation with phone

Checks the association between a CPF and a phone number at Brazil's main
carriers. This service can help reduce costs and validate before sending
messages.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_CPF_PHONE_VALIDATION",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "phone": "11900000000"
}
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cpf` | CPF |
| `result.phone` | Phone number |
| `result.operator` | Carrier name returned in the API example |
| `result.carrierName` | Carrier name, when returned under this name |
| `result.validCarrierPhone` | Indicates whether the phone number is valid |
| `result.matchRateCpfPhone` | Match rate between the CPF and the phone number |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_CPF_PHONE_VALIDATION",
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "phone": "11900000000"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "phone": "5561982358585",
    "operator": "EXAMPLE CARRIER",
    "validCarrierPhone": true,
    "matchRateCpfPhone": 100
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

### CPF validation with address

Validates the association between a CPF and an address at Brazil's main
telecom carriers. This query helps confirm whether the individual is
associated with the given address, and also supports location-related
checks.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_CPF_ADDRESS_VALIDATION",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "zipcode": "00000-000",
  "numberAddress": 13
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cpf` | CPF |
| `result.zipcode` | Postal code |
| `result.numberAddress` | Address number |
| `result.carrierName` | Telecom carrier name |
| `result.zipCodeMatchRate` | Match rate between CPF and postal code |
| `result.numberMatchRate` | Match rate between CPF, postal code, and the given number |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_CPF_ADDRESS_VALIDATION",
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "zipcode": "00000-000",
    "numberAddress": 13
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "message": "Customer not found",
    "carrierName": "CLARO S.A.",
    "zipcode": "00000000",
    "zipCodeMatchRate": -1,
    "numberMatchRate": -1,
    "numberAddress": "13"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

### E-Social validation

The E-Social validation queries the individual's registration status in
E-Social. Although the query can use the NIT, this field isn't required.
If the NIT isn't sent, the API uses the data available in the base.

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

Authorization:

```http
Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}
```

Body:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_ESOCIAL_REGISTRATION_QUALIFICATION",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "nit": "(optional)"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |

| `result.status` | Registration validation status |
| `result.message` | Query message |
| `result.name` | Name |
| `result.birthdate` | Date of birth |
| `result.pis` | PIS number |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_ESOCIAL_REGISTRATION_QUALIFICATION",
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "nit": "(optional)"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "status": "VERIFIED",
    "message": "Os dados estão corretos.",
```

### Digital document analysis

This service extracts information from the sent document and runs
FaceMatch between the given selfie and the document, and can also compare
it against government databases.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY",
  "key": "84bfcd2e-2336-4e30-bcab-15348b7890b5",
  "image1": "base64",
  "image2": "base64",
  "selfie1": "base64"
}
```

Input fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `key` | Key used to query the document analysis result. Can be a UUID or another key defined by the integration |
| `image1` | Document in base64, PDF, or image, with the front side of the RG or CNH. Can also contain the full CNH photo. Required field |
| `image2` | Document in base64 with the back of the RG or CNH. Optional field |
| `selfie1` | Selfie of the person on the document for FaceMatch. Optional field |

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cpf` | CPF |
| `result.name` | Name |
| `result.fatherName` | Father's name |
| `result.motherName` | Mother's name |
| `result.birthdate` | Date of birth |
| `result.cnhCategory` | CNH category |
| `result.expeditionDate` | Issue date |
| `result.rg` | RG number |
| `result.rgUf` | RG's state |
| `result.reanch` | RENACH number |
| `result.place` | Document's place of issue |
| `result.validDate` | Expiration date |
| `result.biometry` | FaceMatch between the document and selfie against the government base |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY",
    "key": "84bfcd2e-2336-4e30-bcab-15348b7890b5",
    "image1": "base64",
    "image2": "base64",
    "selfie1": "base64"
  }'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "00000000000",
    "name": "PERSON NAME",
    "fatherName": "FATHER'S NAME",
    "motherName": "MOTHER'S NAME",
    "birthDate": "1984-05-21",
    "cnhCategory": "AD",
    "expeditionDate": "19/03/2021",
    "rg": "3261880",
    "rgUf": "DF",
    "reanch": "DF765309297",
    "place": "Distrito Federal, Goiás, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul ou Tocantins",
    "validDate": "2026-02-24",
    "biometry": 1
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

# Business Services

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/guides/servicos-pessoa-juridica
Source: en/guides/servicos-pessoa-juridica.mdx
Description: External services available for CNPJ queries

# Business Services

Business services let you query, validate, and enrich CNPJ data across PJ
onboarding flows, registration analysis, business KYC, business owner
assessment, tax standing, debts, protests, and compliance.

Just like individual services, all of them run through the central
services endpoint. The `service` field defines which product will be
processed.

Before building the body, check the client's product to see which alias is
enabled. That's the value that should go in the `service` field.

```http
POST /api/service-api
```

In the `curl` examples, `{base_url}` represents the URL of the chosen
environment:

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` |

Example request:

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_CORPORATE_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

## How to use this catalog

This is the full technical reference for businesses. Use it when you need
a service's full contract. To navigate by goal or product family first, see
[Choose the right service](/en/guides/escolha-o-servico-certo),
[Service matrix](/en/guides/matriz-de-servicos), or
[Service families](/en/guides/service-api/familias-de-servicos).

Use this page to look up the full list of CNPJ services, their `service`
codes, main fields, and more extensive request and response examples.

## Related guides

| Guide | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| [Service families](/en/guides/service-api/familias-de-servicos) | To navigate by product group. |
| [OCR via Service API](/en/guides/service-api/sobre-ocr-service-api) | For CNPJ card, image, base64 payloads and return examples. |
| [API Reference](/en/api-reference/autorização/gerar-token-de-api) | For endpoint-by-endpoint details. |

> Atencao:
  For PJ protests, some products use a short alias in the body. If
  `SERVICE_PROTEST_PJ` or `SERVICE_PROTEST_PJ` are documented, but the
  product is configured with a short alias, send
  `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE_PJ` in the `service` field.

Quick step to avoid errors:

1. Open the client's product in the Backoffice.
2. Confirm the alias enabled for the service.
3. Send that alias in the `service` field.
4. Use the table's other fields as the query's main input.
