## CNPJ on-demand query

The `SERVICE_RFB_PJ_ON_DEMAND` service runs the CNPJ query at the Federal
Revenue in on-demand mode. Use it when the integration needs to fetch or
update the company's registration information directly at request time.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_RFB_PJ_ON_DEMAND",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "00000000000000"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

> Nota:
  This service runs the on-demand query, but the response currently exposed
  can be minimal. For a more complete registration view of the company, also
  use `SERVICE_CORPORATE_DATA_ENRICHMENT`.

## Examples

### Business data enrichment

Returns information about a business that exists at the Federal Revenue,
such as official name, trade name, founding date, activities, legal
nature, and share capital.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_CORPORATE_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Example with `curl`:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_CORPORATE_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cnpj": "cnpj"
  }'
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cnpj` | CNPJ |
| `result.status` | CNPJ status at the Federal Revenue |
| `result.statusDate` | Status update date |
| `result.name` | Official name |
| `result.country` | Country where the company was created |
| `result.fantasyName` | Trade name |
| `result.origin` | Source of the information |
| `result.regime` | Tax regime type |
| `result.age` | Company age in years |
| `result.registrationStatusDate` | Registration status update date |
| `result.foundedDate` | Founding date |
| `result.activities` | Company activities |
| `result.legalNatureCode` | Legal nature code |
| `result.legalNatureActivity` | Legal nature description |
| `result.capital` | Initial capital, written out |
| `result.capitalRS` | Initial capital in reais |
| `result.nire` | Business Registry Identification Number |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "00000000000000",
    "status": "ATIVA",
    "statusDate": "2022-07-26T00:00:00Z",
    "name": "EXAMPLE COMPANY LTDA",
    "country": "Brazil",
    "fantasyName": "EXAMPLE COMPANY",
    "origin": "Receita Federal",
    "regime": "SIMPLES",
    "age": 4,
    "registrationStatusDate": "2018-04-04T00:00:00Z",
    "foundedDate": "2018-04-04T00:00:00Z",
    "activities": [
      {
        "IsMain": true,
        "Code": "6209100",
        "Activity": "SUPORTE TECNICO, MANUTENCAO E OUTROS SERVICOS EM TECNOLOGIA DA INFORMACAO"
      },
      {
        "IsMain": false,
        "Code": "6201501",
        "Activity": "DESENVOLVIMENTO DE PROGRAMAS DE COMPUTADOR SOB ENCOMENDA"
      },
      {
        "IsMain": false,
        "Code": "6201502",
        "Activity": "WEB DESIGN"
      },
      {
        "IsMain": false,
        "Code": "6202300",
        "Activity": "DESENVOLVIMENTO E LICENCIAMENTO DE PROGRAMAS DE COMPUTADOR CUSTOMIZAVEIS"
      }
    ],
    "legalNatureCode": "2062",
    "legalNatureActivity": "SOCIEDADE EMPRESARIA LIMITADA",
    "capital": "DEZ MIL REAIS",
    "capitalRS": "10000.00",

  "status": {
```

### Company relationships query

Queries the company's relationships, including owners, employees, owned
companies, and ownership ties.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_COMPANY_RELATIONSHIP",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cnpj` | CNPJ |
| `result.isFamilyCompany` | Indicates whether the owners belong to the same family |
| `result.isFamilyEmployees` | Indicates whether employees belong to an owner's family |
| `result.relationshipTotal` | Total number of relationships |
| `result.totalOwners` | Total number of owners |
| `result.totalEmployees` | Total number of employees |
| `result.totalOwned` | Total number of owned companies |
| `result.companyRelationships` | The company's relationships |
| `result.companyRelationships.cpf` | Related CPF |
| `result.companyRelationships.name` | Name |
| `result.companyRelationships.relationshipName` | Relationship name |
| `result.companyRelationships.relationshipType` | Relationship type |
| `result.companyRelationships.origin` | Source of the information |

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "00000000000000",
    "isFamilyCompany": false,
    "isFamilyEmployees": false,
    "relationshipTotal": 1,
    "totalOwners": 1,
    "totalEmployees": 1,
    "totalOwned": 1,
    "companyRelationships": [
      {
        "cpf": "77272722314",
        "name": "EXAMPLE NAME",
        "country": "Brazil",
        "relationshipName": "SOCIO-ADMINISTRADOR",
        "relationshipType": "REPRESENTANTELEGAL",
        "origin": "RECEITA FEDERAL",
        "relationshipStartDate": "2021-03-01",
        "relationshipEndDate": "2021-03-01"
      }

    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

### SINTEGRA query

The SINTEGRA query looks up information in the Integrated System for
Information on Interstate Goods and Services Operations, on the official
government site. SINTEGRA tracks interstate operations carried out by ICMS
taxpayers and helps businesses issue invoices for customers.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_SINTEGRA_CONSULTATION",
  "cnpj": "cnpj",
  "uf": "uf"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cnpj` | CNPJ |
| `result.status` | CNPJ status in SINTEGRA |
| `result.uf` | CNPJ's state |
| `result.cfdf` | Federal District Tax Registration, exclusive to companies registered in the DF |
| `result.origin` | Source of the information |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example request:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_SINTEGRA_CONSULTATION",
    "cnpj": "cnpj",
    "uf": "uf (optional)"
}'
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "30108283000000",
    "status": "NOT REGISTERED",
    "uf": "DF",
    "cfdf": "0785286100111",
    "origin": "Sintegra"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

### Extended business addresses

Returns the complete list of addresses associated with the queried CNPJ
(current and historical), with normalized data on street, neighborhood,
city, state, country, postal code, and address type, plus an aggregated
summary with totals and pass-through dates. Use this query when the
registration analysis needs to go beyond the main address returned by
basic CNPJ queries.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_ADDRESSES_EXTENDED_CNPJ",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cnpj` | Queried CNPJ |
| `result.addresses` | List of addresses associated with the company (all values come as text/string) |
| `result.addresses.address` | Street address |
| `result.addresses.number` | Number |
| `result.addresses.complement` | Complement, when present |
| `result.addresses.neighborhood` | Neighborhood |
| `result.addresses.city` | City |
| `result.addresses.state` | State |
| `result.addresses.country` | Country |
| `result.addresses.zipcode` | Postal code |
| `result.addresses.addressType` | Address type (e.g., `COMMERCIAL`, `RESIDENTIAL`) |
| `result.addresses.isActive` | `"true"`/`"false"`, indicates whether the address is currently active |
| `result.addresses.isMainForEntity` | `"true"`/`"false"`, indicates whether it's the company's main address |
| `result.addressesExtendedTotal` | Total number of addresses found |
| `result.addressesExtendedTotalActive` | How many are active |
| `result.addressesExtendedOldestPassageDate` / `result.addressesExtendedNewestPassageDate` | Date of the oldest and most recent pass-through across all addresses |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "00000000000000",
    "addresses": [
      {
        "address": "EXAMPLE AVENUE",
        "number": "1000",
        "neighborhood": "CENTRO",
        "city": "SAO PAULO",
        "state": "SP",
        "country": "BRASIL",
        "zipcode": "01001000",
        "addressType": "COMMERCIAL",
        "isActive": "true",
        "isMainForEntity": "true"
      }
    ],
    "addressesExtendedTotal": 1,
    "addressesExtendedTotalActive": 1,
    "addressesExtendedOldestPassageDate": "2018-02-10",
    "addressesExtendedNewestPassageDate": "2026-05-12"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Consulta de API Realizada com Sucesso"
  }
}
```

### First-level partners query

Searches for aggregated circles of individuals related to the given CNPJ.
These people are retrieved from the companies' ownership structure data.

Notes:

1. A circle can exist with no participating individuals.
2. The circles' return is contained in the main result object.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_FIRST_LEVEL_PARTNER",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cnpj` | CNPJ |
| `result.circleType` | Circle type |
| `result.totalEntities` | Total number of related entities |
| `result.totalDistinctAddresses` | Total number of distinct related addresses |
| `result.totalDistinctPhones` | Total number of distinct related phone numbers |
| `result.totalDistinctEmails` | Total number of distinct related emails |
| `result.totalEmployedEntities` | Total number of related people who are employed |
| `result.totalCompaniesOwned` | Total number of owned companies |
| `result.totalRelatedEntities` | Total number of related people |
| `result.totalPEPs` | Total number of politically exposed people |
| `result.totalPublicServants` | Total number of related public servants |
| `result.totalClassMember` | Total number of people registered with professional bodies |
| `result.totalLivingPeople` | Total number of living people in the circles |
| `result.totalDeceasedPeople` | Total number of deceased people in the circles |
| `result.minAge` | Minimum age among the entities |
| `result.maxAge` | Maximum age among the entities |
| `result.avgAge` | Average age among the entities |
| `result.circleTotalIncomeRange` | Total income range for the entities |
| `result.entitiesAvgIncomeRange` | Average income range for the entities |
| `result.avgGeographicDistance` | Average geographic distance |
| `result.totalLawSuits` | Total number of lawsuits |
| `result.genderDistribution` | Distribution by gender |
| `result.ageRangeDistribution` | Distribution by age range |
| `result.incomeRangeDistribution` | Distribution by income range |
| `result.stateDistribution` | Distribution by state |
| `status.code` | Status message code |
| `status.message` | Status code message |

Example request:

```bash
curl --location '{base_url}/api/service-api' \

    "service": "SERVICE_FIRST_LEVEL_PARTNER",

}'
```

### Business owners' legal cases query

Queries legal and administrative cases related to business owners.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_JURIDICAL_PROCESSES_PJ_OWNERS",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.totalLawsuitsOwners` | Total number of business owners' lawsuits |
| `result.totalLawsuitsReplaceOwners` | Total number of substitute owners' lawsuits |
| `result.totalLawsuitsAsAuthorOwners` | Total number of lawsuits as plaintiff |
| `result.totalLawsuitsAsOtherOwners` | Total number of lawsuits in other roles |
| `result.avgLawsuitsOwners` | Average number of lawsuits per business owner |
| `result.lawSuitsOwners` | Lawsuits grouped by business owner |

### Business owners' KYC and compliance query

Queries KYC and compliance information for all of the company's business
owners in a single call (individuals and businesses), including political
exposure (PEP) and sanctions on national and international restrictive
lists.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_COMPANY_KYC_OWNERS",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.totalCurrentPep` | Number of business owners currently classified as PEP |
| `result.totalHistoricallyPEP` | Number of business owners with a PEP history (includes anyone who was PEP and no longer is) |
| `result.totalCurrentSanctioned` | Number of currently sanctioned business owners |
| `result.totalHistoricallySanctioned` | Number of business owners with a sanctions history |
| `result.averageSanctionsPerOwner` | Average number of sanctions per business owner (rounded) |
| `result.pepPercentage` | Percentage of business owners classified as PEP |
| `result.kycOwners` | Combined list with the KYC breakdown for each business owner (individuals and businesses) |
| `result.companyOwners` / `result.peopleOwners` | The same breakdown as `kycOwners`, but already split into business and individual owners |
| `kycOwners[].isPep` | Indicates whether the business owner is currently PEP |
| `kycOwners[].isCurrentlySanctioned` | Indicates whether the business owner is currently sanctioned |
| `kycOwners[].sanctionsHistory` | The business owner's full sanctions history |
| `kycOwners[].highConfidenceSanctionsHistory` | The same history, filtered to a `matchRate` above 90; use this list for automated decisions |
| `kycOwners[].pepHistories` | The business owner's history of positions and political exposure |

There's no `partnersHistory` field in this service's return. The
per-business-owner breakdown comes in `kycOwners` (or
`companyOwners`/`peopleOwners`).

### Business owners' media exposure and profile

Queries public exposure and media profile for the business owners related
to the CNPJ. The return carries a list in `results`, with one item per
individual found.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_MEDIA_PROFILE_EXPOSURE_PJ",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}
```

Main response fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `results.cpf` | Queried business owner's CPF |
| `results.mediaExposureLevel` | Media exposure level |
| `results.celebrityLevel` | Public notoriety level |
| `results.unpopularityLevel` | Unpopularity level |
| `results.fullName` | Full name returned |
| `results.shortName` | Short name returned |
| `results.fullNameUniquenessScore` | Full name uniqueness score |
| `results.shortNameUniquenessScore` | Short name uniqueness score |
| `results.newsItems` | Related news found |

# Welcome

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/boas-vindas
Source: en/api-reference/boas-vindas.mdx
Description: Start implementing the idCerberus API endpoints

# Welcome

Start your technical integration with the idCerberus API. This reference
brings together the endpoints, request examples, response examples,
authentication, and return structures used to integrate onboarding, KYC,
biometrics, risk, compliance, and data enrichment products.

Use this section when you're implementing in code. For product context,
suggested flows, and domain explanations, see the guides.

> Nota:
  Every endpoint page has a test panel right in the browser, no need for
  Postman. Fill in your `access_token` and the body fields right there and
  click send to see the real response.


    Open the `POST /api/token-generate` endpoint with request, response, and
    a cURL example.


    Create the token used to start an onboarding flow via SDK.


    Query the consolidated result of an onboarding process.


    Use `POST /api/service-api` to run data, risk, document, biometric, and
    compliance queries.


    See payloads with images, base64, `documentType`, and clean examples in `result`.


    Query customers by the CPF or CNPJ provided in `documentKey`.


    Activate or deactivate customer records through the API.


## Base URL

The API has separate environments for staging and production. The endpoint
structure is the same; what changes is the base URL.

Use the same method, headers, and payload in both environments. To switch to
production, just swap the staging URL for the production URL.

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` |

Example of a full staging URL:

```txt
POST https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api
```

Example of a full production URL:

```txt
POST https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/service-api
```

## Authentication

Protected calls require a JWT token in the `Authorization` header.


    Send `client` and `secret` to `POST /api/token-generate`.


    The response contains `access_token` and `expires_in`.


    Use the format `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}`.


Staging:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "client": "{client}",
    "secret": "{secret}"
  }'
```

Production:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "client": "{client}",
    "secret": "{secret}"
  }'
```

Response:

```json
{
  "access_token": "{jwt_token}",
  "expires_in": "300"
}
```

## First request

To run single-shot queries, use `POST /api/service-api`. The `service`
field defines which product will be processed.

Staging:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

Production:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "service": "SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT",
    "cpf": "cpf"
  }'
```

## How to find the right example

Inside `POST /api/service-api`, examples are separated by product name.
Choose the example by the `service` code and replace the test values with
real data.

The endpoint is a single one, but the examples are organized as a technical
catalog. In practice, each example represents a different product run
through the same endpoint.

| Need | `service` code |
| --- | --- |
| Enrich CPF data | `SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT` |
| Check CPF at the Federal Revenue | `SERVICE_RFB_PF` |
| Read a document via OCR | `SERVICE_OCR` |
| Compare two faces | `SERVICE_FACE_MATCH` |
| Check CNPJ status | `SERVICE_RFB_PJ` |
| Query a company's relationships | `SERVICE_COMPANY_RELATIONSHIP` |
| Query PJ active debts | `SERVICE_ACTIVE_DEBT_PJ` |
| Query PJ betting compliance | `SERVICE_COMPLIANCE_BET_PJ` |

To browse every group, see [Service families](/en/guides/service-api/familias-de-servicos).

## How to read POST /api/service-api

| Part | How to interpret it |
| --- | --- |
| `service` | Code of the product that will run |
| Additional fields | Parameters required by the chosen product |
| Request example | Ready-to-copy payload to adapt |
| Response example | Expected structure of that product's return |
| Schemas | Generic structures and supporting schemas for the most-used returns |

## Reference conventions

| Convention | How to apply it |
| --- | --- |
| `{jwt_token}` | Replace with the token returned by `POST /api/token-generate` |
| `cpf` and `cnpj` | Send the documents in the format expected by your integration contract |
| `base64` | Send only the encoded content of the image or document |
| Optional fields | Send them only when the service requires extra support to increase accuracy |
| `status.code` | Use to handle technical success or failure of the processing |
| `result` | Use to map the business data returned by the product |

## Response pattern

Most queries return:

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  }
}
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result` | Business data returned by the query |
| `status.code` | Technical processing code |
| `status.message` | Technical processing message |
| `externalId` | External query identifier, when returned |

> Nota:
  Not every endpoint returns JSON. Downloading the onboarding report returns a PDF file.

## Main endpoints

| Operation | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| [Generate token](/en/api-reference/autorização/gerar-token-de-api) | `POST /api/token-generate` |
| [Generate TokenOnboarding](/en/api-reference/integração-via-sdk/gerar-tokenonboarding-para-sdk) | `POST /api/token-history-onboarding` |
| [Query onboarding](/en/api-reference/integração-via-sdk/consultar-resultado-de-onboarding) | `GET /api/onboarding/report/{tokenOnboarding}` |
| [Download onboarding PDF](/en/api-reference/integração-via-sdk/baixar-relatório-pdf-do-onboarding) | `GET /api/history-onboarding-report/{tokenOnboarding}` |
| [Run external service](/en/api-reference/serviços--pessoas/executar-serviço-de-dados-risco-ou-compliance) | `POST /api/service-api` |
| [Query customer](/en/api-reference/customers/consultar-cliente) | `GET /api/customer?documentKey={documentKey}` |
| [Change customer status](/en/api-reference/customers/alterar-status-de-cliente) | `POST /api/changeStatusOfCustomer` |

## Status and errors

Use `status.code` and `status.message` to interpret technical processing.
When there's a failure, handle the returned message before repeating the
call.

```json
{
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Failed to fetch information"
  }
}
```

## Recommended path

1. Generate a token at `POST /api/token-generate`.
2. Open the endpoint you want to consume.
3. If you're using `POST /api/service-api`, select the example by the `service` field.
4. Test it in the page's own panel (with your `access_token` and staging data) before copying it into your code.
5. Replace the test values with real data.
6. Validate the expected response and map the `result` fields.
7. Use the guides when you need to understand the product's business context.

# How to run a service

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/como-executar-service
Source: en/api-reference/como-executar-service.mdx
Description: Step by step to authenticate, choose the environment, build the body and call a service in the idCerberus API.

# How to run a service

This page explains the standard flow to run any product documented in the API Reference.

> Info:
Most queries use the `POST /api/service-api` endpoint. The `service` field defines which product will be executed.

> Atencao:
Before running the call, confirm which service is enabled on the client's product. The `service` field must receive exactly the public value shown in the catalog.

In practice: copy the `Service` value from the card or accordion of the product and send that value in the request body. The documentation does not expose internal integration aliases.

## Step by step

| Environment | Base URL | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Homologation | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com` | Tests, validations and development. |
| Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com` | Real use, after the client has been released. |

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{
  "client": "{client}",
  "secret": "{secret}"
}'
```

Use the value returned in `access_token` in the `Authorization` header of the next calls.

Use the individual (PF) and business (PJ) catalogs to copy the exact value of the `service` field.

1. [Individual (PF) services](/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-fisica)
2. [Business (PJ) services](/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-juridica)
3. [Services by use case](/en/api-reference/services-por-caso-de-uso)

The body always needs `service`. The other fields depend on the chosen product.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_RFB_PF",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}
```

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
--data '{
  "service": "SERVICE_RFB_PF",
  "cpf": "cpf"
}'
```

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  },
  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

1. `result`: data returned by the product.
2. `status.code`: processing code.
3. `status.message`: short processing message.
4. `externalId`: external identifier for the query, when returned.

## Common errors

| Situation | How to fix |
| --- | --- |
| Missing, expired or invalid token | Generate a new token and send `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}`. |
| `service` field written incorrectly | Copy the service from the API Reference catalog. |
| Product uses a short alias | Confirm with the product which alias is enabled and send that value in the `service` field. |
| Missing CPF, CNPJ, image or required parameter | Check the fields section for the chosen service. |
| Document, OCR or biometrics service returned a parameter error | Send a real image/base64, URL or `key`. Short payloads only test authentication and product access. |
| Product not released to the client | Confirm commercial/technical release before running in production. |
| Response without data in `result` | Confirm whether the queried document has information available for that product. |

# Individual (PF) services

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-fisica
Source: en/api-reference/services-pessoa-fisica.mdx
Description: Explicit catalog of individual (PF) services available via API, with expected fields and request examples.

> Info:
Explicit catalog of individual (PF) services available via API, with expected fields and request examples. All services use `POST /api/service-api`; the product executed is defined by the `service` field in the body.

> Atencao:
Use exactly the value shown in `Service`. Do not send an internal alias or integration name.

## Before testing


 See the token, headers, standard body, `result`, `status` and `externalId`.


 Set up HML, generate a token and run `POST /api/service-api` with a real payload.


 Payloads for CNH, RG, proof of address, CNPJ card, base64 and image errors.


 Full examples for CPF, OCR, Face Index, risk and score.


## How to use this page


 Use the cards below to find the right group of services.


 In the full catalog, open the service accordion and copy the example body.


 Use `result` as the public contract and preserve `status`, `onboardingStatus` and `externalId`.


## How to interpret any response


 Read the `result` object first. It concentrates the business fields the client should consume.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the call processed, was refused or failed.


 Keep `externalId` for tests, support and audits. It is the most practical identifier for the query.


 Do not rely on internal metadata. The integration should only map the documented public fields.


## Service families


 5 services: `SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH`, `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION`, `SERVICE_FACE_INDEX` and 2 more.


 14 services: `SERVICE_ADDRESS`, `SERVICE_CPF_ADDRESS_VALIDATION`, `SERVICE_CPF_PHONE_VALIDATION` and 11 more.


 8 services: `SERVICE_ELECTION_CANDIDATE_DATA_CPF`, `SERVICE_ELECTORAL_DONORS_CPF`, `SERVICE_ELECTORAL_PROVIDERS_CPF` and 5 more.


 2 services: `SERVICE_MEDIA_PROFILE_EXPOSURE_PF`, `SEVICE_ONLINE_BETTING_PROPENSITY`.


 6 services: `SERVICE_CRIMINAL_RECORD_CIVIL`, `SERVICE_CRIMINAL_RECORD_FEDERAL`, `SERVICE_JURIDICAL_PROCESSES` and 3 more.


 17 services: `SERVICE_PROFESSIONAL_HISTORY_OWNER_ONLY`, `SERVICE_ACTIVITIES_INDICATORS`, `SERVICE_PERSON_AI_PROMPT` and 14 more.


 6 services: `SERVICE_RFB_PF_ON_DEMAND`, `SERVICE_RFB_PF`, `SERVICE_DEMOGRAPHIC_DATA_CPF` and 3 more.


 9 services: `SERVICE_ACTIVE_DEBT_PF`, `SERVICE_QUOD_CREDIT_SCORE_PERSON`, `SERVICE_CREDIT_SCORE` and 6 more.


## Full catalog

Open a service to see when to use it, required fields, body, curl and a summarized response.

**Service:** `SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH`

**When to use:** Use to compare the submitted image against available biometric databases and return the similarity.

**What it returns:** Returns CNH document validation, including biometric score, facial similarity, validation status and checked fields.


 Required fields: `service`, `cpf`, `image1`.


 Main fields in `result`: `cpf`, `biometricScore`, `validated`, `validationStatus`.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `cpf`, `image1`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

### Step by step

1. Generate the token at `POST /api/token-generate` and send it in the `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}` header.
2. Build the body with the exact `service` and the required fields listed below.
3. Run `POST /api/service-api` in the chosen environment.
4. Check `status.code` and `status.message` to validate the technical processing.
5. Map the `result` fields per the summary and the response example for this service.

### Copy and test

Use this body in Postman under `Body > raw > JSON`. Only change the test values.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "image1": "{base64Image}"
}
```

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
--data '{
  "service": "SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "image1": "{base64Image}"
}'
```

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
--data '{
  "service": "SERVICE_DATAVALID_CNH",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "image1": "{base64Image}"
}'
```

### Body fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `service` | Yes | Exact code of the product that will be executed by the central endpoint. |
| `cpf` | Yes | The queried individual's CPF. |
| `image1` | Yes | First image sent as base64 or an equivalent reference, depending on the product. |

### Main result fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cpf` | CPF related to the query result. |
| `result.biometricScore` | Field returned in the result object for the client's consumption. |
| `result.validated` | Date returned by the query, depending on the service context. |
| `result.validationStatus` | Field returned in the result object for the client's consumption. |

### How to consume the response


 Public data from the service. It is the main object to map into the client's system.


 Technical status of the call, with `code` and `message`.


 When returned, summarizes the operational outcome: `APPROVED`, `REFUSED` or `ERROR`.


 Identifier to trace the query in support, logs or audits.


### Summarized response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "biometricScore": 0.98,
    "validated": true,
    "validationStatus": "APPROVED"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  },
  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

In this service, the `result` object represents: Returns CNH document validation, including biometric score, facial similarity, validation status and checked fields.

**Service:** `SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION`

**When to use:** Use to extract data from documents sent as base64 or by URL.

**What it returns:** Returns the OCR text of the emancipation document and objective data extracted when it exists, without failing due to the absence of variable fields.


 Required fields: `service`, `image1`.


 Main fields in `result`: `docType`, `genericOcr`, `extractedFields`, `analysis`.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `image1`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

### OCR guide

For ready-made payloads, image quality and error diagnostics, see [OCR via Service API](/en/guides/service-api/sobre-ocr-service-api).

### Minimum payload

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR_EMANCIPATION",
  "image1": "BASE64_DO_DOCUMENTO"
}
```

### Expected clean return

```json
{
  "result": {
    "docType": "EMANCIPATION_DOCUMENT",
    "genericOcr": "extracted text",
    "extractedFields": {
      "cpf": "cpf",
      "dates": [
        "yyyy-MM-dd"
      ]
    },
    "analysis": {
      "isEmancipationRelated": true,
      "confidence": "MEDIUM"
    }
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  },
  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

### Common error

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Não foi possível ler o documento de emancipação"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "REFUSED",
  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

**Service:** `SERVICE_FACE_INDEX`

**When to use:** Use to compare two facial images and return the similarity between them.

**What it returns:** Searches for a selfie in the indexed face database and returns whether a face was found, the associated CPF and the similarity when available.


 Required fields: `service`, `image1`.


 Main fields in `result`: `cpf`, `faceFound`, `similarity`.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `image1`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

**Service:** `SERVICE_FACE_MATCH`

**When to use:** Use to compare two facial images and return the similarity between them.

**What it returns:** Returns the facial comparison between two images, with a similarity score, match status and approval/rejection message.


 Required fields: `service`, `image1`, `image2`.


 Main fields in `result`: `match`, `similarity`, `status`.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `image1`, `image2`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

**Service:** `SERVICE_OCR`

**When to use:** Use to extract data from documents sent as base64 or by URL.

**What it returns:** Returns data extracted from identification documents sent as an image, such as RG/CIN, CNH, OAB, RNE/CRNM, passport or automatic identification.


 Required fields: `service`, `documentType`, `image1`.


 Main fields in `result`: `cpf`, `docType`, `name`, `birthDate`, `cnhCategory`, `cnhNumber`.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 `image2`


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `documentType`, `image1`

**Optional fields:** `image2`

```json
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR",
  "documentType": "CNH",
  "image1": "BASE64_DA_CNH"
}
```

### Expected clean return

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "docType": "CNH",
    "name": "Extracted name",

    "cnhNumber": "00000000000"
  },

    "code": 200,

  },
  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

```json
    "code": 400,

}
```

**Service:** `SERVICE_CPF_ADDRESS_VALIDATION`

**When to use:** Use to look up or validate addresses associated with the document.

**What it returns:** Returns whether the informed address is associated with the CPF, including match level, normalized address and signals used in the validation.


 Required fields: `service`, `cpf`, `zipcode`, `numberAddress`.


 Main fields in `result`: `cpf`, `zipcode`, `match`, `confidence`, `normalizedAddress`.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `cpf`, `zipcode`, `numberAddress`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

**Service:** `SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS`

**When to use:** Use to extract data from documents sent as base64 or by URL.

**What it returns:** Returns data extracted from the proof of address by OCR, such as OCR text, name, address, document type, dates and amounts when found.


 Required fields: `service`, `image1`.


 Main fields in `result`: `genericOcr`, `fullName`, `fullAddress`, `docType`, `dueDate`, `invoiceAmount`.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `image1`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

### OCR guide

For ready-made payloads, image quality and error diagnostics, see [OCR via Service API](/en/guides/service-api/sobre-ocr-service-api).

### Minimum payload

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR_PROOF_OF_ADDRESS",
  "image1": "BASE64_DO_COMPROVANTE"
}
```

### Expected clean return

```json
{
  "result": {
    "genericOcr": "extracted text",
    "fullName": "Extracted name",
    "fullAddress": "Extracted address",
    "docType": "Utility bill",
    "dueDate": "yyyy-MM-dd",
    "invoiceAmount": "R$ 100.00"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  },
  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

### Common error

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Não foi possível ler o comprovante de endereço"
  },

  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

## Checklist before opening a ticket


 Confirm the token belongs to the right product and that the service is enabled for the API.


 Confirm the exact `service` value and the required fields listed in the accordion.


 Validate whether the call was made in HML or production with the token from the same environment.


 Keep the body without sensitive data, timestamp, environment, `status.message` and `externalId`.


## Error patterns

The examples below show common formats. The message may vary depending on validation, product and environment.

```json
{
  "status": {
    "code": 401,
    "message": "Unauthorized"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Required field is missing or invalid"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "status": {
    "code": 403,
    "message": "Service unavailable or not enabled for this client"
  }
}
```

# Business (PJ) services

URL: https://api-docs.idcerberus.com/en/api-reference/services-pessoa-juridica
Source: en/api-reference/services-pessoa-juridica.mdx
Description: Explicit catalog of business (PJ) services available via API, with expected fields and request examples.

> Info:
Explicit catalog of business (PJ) services available via API, with expected fields and request examples. All services use `POST /api/service-api`; the product executed is defined by the `service` field in the body.

> Atencao:
Use exactly the value shown in `Service`. Do not send an internal alias or integration name.

## Before testing


 See the token, headers, standard body, `result`, `status` and `externalId`.


 Set up HML, generate a token and run `POST /api/service-api` with a real payload.


 Payload, expected image, clean return and error diagnostics for the CNPJ card.


 Full examples for CNPJ, risk, registration and OCR.


## How to use this page


 Use the cards below to find the right group of services.


 In the full catalog, open the service accordion and copy the example body.


 Use `result` as the public contract and preserve `status`, `onboardingStatus` and `externalId`.


## How to interpret any response


 Read the `result` object first. It concentrates the business fields the client should consume.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the call processed, was refused or failed.


 Keep `externalId` for tests, support and audits. It is the most practical identifier for the query.


 Do not rely on internal metadata. The integration should only map the documented public fields.


## Service families


 1 service: `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD`.


 6 services: `SERVICE_DOMAINS_CNPJ`, `SERVICE_COMPANY_RELATIONSHIP`, `SERVICE_ECONOMIC_GROUP_RELATIONSHIPS` and 3 more.


 6 services: `SERVICE_OWNERS_ELECTORAL_DONORS_CNPJ`, `SERVICE_COMPANY_KYC_OWNERS`, `SERVICE_ECONOMIC_GROUP_KYC_COMPANY` and 3 more.


 3 services: `SERVICE_COMPLIANCE_BET_PJ`, `SERVICE_COMPLIANCE_BET`, `SERVICE_MEDIA_PROFILE_EXPOSURE_PJ`.


 6 services: `SERVICE_OWNERS_LAWSUITS_DISTRIBUTION`, `SERVICE_JURIDICAL_PROCESSES_PJ_OWNERS`, `SERVICE_LABOR_LAWSUITS` and 3 more.


 22 services: `SERVICE_HISTORY_BASIC_DATA`, `SERVICE_OWNERS_INFLUENCE`, `SERVICE_CGU_NEGATIVE_CERTIFICATE_COMPANY` and 19 more.


 7 services: `SERVICE_COMPANY_RFB_OWNERS`, `SERVICE_RFB_PJ_ON_DEMAND`, `SERVICE_REGISTRATION_DATA_CNPJ` and 4 more.


 7 services: `SERVICE_ACTIVE_DEBT_PJ`, `SERVICE_QUOD_CREDIT_SCORE_COMPANY`, `SERVICE_BOAVISTA_ONE_SCORE_COMPANY` and 4 more.


## Full catalog

Open a service to see when to use it, required fields, body, curl and a summarized response.

**Service:** `SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD`

**When to use:** Use to extract data from documents sent as base64 or by URL.

**What it returns:** Returns data extracted from the CNPJ card sent as an image, including the CNPJ, document type and OCR text when available.


 Required fields: `service`, `image1`.


 Main fields in `result`: `cnpj`, `docType`, `genericOcr`.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `image1`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

### OCR guide

For ready-made payloads, image quality and error diagnostics, see [OCR via Service API](/en/guides/service-api/sobre-ocr-service-api).

### Minimum payload

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD",
  "image1": "BASE64_DO_CARTAO_CNPJ"
}
```

### Expected clean return

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "cnpj",
    "docType": "CNPJ_CARD",
    "genericOcr": "text extracted from the CNPJ card"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  },
  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

### Common error

```json
{
  "result": {},
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "CNPJ não encontrado no cartão CNPJ"
  },
  "onboardingStatus": "REFUSED",
  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

### Step by step

1. Generate the token at `POST /api/token-generate` and send it in the `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}` header.
2. Build the body with the exact `service` and the required fields listed below.
3. Run `POST /api/service-api` in the chosen environment.
4. Check `status.code` and `status.message` to validate the technical processing.
5. Map the `result` fields per the summary and the response example for this service.

### Copy and test

Use this body in Postman under `Body > raw > JSON`. Only change the test values.

```json
{
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD",
  "image1": "base64"
}
```

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
--data '{
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD",
  "image1": "base64"
}'
```

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
--data '{
  "service": "SERVICE_OCR_CNPJ_CARD",
  "image1": "base64"
}'
```

### Body fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `service` | Yes | Exact code of the product that will be executed by the central endpoint. |
| `image1` | Yes | First image sent as base64 or an equivalent reference, depending on the product. |

### Main result fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cnpj` | CNPJ related to the query result. |
| `result.docType` | Document type identified in the processing. |
| `result.genericOcr` | Raw text extracted from the document by OCR. |

### How to consume the response


 Public data from the service. It is the main object to map into the client's system.


 Technical status of the call, with `code` and `message`.


 When returned, summarizes the operational outcome: `APPROVED`, `REFUSED` or `ERROR`.


 Identifier to trace the query in support, logs or audits.


### Summarized response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "cnpj",
    "docType": "CNPJ_CARD",
    "genericOcr": "text extracted from the CNPJ card"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  },
  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

In this service, the `result` object represents: Returns data extracted from the CNPJ card sent as an image, including the CNPJ, document type and OCR text when available.

**Service:** `SERVICE_ECONOMIC_GROUP_RELATIONSHIPS`

**When to use:** Use to look up ties, partners or relationships associated with the company.

**What it returns:** Returns the entities (people and companies) that are part of the same economic group as the queried CNPJ, with current, historical relationships and aggregated statistics.


 Required fields: `service`, `cnpj`.


 Main fields in `result`: `cnpj`, `totalEconomicGroupRelationships`, `economicGroupRelationshipsSummary`, `economicGroupRelationships`, `economicGroupCurrentRelationships`, `economicGroupHistoricalRelationships` and 1 more.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `cnpj`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

**Service:** `SERVICE_ADDRESSES_EXTENDED_CNPJ`

**When to use:** Use to look up or validate addresses associated with the document.

**What it returns:** Returns the full list of CNPJ addresses in result.addresses (street, number, complement, neighborhood, city, state, country, zip code, type, whether it is active and whether it is the primary one), plus an aggregated summary in result.addressesExtendedTotal* with totals and dates of the first/last confirmed passage.


 Required fields: `service`, `cnpj`.


 Main fields in `result`: `cnpj`, `addresses`, `addressesExtendedTotal`, `addressesExtendedTotalActive`, `addressesExtendedTotalWork`, `addressesExtendedTotalPersonal` and 5 more.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `cnpj`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

### Step by step

1. Generate the token at `POST /api/token-generate` and send it in the `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}` header.

3. Run `POST /api/service-api` in the chosen environment.
4. Check `status.code` and `status.message` to validate the technical processing.
5. Map the `result` fields per the summary and the response example for this service.

### Main result fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cnpj` | CNPJ related to the query result. |
| `result.addresses` | Address, list of addresses or address validation returned by the query. |
| `result.addressesExtendedTotal` | Total number of addresses found for the company. |
| `result.addressesExtendedTotalActive` | Number of addresses currently marked as active. |
| `result.addressesExtendedTotalWork` | Number of addresses of the commercial type. |
| `result.addressesExtendedTotalPersonal` | Number of addresses of the residential type. |
| `result.addressesExtendedTotalUnique` | Number of unique addresses, without duplicates. |
| `result.addressesExtendedTotalPassages` | Total number of passages (confirmations) recorded across the addresses found. |
| `result.addressesExtendedTotalBadPassages` | Number of passages flagged as inconsistent across the addresses found. |
| `result.addressesExtendedOldestPassageDate` | Date of the oldest passage recorded across the addresses found. |
| `result.addressesExtendedNewestPassageDate` | Date of the most recent passage recorded across the addresses found. |

**Service:** `SERVICE_RF_QSA`

**When to use:** Use this service when you need to run the "Federal Revenue - QSA" query via the API.

**What it returns:** Returns the corporate/administrative structure (QSA) of the informed CNPJ, with registration data of the headquarters (size, capital, CNAE, legal nature, registration status) and the list of partners and officers.


 Required fields: `service`, `cnpj`.


 Main fields in `result`: `cnpj`, `qsaCompanyType`, `qsaCompanySize`, `qsaCapital`, `qsaCapitalValue`, `qsaCnae` and 10 more.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `cnpj`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

### Step by step

1. Generate the token at `POST /api/token-generate` and send it in the `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}` header.
2. Build the body with the exact `service` and the required fields listed below.
3. Run `POST /api/service-api` in the chosen environment.
4. Check `status.code` and `status.message` to validate the technical processing.
5. Map the `result` fields per the summary and the response example for this service.

### Body fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `service` | Yes | Exact code of the product that will be executed by the central endpoint. |
| `cnpj` | Yes | The queried company's CNPJ. |

### Main result fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cnpj` | CNPJ related to the query result. |
| `result.qsaCompanyType` | Indicates whether the queried CNPJ is a HEADQUARTERS (MATRIZ) or BRANCH (FILIAL). |
| `result.qsaCompanySize` | Company size per Federal Revenue classification. |
| `result.qsaCapital` | Company's share capital amount. |
| `result.qsaCapitalValue` | Numeric value of the company's share capital, extracted from the Share Capital field for use in rules and comparisons. |
| `result.qsaCnae` | Main economic activity code. |
| `result.qsaMainEconomicActivity` | Description of the main economic activity. |
| `result.qsaSecondaryActivity` | Description of the secondary economic activities. |
| `result.qsaLegalNatureCode` | Code of the company's legal nature. |
| `result.qsaLegalNature` | Description of the company's legal nature. |
| `result.qsaIrsStatus` | Company's registration status at the Federal Revenue. |
| `result.qsaIsActive` | Indicates whether the CNPJ's registration status is ACTIVE (ATIVA), derived from the Registration Status field. |

### How to consume the response


 Public data from the service. It is the main object to map into the client's system.


 Technical status of the call, with `code` and `message`.


 When returned, summarizes the operational outcome: `APPROVED`, `REFUSED` or `ERROR`.


 Identifier to trace the query in support, logs or audits.

```bash
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
--data '{
  "service": "SERVICE_QUANTUM_CUSTOM_SCORE_COMPANY",
  "cnpj": "cnpj"
}'
```

### Body fields

| Field | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `service` | Yes | Exact code of the product that will be executed by the central endpoint. |
| `cnpj` | Yes | The queried company's CNPJ. |

### Main result fields

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `result.cnpj` | CNPJ related to the query result. |
| `result.score` | Credit score returned by the bureau for the queried CNPJ. |
| `result.creditBureauSummary` | Text summary of the main credit bureau data returned. |
| `result.creditBureauDetails` | Structured credit bureau data for consumption via the API. |
| `result.origin` | Functional source of the executed query. |
| `result.queryDate` | Date returned by the data source for the query. |

### How to consume the response


 Public data from the service. It is the main object to map into the client's system.


 Technical status of the call, with `code` and `message`.


 When returned, summarizes the operational outcome: `APPROVED`, `REFUSED` or `ERROR`.


 Identifier to trace the query in support, logs or audits.


### Summarized response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cnpj": "cnpj",
    "score": 690,
    "creditBureauSummary": "Score de crédito dentro da média do setor",
    "creditBureauDetails": {},
    "origin": "Quantum",
    "queryDate": "2026-08-01"
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  },
  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

In this service, the `result` object represents: Returns the business (PJ) Quantum credit score by the informed CNPJ, with a text summary and structured credit bureau data.

**Service:** `SERVICE_BOAVISTA_CREDIT_SCORE_COMPANY`

**When to use:** Use to assess risk, score or propensity associated with the company.

**What it returns:** Returns business (PJ) restrictive credit data by the informed CNPJ, including score, indicator and count of restrictions found.


 Required fields: `service`, `cnpj`.


 Main fields in `result`: `cnpj`, `score`, `hasRestrictions`, `restrictionCount`, `creditBureauSummary`, `creditBureauDetails` and 2 more.


 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `cnpj`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

### Step by step

1. Generate the token at `POST /api/token-generate` and send it in the `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}` header.
2. Build the body with the exact `service` and the required fields listed below.
3. Run `POST /api/service-api` in the chosen environment.
4. Check `status.code` and `status.message` to validate the technical processing.
5. Map the `result` fields per the summary and the response example for this service.

 Use `status.code` and `status.message` to understand whether the query processed correctly.


 No optional field mapped in this example.


**Endpoint:** `POST /api/service-api`

**Required fields:** `service`, `cnpj`

**Optional fields:** No optional field mapped in this example.

| `result.stateDebtState` | State (UF) the state debt certificate refers to. |
| `result.stateDebtRegistration` | Company's state registration status (CAD/ICMS). |
| `result.stateDebtValidUntil` | Validity date of the state debt certificate. |
| `result.stateDebtCertificateUrl` | Link to the state debt certificate file. |

 Public data from the service. It is the main object to map into the client's system.


 Technical status of the call, with `code` and `message`.


 When returned, summarizes the operational outcome: `APPROVED`, `REFUSED` or `ERROR`.


 Identifier to trace the query in support, logs or audits.

```json
    "stateDebtBaseStatus": "NEGATIVA",

    "stateDebtRegistration": "000.000.000.000",
```

In this service, the `result` object represents: Returns the negative state debt certificate by the informed CNPJ, available for every state.

## Checklist before opening a ticket


 Confirm the token belongs to the right product and that the service is enabled for the API.


 Confirm the exact `service` value and the required fields listed in the accordion.


 Validate whether the call was made in HML or production with the token from the same environment.


 Keep the body without sensitive data, timestamp, environment, `status.message` and `externalId`.


## Error patterns

The examples below show common formats. The message may vary depending on validation, product and environment.

```json
{
  "status": {
    "code": 401,
    "message": "Unauthorized"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "status": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "Required field is missing or invalid"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "status": {
    "code": 403,
    "message": "Service unavailable or not enabled for this client"
  }
}
```

## Operational API Reference for LLM

# idCerberus API Reference - operational summary for LLM

Use this file to generate request examples, explain API calls and choose the correct `service` without relying on the full OpenAPI.

## Mandatory rules

1. Do not invent endpoints, parameters or services.
2. For external queries, use `POST /api/service-api` and select the product through the `service` field.
3. Before answering with a payload, confirm the alias is the calling alias configured on the product.
4. Use staging for tests: `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com`.
5. Use production only when the user explicitly asks for it: `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com`.
6. Never expose `client`, `secret`, a real JWT, a real CPF, a real CNPJ or real images in examples.
7. When a service is missing from the catalog, say it needs to be confirmed before documenting or integrating it.

## Authentication

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data '{
 "client": "{client}",
 "secret": "{secret}"
}'
```

## Pessoa Física

### Account holder's professional history

1. Service: `SERVICE_PROFESSIONAL_HISTORY_OWNER_ONLY`
2. Endpoint: `POST /api/service-api`
3. Request fields: `cpf`, `birthDate`
4. Search terms: PF - Account holder's professional history
5. Main return: Returns professional history where the person appears as a holder, partner or owner, with companies, roles and tie dates.

Summarized response:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "cpf": "cpf",
    "ownerHistory": [
      {
        "companyName": "Empresa Exemplo",
        "cnpj": "cnpj",
        "qualification": "SOCIO"
      }
    ]
  },
  "status": {
    "code": 200,
    "message": "Success"
  },
  "externalId": "{externalId}"
}
```

Staging curl:

```bash
curl --location 'https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/service-api' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}' \
--data '{
  "service": "SERVICE_PROFESSIONAL_HISTORY_OWNER_ONLY",
  "cpf": "cpf",
  "birthDate": "yyyy-MM-dd (optional)"
}'
```

## Raw OpenAPI

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.0

info:
  title: idCerberus API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: |
    Technical reference for the idCerberus API, for integrating digital
    onboarding, KYC, biometrics, fraud prevention, risk analysis, compliance,
    registration enrichment, and individual and business query products.

    Use this reference when you already know which endpoint or service you
    want to implement. To understand flows, environments, best practices, and
    how to choose between services, see the guides first.

    Most data queries run through `POST /api/service-api`. On this endpoint,
    the route stays the same and the product run is defined by the `service`
    field sent in the body.

    In practice, the central endpoint works as a product runner: the method,
    URL, and headers are the same; what changes is the `service` value and
    the chosen product's required fields.

    The value sent in `service` needs to exist in the product enabled for the
    client. In some products, the calling alias configured for the product is
    shorter than another alias shown in the catalog. In those cases, send the
    calling alias in the body.

    1. Individual services usually use `cpf`.
    2. Business services usually use `cnpj`.
    3. Biometric and document services use base64 images or URLs.
    4. Some services require complementary fields, like `birthDate`, `uf`,
       `rg`, `phone`, `email`, `image1`, or `image2`.

    If you're unsure which `service` to use, see the guides "Choose the right
    service", "Service matrix", and "Service index".

    Useful search terms: CPF Federal Revenue, RFB PF, CNPJ Federal Revenue,
    RFB PJ, KYC PF, KYC PJ, OCR, FaceMatch, Liveness, fraud score, financial
    risk, electoral data, active debts, and protests.

servers:
  - url: https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com
    description: Staging environment
  - url: https://backoffice.idcerberus.com
    description: Production environment

tags:
  - name: Authorization
    description: |
      Generate the JWT token used in protected calls. Before consuming
      onboarding, external services, or customers, generate a token with
      `client` and `secret` and send it in the `Authorization` header.
  - name: SDK Integration
    description: |
      Endpoints used in the onboarding-via-SDK flow. Use this section to
      generate the `tokenOnboarding`, query the processed result, and
      download the final PDF report.
  - name: Services - Individuals
    description: |
      Individual services run through `POST /api/service-api`. Includes CPF
      enrichment, Federal Revenue, OCR, biometrics, FaceMatch, Liveness,
      risk, compliance, certificates, contacts, electoral data, and other
      products defined by the `service` field.
  - name: Services - Businesses
    description: |
      Business services run through `POST /api/service-api`. Includes CNPJ
      enrichment, Federal Revenue, SINTEGRA, business owners, relationships,
      debts, protests, business owners' KYC, and compliance.
  - name: Customers
    description: |
      Operations to query registered customers and change the active or
      inactive status of one or more records.

paths:
  /api/token-generate:
    post:
      tags:
        - Authorization
      summary: Generate API token
      x-mint:
        href: /en/api-reference/autorização/gerar-token-de-api
        metadata:
          title: Generate API token
          sidebarTitle: Generate API token
      description: |
        Generates the JWT token used in protected calls to the idCerberus API.

        Send the `client` and `secret` provided by idCerberus. The response
        contains `access_token` and `expires_in`. Use the returned token in
        the header:

        `Authorization: Bearer {jwt_token}`

        When the token expires, generate a new one using the same credentials.

        Available environments:

        | Environment | URL |
        | --- | --- |
        | Staging | `https://backoffice-hml.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate` |
        | Production | `https://backoffice.idcerberus.com/api/token-generate` |
      requestBody:
        description: |
          Send the application's credentials to generate a JWT token.
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/TokenRequest'
            example:
              client: "{client}"
              secret: "{secret}"
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Token generated successfully.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/TokenResponse'
              example:
                access_token: "{jwt_token}"
                expires_in: "300"
        '400':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/BadRequest'
        '401':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthorized'

  /api/token-history-onboarding:
    post:
      tags:
        - SDK Integration
      summary: Generate TokenOnboarding for SDK
      x-mint:
        href: /en/api-reference/integração-via-sdk/gerar-tokenonboarding-para-sdk
        metadata:
          title: Generate TokenOnboarding for SDK
          sidebarTitle: Generate TokenOnboarding for SDK
      description: |
        Creates a new `tokenOnboarding` to start a registration flow via SDK.

        The generated token should be handed to the SDK and will later be
        used to query the result processed by the backoffice and download
        the PDF report.

        Use `documentFiles` when you want to send documents or file URLs
        already at the start of the process.
      security:
        - bearerAuth: []
      requestBody:
        description: |
          Provide the user's initial data and, when applicable, files or

        required: true
        content:

            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/TokenOnboardingRequest'

          $ref: '#/components/responses/BadRequest'
        '401':

      description: |
        Central endpoint for running data, risk, biometrics, document, and

        The route is always `POST /api/service-api`. The product run is

        The `service` value is validated against the services enabled for the
        client's product. If the product is configured with a short alias,
        use that alias in the body, even if the catalog shows another
        documented alias.

        Common calling-alias examples:

        | Service |
        | --- |

        | `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY_CONSULT` | `SERVICE_DIGITAL_DOCUMENTOSCOPY` |
        | `SERVICE_ECONOMIC_RELATIONSHIP` | `economic_relationships` |
        | `SERVICE_EMAIL_VALIDATION` | `SERVICE_EMAIL_VALIDATION1` |
        | `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE`, `SERVICE_PROTEST_PF` | `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE` |
        | `SERVICE_PROTEST_PJ` | `SERVICE_PROTEST_CLEARANCE_CERTIFICATE_PJ` |

        This endpoint serves both individual and business services. In the
        examples, use the items prefixed `PF -` for CPF queries and the items
        prefixed `PJ -` for CNPJ queries.

        Most common fields:

        | Field | Use |
        | --- | --- |
        | `service` | Code of the product that will run |
        | `cpf` | Main document in individual services |
        | `cnpj` | Main document in business services |
        | `image1`, `image2` | Base64 images for OCR, biometrics, or documents |
        | `image1Url`, `image2Url` | Image URLs, when the service accepts a URL |
        | `selfie1` | Selfie used in documentoscopy and FaceMatch |
        | `key` | Query key used in asynchronous flows |

        Examples:

        1. CPF queries usually use `cpf`;
        2. CNPJ queries usually use `cnpj`;
        3. OCR, FaceMatch, and documentoscopy use base64 images or a URL;
        4. asynchronous services use `key` to query the result afterward.
        5. short payloads help validate access to the product, but document,
           OCR, and biometric services need real data to return complete
           results.

        Most responses return:

        1. `result`: the query's business data;
        2. `status.code`: technical processing code;
        3. `status.message`: technical processing message;
        4. `externalId`: external identifier, when available.

        product's payload.

  /api/customer:
    get:
      tags:
        - Customers
      summary: Query customer
      x-mint:
        href: /en/api-reference/customers/consultar-cliente
        metadata:
          title: Query customer
          sidebarTitle: Query customer
      description: |
        Queries registered customers by CPF or CNPJ provided in
        `documentKey`.

        Use this endpoint to check whether a customer already exists,
        retrieve its `tokenCustomer`, and query its current activation
        status.
      security:
        - bearerAuth: []
      parameters:
        - name: documentKey
          in: query
          required: true
          description: Customer's CPF or CNPJ.
          schema:
            type: string
          example: cpf or cnpj
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Customer found.
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/Customer'
              example:
                - tokenCustomer: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
                  type: PF
                  documentKey: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
                  name: CUSTOMER NAME
                  addInformation: Cliente cadastrado via integração
                  active: false
                  imageUrl: https://exemplo.com/imagem-cliente.jpg
        '400':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/BadRequest'
        '401':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthorized'
        '403':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Forbidden'

  /api/changeStatusOfCustomer:
    post:
      tags:
        - Customers
      summary: Change customer status
      x-mint:
        href: /en/api-reference/customers/alterar-status-de-cliente
        metadata:
          title: Change customer status
          sidebarTitle: Change customer status
      description: |
        Changes the active or inactive status of one or more customers.

        Send a list of objects with `documentKey` and `active`. Use `active:
        true` to activate and `active: false` to deactivate the customer.
      security:
        - bearerAuth: []
      requestBody:
        description: List of customers whose status should be changed.
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ChangeCustomerStatusRequest'
            example:
              - documentKey: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
                active: false
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Status changed successfully.

            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenericStatusResponse'
              example:
                status:
                  code: 200

    ServiceApiRequest:
      type: object
      description: |
        Base payload for the `/api/service-api` endpoint. The `service` field
        defines which product will run; the other fields are dynamic and
        depend on the service chosen.

        Main families:

        - PF registration and identity
        - Documents and biometrics
        - PF risk, validations, and compliance
        - Political and electoral
        - PJ registration and compliance status
        - PJ business owners, relationships, and compliance
      required:
        - service
      additionalProperties: true
      properties:
        service:
          type: string
          description: Code of the service that will run.
          example: SERVICE_PERSON_DATA_ENRICHMENT
        cpf:
          type: string
          description: CPF used in individual (PF) queries.
          example: cpf
        cnpj:
          type: string
          description: CNPJ used in business (PJ) queries.
          example: cnpj
        email:
          type: string
          description: Email used in email address validation.
          example: email@email.com
        phone:
          type: string
          description: Phone used in contact queries and validations.
          example: "11900000000"
        zipcode:
          type: string
          description: ZIP code used in address validations.
          example: 00000-000
        numberAddress:
          type: string
          description: Address number used in residence validations.
          example: "13"
        uf:
          type: string
          description: State (UF) when the service requires a state-level scope.
          example: SP
        image1:
          type: string
          description: Base64 image or main content for OCR, biometrics, and FaceMatch services.
          example: base64
        image2:
          type: string
          description: Second base64 image, when the service requires a comparison or the back of a document.
          example: base64
        image1Url:
          type: string
          description: URL of the first image, when the integration uses a hosted file.
          example: url_image
        image2Url:
          type: string
          description: URL of the second image, when the integration uses a hosted file.
          example: urlImageMatch
        selfie1:
          type: string
          description: Base64 selfie used in documentoscopy or face comparison.
          example: base64
        key:
          type: string
          description: Query key used in asynchronous services, such as digital documentoscopy.
          example: de0cd562-5962-40bd-8f94-5a7184ecde0e
        nit:
          type: string
          description: Worker identification number, when applicable.
```
